project.summary: Move Forge from browser-local work tracking to a reliable collaborative production product, with explicit feature and release gates.
project.description:
## Outcome

Move Forge from browser-local work tracking to a reliable collaborative production product, following the 28 October 2026 source-backed review at `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`.

## Current backlog

133 items across 10 milestones: 82 user stories, 28 technical enablers, 8 product decisions and 15 release gates. Labels distinguish 57 Core production, 70 Feature gated and 6 Later expansion items. All preference work is owned within this project.

The pre-implementation audit read all issue specifications and native relations, added five missing coverage items, split four bundled stories and refined 73 existing issues. The verified graph has 251 native prerequisites, no cycles, no external project dependency and no optional item forced into core launch.

## Sequencing and release contract

Start with serving-environment identity, release scope and pure preference schemas. Native prerequisites govern completion; agreed-interface preparation can proceed concurrently. Related links can denote conditional work. Every enabled surface still requires its stated implementation and candidate evidence; exclusions require an explicit scope decision and enforced gates.

Milestones are outcome groups, not dates. High priority blocks the labeled scope, Medium is required before feature enablement and Low denotes later expansion. Owners, estimates, service targets and dates remain refinement decisions.

## Completion evidence

Each implementation item includes guidance, business rules, acceptance criteria and mapped Given/When/Then tests. Specifications are not passing results. Core promotion requires [FOR-123](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-123/approve-and-execute-the-controlled-core-production-launch>) and the evidence register for every selected optional module. Nothing is marked Done or certified production-ready by this review.

## Project documents

* [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>)
* [Backlog map, dependencies and release gates](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/backlog-map-dependencies-and-production-release-gates-d8a0fa0049fa>)
* [Pre-implementation backlog audit](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/pre-implementation-backlog-audit-28-october-2026-b6a59c9e01c0>)

# Forge production backlog — coverage, dependencies and release rules

Based on the [production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) and the [whole-backlog pre-implementation audit](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/pre-implementation-backlog-audit-28-october-2026-b6a59c9e01c0>), checked against source revision `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. This is the current planning map, not production certification.

## Current inventory and verification

* **136 issues:** 85 user stories, 28 technical enablers, 8 product decisions, 15 release gates.
* **10 native milestones** and labels for type, release scope and product area. **18 preference items** also carry the Preferences label.
* **258 prerequisite relationships** in the maintained graph, all internal. The original 133-issue audit read every native relationship; subsequent selected-release and plan-limit changes were read back. The current local graph was checked for cycles and duplicate titles; this is not a fresh whole-backlog remote audit.
* **57 Core production**, **73 Feature gated**, **6 Later expansion** items.
* **75 High**, **55 Medium**, **6 Low** priorities. High blocks its labeled launch scope; Medium is required before enabling the corresponding feature; Low is later expansion. Priority is not a delivery date.
* Implementation tracking: **FOR-21, FOR-128 and FOR-153 Done**; **FOR-20, FOR-25, FOR-27, FOR-28, FOR-39, FOR-75, FOR-76, FOR-97, FOR-109, FOR-110, FOR-111 and FOR-155 In Progress**. Other live statuses are authoritative in Linear. No assignees, estimates, sprints or deadlines were invented.
* The graph is acyclic. Every pre-launch core item reaches the core launch gate. The user selected web collaboration, Forge agent, macOS and paid billing, so their conditional gates are now mandatory for this selected release.
* No active issue depends on the removed preference project. The audit found no exact duplicate tickets to delete; overlapping responsibilities were separated.

The pre-implementation audit added five missing coverage items and split four existing bundles. It refined 73 existing issues and reduced native links from 296 to 251 at that stage. Selected-release gates and the later confirmed plan requirements brought the maintained graph to the current inventory above. See the audit document for its historical finding-by-finding rationale and outstanding refinement choices.

## How to use dependencies

Start with [FOR-25](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-25/identify-the-serving-production-services-and-database>) (serving-environment identity), [FOR-20](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates>) (release contract) and [FOR-128](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-128/validate-and-safely-migrate-personal-preference-schemas>) (pure schemas/defaults). These have no native prerequisites. Work in different milestones can proceed concurrently once its interfaces and policy are clear.

**Blocked by** means a prerequisite for completing the issue's acceptance contract. It does not prohibit drafting, fixture tests or agreed-interface implementation. Transitive prerequisites remain enforced without repeating every ancestor as another direct link.

**Related to** can identify coordination or conditional work. When a surface is enabled, its implementation and acceptance evidence remain mandatory even when it is not an unconditional graph blocker. Every release must have a manifest mapping selected features to issue/gate evidence and owners. Missing evidence blocks that selected surface. An exclusion requires a recorded decision plus enforced UI/direct-route/job behavior; it never marks unfinished implementation Done.

The core go/no-go is [FOR-123](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-123/approve-and-execute-the-controlled-core-production-launch>). [FOR-103](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-103/disable-unfinished-features-consistently-across-ui-and-server-routes>) prevents hidden routes, tools, previews or background execution bypassing the manifest. [FOR-124](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-124/verify-production-behavior-and-resolve-launch-regressions>) checks the actual serving release.

## Milestones

| Milestone | Items | Exit outcome |
| -- | -- | -- |
| M00 · Scope and product decisions | 8 | Release contract, visibility, migration ownership, retention and service objectives are decided. Product decisions remain blockers until recorded; no dates are implied. |
| M01 · Platform and durable foundations | 17 | Production identities verified; staging isolated; transactional command/outbox, tenant integrity, private storage, observability and restore mechanisms ready. |
| M02 · Collaborative issues and migration | 19 | Canonical issue creation/editing, issue detail, triage and My issues work for multiple users; browser data imports reconcile without loss. |
| M03 · Planning and shared content | 19 | Projects, cycles, initiatives, documents and saved views use server persistence and consistent resource visibility. |
| M04 · Inbox, jobs and Calls | 11 | Durable jobs, notifications, recurrence and Calls operate with deduplication, recovery, explicit retention and scheduler health. |
| M05 · Production Forge agent | 14 | Atomic admission, reserved spend, crash-safe approvals, runtime recovery, durable files, skills and deployed provider evaluations. |
| M06 · Public API and MCP | 8 | Scoped/versioned API and webhooks; external MCP read and write readiness with explicit authorization and compatibility gates. |
| M07 · Commercial and integration surfaces | 12 | Complete or explicitly gate billing, Signals, Reviews, Insights, connected apps and import/export. Each feature has an enablement gate. |
| M08 · Security, quality and desktop | 21 | Recovery, revocation, abuse controls, key rotation, performance, accessibility, supply-chain and packaged-desktop evidence. |
| M09 · Production launch | 4 | Cross-surface production evidence reviewed, enabled-feature gates satisfied, runbooks and rollback proven, controlled launch and post-launch checks. |

Milestones group outcomes, not promised dates. Optional milestone work is not a blanket prerequisite for core release.

## Preference implementation map

[FOR-128](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-128/validate-and-safely-migrate-personal-preference-schemas>) defines scopes, schemas/defaults and safe parsing independently. [FOR-127](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-127/keep-personal-preferences-consistent-across-authenticated-sessions>) consumes that contract for account persistence. [FOR-144](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-144/import-legacy-personal-preferences-without-overwriting-account-choices>) handles ownership-aware legacy migration separately; the remaining consumers no longer wait for legacy-import policy.

[FOR-141](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-141/verify-web-preference-behavior-before-exposing-production-controls>) verifies the controls selected in the release manifest. [FOR-142](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-142/verify-packaged-desktop-preferences-and-web-handoff>) adds packaged security and selected native behavior. Native adapters can be implemented against the existing safe host interface before the final packaged security gate, while distribution still requires the gate.

These are distinct behaviors and must not share accidental side effects.

## Implementation ownership boundaries

* [FOR-32](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-32/commit-commands-receipts-audit-and-outbox-events-atomically>) owns atomic mutation/receipt/activity/outbox commit; [FOR-64](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-64/run-leased-resumable-background-jobs-with-operator-recovery>) owns generic execution leases/checkpoints/retries; [FOR-33](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-33/deliver-external-effects-with-recoverable-outbox-processing>) owns provider/event delivery semantics.
* [FOR-34](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-34/store-all-agent-and-issue-files-durably-in-private-object-storage>) owns durable bytes; [FOR-48](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-48/attach-durable-files-to-issues-and-comments>) and [FOR-83](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-83/use-durable-attachments-and-artifacts-throughout-an-agent-run>) own domain bindings; [FOR-37](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-37/reconcile-orphaned-files-and-retry-durable-deletion>) owns shared byte deletion; [FOR-147](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-147/expire-agent-conversation-data-through-scheduled-recoverable-retention>) owns agent data eligibility and scheduling.
* [FOR-102](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-102/sync-editable-profile-extras-across-authorized-sessions>) owns public/allowed profile fields independently of private presentation preferences.
* [FOR-93](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-93/execute-mcp-writes-through-explicit-delegation-or-pending-approvals>) owns external delegated/pending approval identity; [FOR-80](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-80/execute-approved-agent-writes-with-crash-safe-command-receipts>) owns internal agent authority. Shared command invariants do not imply the same interaction model.
* [FOR-88](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-88/expose-authorized-projects-cycles-labels-and-initiatives>) and [FOR-82](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-82/let-forge-use-authorized-cycles-documents-inbox-and-call-recaps>) can ship without advanced initiatives, document tools or Calls tools. Their separate extension issues preserve that scope.
* [FOR-126](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-126/migrate-legacy-planning-content-and-shared-views-when-enabled>) still covers the full planned advanced-content migration batch. If modules launch separately, split its domain adapters during rollout refinement and preserve excluded data meanwhile.

## Decisions and definition of ready

The eight decision items remain [FOR-20](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates>), [FOR-21](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-21/decide-project-team-and-shared-resource-visibility-rules>), [FOR-22](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-22/decide-ownership-and-conflict-rules-for-legacy-browser-data>), [FOR-23](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-23/define-retention-and-accountworkspace-deletion-behavior>), [FOR-24](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-24/agree-capacity-service-and-recovery-objectives>), [FOR-75](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-75/define-provider-spending-and-execution-admission-policy>), [FOR-91](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-91/choose-external-mcp-transport-client-support-and-write-authority>), [FOR-109](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-109/agree-plans-entitlements-and-subscription-lifecycle-rules>). They cover launch scope, sharing, ownership, retention, service/recovery/capacity limits, provider spend, MCP authority and commercial behavior. They are not automatically approved by this planning task.

Before implementing a policy-dependent story, record the chosen rule, concrete fixtures and owner in that story or its linked decision. Provider lists, notification precedence, supported OS/client capabilities, SLA business hours, recurrence/DST/catch-up rules and external import formats still require explicit refinement. Do not invent numerical thresholds or a production guarantee.

**INVEST:** each item has an actor/outcome or technical guarantee, bounded ownership and acceptance specifications. Independence is improved by separating genuine prerequisites from conditional scope. Estimates and sprint fit still need team review, especially provider integrations, deletion/export and multi-domain migrations.

**Definition of done:** demonstrate every selected AC through its mapped test at a named commit/environment; include actual deployed/provider/packaged evidence where required. Existing source, test headings and historical passing tests are not substitutes for those results. No stories are marked Done by the review.

## Current seat policy and implementation amendment · 28 October 2026

The user selected subscription seat charges/credits **at the next renewal**, with no mid-cycle seat proration. Current billed-seat quantity stays separate from the current-active-member US$5 allowance pool. FOR-109 records the decision. FOR-110 now has a locally verified Polar `next_period` seat adapter (30 renewal cases; complete billing suite 70 tests in 8 files; TypeScript and changed-file lint passed). The adapter preserves current billed seats/amount and handles repeat, replacement and withdrawal requests. It is uncommitted, undeployed and disconnected from membership events/public routes. Durable membership outbox, per-workspace serialization, reconciliation, provider sandbox evidence and remaining billing policy are still required. FOR-110 stays In Progress; FOR-111 and FOR-112 are not completed by these helper tests.

## Current billing-country policy · 28 October 2026

Workspace billing address country selects EUR/USD for new checkout. The user confirmed EUR for EU/EEA countries, the UK and Switzerland; other accepted countries use USD. FOR-109 records these decisions. FOR-110 now derives checkout product/currency from that country, requires a billing address, and refuses invalid/missing countries or a separate currency override. Local billing suite: 9 files / 137 passing tests; TypeScript, changed-file lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Persisted workspace billing profile/trusted resolver, public routes, provider catalog and receipt reconciliation remain open. No live billing changes; FOR-110 stays In Progress.

## Current plan and trial implementation · 28 October 2026

[Forge launch plans — entitlements and usage policy](https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b) transcribes the user's screenshots (Basic → Starter, Business → Plus) with explicit Forge overrides. Monthly billing remains confirmed. Free allows 5 active members with a fixed US$5 monthly workspace pool and no paid overage. Paid Starter/Plus retain US$5 per active member. Calls/Signals debit Free and trial pools, but not paid pools. BYOK is excluded. Downgrades above the Free member limit preserve existing access and block new joins until the count falls below five.

Starter/Plus trials are 14 days, card-free and managed in Forge, with one fixed US$5 workspace pool for the entire trial. Expiry never charges automatically; upgrade is manual. Polar checkout always disables hosted trials. Eligibility/redemption, lifecycle transitions and actual persistence/expiry wiring remain open.

Added bounded member-capacity FOR-153 (In Progress; atomic database/auth implementation verified, serving rollout pending), team-capacity FOR-154 (Backlog) and card-free trial FOR-155 (In Progress; local period/usage contract preparation). Reused FOR-35 for upload limits, FOR-41 for active-issue creation and FOR-45 for archive/restore capacity; FOR-111 owns the single entitlement projection and integration. New numeric-limit stories depend only on FOR-39's authorization foundation, with related links for billing coordination. FOR-112 now also requires FOR-153/FOR-154/FOR-155, rather than forcing every preparatory story to wait on complete billing.

Current inventory: **136 issues / 260 prerequisites**; 85 user stories, 28 enablers, 8 decisions and 15 gates. Updated relations were read back; local graph has no cycles, missing dependency targets or exact duplicate titles. This does not repeat the original whole-backlog remote audit.

Verification: **211 app test files / 1,242 tests passed on rerun**, including **9 billing files / 164 tests**; TypeScript, billing lint, formatting and diff checks passed. The first full run had one review-screen emoji-picker failure; its isolated rerun and the second full run passed without source changes to that screen. These are local, uncommitted/undeployed results, not live provider/database/release evidence.

Trial refinement: eligibility is **once per workspace**, shared across Starter/Plus and all admins. Durable workspace-unique redemption and atomic initial grant are required; expiry, tier/owner change and retries cannot grant another trial. FOR-155 is In Progress for local contract preparation and still requires actual persistence/expiry/UI evidence.

## Atomic member-capacity implementation checkpoint · 28 October 2026

FOR-153 now has a Drizzle counter/trigger migration and auth/join integration, verified by **11 real PostgreSQL integration cases**, including concurrent joins, rejected batch/move rollback, preserved grandfathered access and invitation state, paid admin additions and verified-owner workspace creation. The acceptance endpoint keeps an outer transaction and inner savepoint. [Implementation/rollout guide](https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/atomic-workspace-member-capacity-implementation-and-rollout-a8b750fd4060).

`bun run test` passed **1,254 app tests + 4 workflow tests**; live database tests ran separately on a schema-only test branch. TypeScript, changed-file lint, diff checks and production build passed. No unrelated schema formatting was retained. Source is uncommitted; the serving/default database and local connection selection were unchanged. **FOR-153 remains In Progress** until its review/serving-environment rollout and prerequisite evidence are complete. Other production gates remain open.



## Foundation implementation checkpoint · 28 October 2026

FOR-21 is Done: the user confirmed project/private-team, administrator, document-sharing and initiative rules; the full role/resource matrix and executable fixtures are recorded. FOR-153 is Done: atomic member capacity and all enabled real-auth join paths passed 11 PostgreSQL cases on the fresh persistent staging database. Production rollout remains separately release-gated. Removed two unnecessary blanket blockers: FOR-20 → FOR-21 and FOR-39 → FOR-153; both remain related coordination links. The maintained graph has 136 issues and 258 prerequisites, with no cycle or exact duplicate title.

Team SQL visibility now filters direct lookup and pagination before limits; six PostgreSQL cases passed. The new staging database applied all 27 migrations through an exact-target, serialized runner; three real migration fault/concurrency cases passed. Full app suite: 1,269 tests plus 4 workflow tests; TypeScript and production build passed. FOR-25 still lacks verified deployed DB/commit identity; FOR-27/FOR-28/FOR-39 retain their remaining acceptance work.

Agent concurrency is unlimited per user/workspace/provider under the user’s revised decision. All built-in providers are in the funded launch scope. A first paid period starts a fresh US$5-per-active-member pool, with earlier usage/reservations preserved in their original periods. Commercial ledger, provider provisioning and paid lifecycle verification remain open.


## Billing-grace checkpoint · 28 October 2026

The user confirmed 7 days of paid-access grace after failed renewal, including included AI and existing capped/opted-in overage. FOR-111 is In Progress with durable original-failure/expiry state, signed-byte webhook verification, current provider reconciliation and atomic entitlement/receipt/audit writes. Staging and rehearsal now apply all 29 migrations. Eight billing PostgreSQL cases, twelve real-auth/member cases, six previous-schema team-visibility cases and three migration fault cases passed. Full app rerun: 1,295 tests plus 4 workflow tests; typecheck, lint, formatting and production build passed. No serving/default migration or deployment occurred. The webhook stays disabled pending remaining cancellation/refund/revocation/pause, reconciliation job, communications, ledger and Polar release evidence.


## Scheduled cancellation checkpoint · 28 October 2026

The user selected keeping paid access until billing-period end. The owner/admin server command, durable frozen cutoff, canceled/uncanceled reconciliation and read/member-insertion enforcement are implemented and staging-verified. Thirteen billing-state and thirteen real-auth member cases pass, plus three complete-history migration fault cases. Isolated staging/rehearsal now have 30 migrations. FOR-109/FOR-110/FOR-111 remain In Progress for remaining policy, UI/action and lifecycle/release work; no serving deployment or provider cancellation occurred.


## Full-refund checkpoint · 28 October 2026

The user selected immediate loss of paid access on full refund of the current period. Signed order verification, durable period denial, atomic receipt/audit and shared feature/auth/SQL enforcement are implemented on isolated staging. Refund history survives activation ordering and later active updates; a refunded term cannot start failed-renewal grace. Existing members retain access. Team thread summaries now use the shared policy. Isolated staging and rehearsal have all 31 migrations. Exact checks are in `output/production-readiness/subscription-refunds-2026-10-28.json` and `docs/subscription-refunds.md`. FOR-109/FOR-111 remain In Progress for outstanding policy and full billing lifecycle/release work.


## Partial-refund checkpoint · 28 October 2026

The user selected keeping paid access unchanged on partial subscription-period refunds. Current order status/net/tax validation, atomic unchanged receipt/audit, and promotion to full-period denial on cumulative full refund are implemented. No entitlement row is modified by a partial refund, and late partial delivery cannot restore refunded access. Verified: 1,331 app tests, 4 workflow tests, 24 PostgreSQL billing cases and 14 real-auth member cases; TypeScript, changed-file lint/format and production build. No migration or serving deployment. FOR-109/FOR-111 stay In Progress for exceptional lifecycle policy and remaining billing integration/release gates. See `docs/subscription-refunds.md` and `output/production-readiness/partial-refunds-2026-10-28.json`.


## Immediate termination checkpoint · 28 October 2026

The user selected immediate loss of paid access on final Polar termination, including during grace. Signed revoked/current-provider verification, durable terminal state, atomic audit/receipt and shared feature/auth/SQL enforcement are implemented. Existing members retain access; old/equal terminal proofs, preactivation ordering, cached active-event promotion, later active updates and audit rollback are covered. Staging and rehearsal contain all 32 migrations. Verified: 1,343 app tests, 4 workflow tests, 31 PostgreSQL billing cases, 15 real-auth membership cases and 3 complete-history migration fault cases. FOR-109/FOR-111 remain In Progress for plan-transition/pause policy and remaining integration/release gates. See `docs/subscription-termination.md` and `output/production-readiness/subscription-termination-2026-10-28.json`.


## Paid tier-change and upgrade-refund checkpoint · 28 October 2026

Confirmed and implemented: upgrades after immediate prorated payment, downgrades at renewal, Starter retention on failed upgrade payment and verified paid Starter fallback after full upgrade-only refund. Prepared owner/admin commands preserve billed seats, currency, period and renewal-seat changes; signed payment/refund reconciliation cannot grant Plus from an unpaid or fully refunded invoice. Staging/rehearsal have all 33 migrations. Verified: 1,392 app tests, 4 workflow tests, 43 PostgreSQL billing cases, 16 real-auth membership cases and 3 migration fault cases. FOR-109/FOR-110/FOR-111 remain In Progress for the documented remaining policies, public actions, durable effects, ledger and actual provider/release gates. See `docs/subscription-plan-changes.md` and `output/production-readiness/plan-changes-2026-10-28.json`.


## Upgrade-refund renewal checkpoint · 29 October 2026

Confirmed and implemented: a full upgrade-only refund renews on Starter. The signed refund handler persists access restriction first, redrives provider scheduling without another charge, preserves billed/scheduled seats, and records confirmation with an atomic audit/receipt. Old refunds cannot confirm over a newer paid grant. No new migration; staging remains at 33. Verification: 1,412 app tests, 4 workflow tests, 46 PostgreSQL billing cases and 16 real-auth membership cases. Previous migration-fault evidence is unchanged (3 cases). Initial unrelated emoji-picker timeout passed on isolated and final full reruns. FOR-109/FOR-110/FOR-111 stay In Progress for public/durable/provider-release gates and remaining commercial decisions. See `docs/subscription-plan-changes.md` and `output/production-readiness/refund-renewal-2026-10-29.json`.


## No-pause launch policy checkpoint · 29 October 2026

Confirmed and implemented: no subscription pause/resume at launch; period-end cancellation remains the supported path. Unexpected current provider pause fields now persist a cutoff and audit/receipt; ordinary resume/active events cannot silently reopen access. Shared feature/overage/auth policy and SQL member admission agree while retaining existing sessions. Verification: 1,428 app + 4 workflow tests, 52 isolated PostgreSQL billing cases, 17 real-auth member cases and 3 full-history migration fault cases. Staging and the new empty rehearsal database have all 34 migrations. FOR-109/FOR-110/FOR-111 remain In Progress for remaining commercial/public/durable/provider-release work. See `docs/subscription-pause-policy.md` and `output/production-readiness/no-pause-2026-10-29.json`.


## Overage currency checkpoint · 29 October 2026

Confirmed: overage/caps follow the EUR/USD subscription currency; included pools stay USD. Rates are fixed at usage time from the latest published ECB daily reference, with no added spread and no invoice-time repricing. Prepared currency-aware cap arithmetic, exact conversion and bounded server source adapter are implemented. Current checks: 1,451 app + 4 workflow tests, typecheck/lint/format/diff/build and a read-only live ECB source check. No migration/provider billing or deployment. FOR-109/FOR-76 remain In Progress for atomic dual-currency ledger/quote retention, invoice allocation and actual provider/candidate gates. Prior database evidence remains at `1ba1ff8`. See `docs/overage-currency.md` and `output/production-readiness/overage-currency-2026-10-29.json`.


## Renewal-currency request checkpoint · 29 October 2026

Confirmed: EUR/USD currency changes at renewal and seven-day replacement-checkout grace. A provider-verified first-party owner/admin request is now durable with frozen boundary/deadline, renewal-tier/member snapshot, supersession/withdrawal and atomic audit/receipt. The pinned provider cannot change paid subscription currency in place; responses explicitly require checkout and do not claim provider scheduling or active grace. Checks: 1,465 app + 4 workflow tests, 58 billing + 17 real-auth member cases, 3 full-history migration fault cases, typecheck/lint/format/diff/build. Isolated staging/rehearsal have 35 migrations. FOR-109/FOR-110/FOR-111 remain In Progress for late-checkout anniversary policy and replacement/grace/public/ledger/provider execution gates. See `docs/renewal-currency-change.md` and `output/production-readiness/renewal-currency-2026-10-29.json`.


## Original-anniversary, currency-cap and before-tax checkpoint · 29 October 2026

Confirmed: late currency-replacement checkout retains the original monthly anniversary; automatically convert an existing opted-in cap at a frozen latest published ECB rate; retain existing teams/issues on downgrade while blocking creation/import/unarchiving above capacity; listed subscription prices exclude tax. Migration 0035 stores the original source/day/next boundary and supports safe audited legacy capture. Calendar/payment verification is read-only, retains short-month repair and grants no access/pool. Cap conversion preserves used/reserved capacity as shadows while historical charges retain original units. Checkout now verifies an explicit exclusive-tax monthly seat catalog and rechecks server context before any prepared checkout request.

Checks: **1,553 app + 4 workflow tests; 62 billing + 17 real-auth member cases; 3 full-history migration ownership/fault cases; 36 isolated migrations; typecheck/lint/format/diff/build**. Actual Polar access is not configured; no provider effect, public billing, paid replacement/grace entitlement or commercial ledger execution is claimed. FOR-109/FOR-110/FOR-111/FOR-76 remain In Progress. FOR-154's confirmed downgrade acceptance specification is updated; implementation is next. The transient empty default-branch rehearsal database mistake was verified and cleaned up; serving data and connection settings remain unchanged. See `docs/renewal-currency-change.md` and `output/production-readiness/replacement-anniversary-2026-10-29.json`.

issues.title: Agree the production release scope and feature gates
issues.description:
**Type:** Product decision · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-SCOPE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a product owner, I want an explicit release contract, so that unfinished surfaces cannot accidentally ship.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Publish enabled/disabled/preview matrix, intended audience, core versus conditional launch gates and accountable owner roles; no invented delivery dates.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §01, §14; all 31 areas. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Proposed: a feature may be excluded only with an explicit server-side gate and honest UI.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the release contract is approved, each area has a launch disposition, acceptance gate and owner role.
* **AC-02** — When a deferred feature is specified, the release contract records its UI/server gate and a direct-access denial test.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given the 31-area review inventory.
* When the release contract is approved.
* Then each area has a launch disposition, acceptance gate and owner role.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an optional feature is deferred.
* When a deferred feature is specified.
* Then the release contract records its UI/server gate and a direct-access denial test.

## Dependencies and completion

No upstream issue is required; this is a starting-point item.
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

## Release-scope decision · 28 October 2026

User confirmed the first production release includes **web collaboration, the Forge agent and the macOS app**. Their core, agent and packaged-desktop release gates are mandatory. Other optional surfaces still need an explicit disposition; this decision alone does not approve billing, external MCP, Calls or preview integrations. Implementation has started with <issue id="5478636d-5625-426b-9466-3e9d16dca57b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-128/define-preference-schemas-scope-rules-and-safe-runtime-defaults">FOR-128</issue> while the remaining scope manifest is refined.

### Confirmed audience

User confirmed **anyone can sign up** for the first production release. Public onboarding, email ownership/recovery and distributed abuse controls therefore require release evidence; this is not an invitation-only rollout.

### Confirmed email ownership policy

Public signup requires email verification **before workspace creation or Forge agent use**. Existing unverified sessions must not bypass server checks. Signup/verification/resend UX must remain usable on web and in the desktop authorization flow.

### Confirmed commercial launch scope · 28 October 2026

User requires **both free and paid subscriptions at launch**, using **Polar** as provider. Billing release gate <issue id="b44ca57a-268a-42d2-9cb3-361e17efbc9b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-112/verify-paid-subscription-lifecycle-before-enabling-billing">FOR-112</issue> is mandatory for the selected launch scope. Plan prices, charging unit, entitlements and lifecycle policy still require explicit decisions.

### Agent launch scope amendment — 28 October 2026

The user selected Forge-funded usage for all currently supported providers. No Forge concurrency cap applies per user, workspace or provider; the earlier proposed 3/20/10 limits were explicitly superseded. Provider-specific execution verification, authoritative allowance/overage reservations and independently held BYOK payer classification remain required before enablement.

issues.title: Decide project, team and shared-resource visibility rules
issues.description:
**Type:** Product decision · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-VISIBILITY
**Specification status:** Visibility decisions confirmed by the user on 28 October 2026. Decision record and executable fixtures completed; enforcement delivery remains <issue id="dca691b0-e932-4812-87d9-34b4ede21c89" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-31/enforce-tenant-safe-identifiers-and-relationships-in-the-database">FOR-31</issue>/<issue id="55e64c7b-7034-4ced-bf17-6c30cd33e38b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs">FOR-39</issue>.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want clear sharing rules, so that planning objects never expose private team work.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Resolve multi-team projects, initiative rollups, document sharing, parent links and workspace-level labels. Record an allow/deny matrix for roles and transports.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §05; R1; E03-E04. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (confirmed):** Shared public/private projects retain readable project details while private issues/counts stay hidden. Private-only projects require a readable participating team. Owners/admins may read all same-workspace private teams. Initiative details are workspace-visible, with private children and derived counts filtered. Private-source documents may be explicitly shared workspace-wide only by workspace owners/admins; this grants no access to private source issues.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the visibility policy is reviewed, a nonmember of B has an explicit allowed or denied result for every object and aggregate.
* **AC-02** — When the policy is consulted, allowed combinations and forbidden leakage cases have fixture examples.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given public team A and private team B share a project proposal.
* When the visibility policy is reviewed.
* Then a nonmember of B has an explicit allowed or denied result for every object and aggregate.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a developer adds a cross-team relation.
* When the policy is consulted.
* Then allowed combinations and forbidden leakage cases have fixture examples.

## Dependencies and completion

No unresolved prerequisite remains for this policy decision. <issue id="234188a9-0945-4959-a965-61ca80db44da" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates">FOR-20</issue> is related for release-scope coordination; its remaining provider/launch choices do not block the confirmed resource visibility policy.
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

### Confirmed shared-project/private-team rule

User selected **shared project; hide private issues and counts**. A workspace member may see shared project details when public/private teams participate, but access to that project never grants access to private-team issues. Private titles/descriptions, membership clues, counts, progress and other derived aggregates must not leak through project, initiative, search, export or agent surfaces. Checking existing role semantics before finalizing the allow/deny matrix. Other sharing decisions are not silently inferred.

### Confirmed access policy — 28 October 2026

The user confirmed that workspace owners and admins can read all private teams. Regular members require private-team membership for private issues and derived counts. A project shared across public and private teams stays visible as a shared project, but its private issues, snippets, issue counts and derived progress remain filtered for regular nonmembers. Privilege never crosses workspace boundaries; API credentials also require the appropriate scope. This policy must be applied before filtering, pagination and aggregation.

### Confirmed document sharing — 28 October 2026

The user permits a document attached to a private issue to be explicitly shared with the entire workspace. The grant covers only that document; links/backlinks to unreadable private issues must be omitted or rendered without issue metadata, and private issue counts remain filtered. The document's private origin is not a workspace-wide issue grant. Confirming which roles may perform the explicit sharing action before implementing it.

### Remaining visibility decisions confirmed — 28 October 2026

* Only workspace owners/admins may explicitly share a document originating from a private-team issue with the whole workspace.
* Projects belonging only to private teams are hidden from regular members who belong to none of those teams. A readable participating team is sufficient to see project metadata; issue access remains independent.
* Initiative details are always workspace-visible. Private projects, issues and their derived counts remain filtered from initiative children and rollups.

Writing the full allow/deny matrix and fixture examples; implementation enforcement and SQL invariants remain <issue id="55e64c7b-7034-4ced-bf17-6c30cd33e38b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs">FOR-39</issue>/<issue id="dca691b0-e932-4812-87d9-34b4ede21c89" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-31/enforce-tenant-safe-identifiers-and-relationships-in-the-database">FOR-31</issue> responsibilities.

### Completion evidence

The [full policy and fixtures](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-resource-visibility-policy-and-implementation-fixtures-caf8d571259a>) record the role/resource/transport matrix, private rollup filtering, explicit document grants, workspace label boundaries and relation redaction. Local source: docs/resource-visibility-policy.md and src/application/resource-visibility.ts. Twelve policy cases passed; six real PostgreSQL cases on isolated branch br-square-sky-za2iavfk passed for actual team pagination, direct lookup, directory, cross-workspace denial, read-only admin access and missing-scope denial. Twenty-eight existing team module tests and two public API handler tests also passed. No serving deployment was changed.

This closes the product decision's AC-01/AC-02, not the full enforcement implementation. <issue id="dca691b0-e932-4812-87d9-34b4ede21c89" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-31/enforce-tenant-safe-identifiers-and-relationships-in-the-database">FOR-31</issue>/<issue id="55e64c7b-7034-4ced-bf17-6c30cd33e38b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs">FOR-39</issue> remain open. Removed the unnecessary <issue id="234188a9-0945-4959-a965-61ca80db44da" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates">FOR-20</issue> blocker because this independently resolved decision no longer depends on its remaining release choices; <issue id="234188a9-0945-4959-a965-61ca80db44da" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates">FOR-20</issue> remains related.

issues.title: Decide ownership and conflict rules for legacy browser data
issues.description:
**Type:** Product decision · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-IMPORT_POLICY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an existing user, I want ambiguous local data reviewed before import, so that another account's work is not attributed to me.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Inventory store scopes; decide destination confirmation, duplicates, historical authors, changed snapshots, backup retention and explicit cleanup.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §06; R2; E02. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Source-backed: browser possession alone does not establish ownership.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the ownership policy is reviewed, the policy requires an explicit destination/ownership choice for ambiguous records.
* **AC-02** — When the conflict rule is applied, the recorded policy preserves both versions or requests a choice without silent overwrite.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a browser contains records from two accounts.
* When the ownership policy is reviewed.
* Then the policy requires an explicit destination/ownership choice for ambiguous records.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a legacy record conflicts with a server object.
* When the conflict rule is applied.
* Then the recorded policy preserves both versions or requests a choice without silent overwrite.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-20](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Define retention and account/workspace deletion behavior
issues.description:
**Type:** Product decision · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-RETENTION_POLICY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want clear data-lifetime rules, so that deletion promises include derived data and backups.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Decide lifetimes for transcripts, summaries, actions, notes, files, agent events, exports, audit records and backups; document restore and re-import exceptions.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §10, §12; R10; E12. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

issues.title: Agree capacity, service and recovery objectives
issues.description:
**Type:** Product decision · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-OBJECTIVES
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want measurable service objectives, so that readiness can be evaluated against an agreed workload.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Accept or revise review proposals: RPO 1h, RTO 4h, 99.5% core success/7d, p95 list 500ms/write 1s, notifications 60s. Define dataset/concurrency/regions and measurement exclusions.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §13; R7, R12. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** All numerical targets are proposals until explicitly accepted.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When product and operations refine them, a versioned objective sheet defines workload, measurements, owners and accepted thresholds.
* **AC-02** — When it is submitted as release evidence, it is rejected as insufficient evidence.
* **AC-03** — Given the pilot enables uploads, imports, email or background processing, when capacity policy is agreed, then per-account/workspace limits, retry windows, backlog bounds and operator escalation thresholds have explicit owners and accepted values rather than invented defaults.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given the review's proposed targets.
* When product and operations refine them.
* Then a versioned objective sheet defines workload, measurements, owners and accepted thresholds.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a performance result lacks workload or environment.
* When it is submitted as release evidence.
* Then it is rejected as insufficient evidence.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given the pilot enables uploads, imports, email or background processing.
* When capacity policy is agreed.
* Then per-account/workspace limits, retry windows, backlog bounds and operator escalation thresholds have explicit owners and accepted values rather than invented defaults.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-20](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates>).

Required for core production.

Blocking links describe prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation, contract design and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently where interfaces are agreed. Related links are coordination or conditional enablement work, not automatic blockers.

**Completion evidence:** every AC has a corresponding AT specification above. Attach results for the named commit/environment and relevant artifact. Resolve open policy choices before coding them; no passing test, estimate, owner assignment or delivery date is implied.

issues.title: Identify the serving production services and database
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-ENV
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want an authoritative deployment map, so that changes target the database actually serving Forge.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Map Vercel app/runtime deployments to commit, regions, secret references, DB host/project/branch/database, migration version and bucket; inspect metadata only.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §02, §13; E01, E20. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Do not infer the serving DB from the connected account's empty project or print credentials.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When deployment and schema metadata are inspected, one verified serving chain and unresolved mismatches are documented without secret values.
* **AC-02** — When release identity is assessed, the missing SHA remains an explicit blocker rather than guessed.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given the linked Vercel project and two candidate Neon projects.
* When deployment and schema metadata are inspected.
* Then one verified serving chain and unresolved mismatches are documented without secret values.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a deployment lacks commit metadata.
* When release identity is assessed.
* Then the missing SHA remains an explicit blocker rather than guessed.

## Dependencies and completion

No upstream issue is required; this is a starting-point item.
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

### Serving-chain verification started

Inspecting linked web/runtime deployment metadata, deployed commit identity, redacted service configuration and database/migration identity. This is read-only infrastructure investigation; credentials will not be printed. Establishing the real serving chain before any migration/application rollout. Implementation continues through the foundation prerequisites; no user action is currently requested.

### Read-only environment investigation — 28 October 2026

Verified aliases point to web deployment dpl_DHbhSDCAubnVvndVKDUgvCCzH5Bu (forge-app, prj_S0XLtdngbexhl2ao7WviBrlMScar) and runtime dpl_12bYPfjiXsMhFB7U2DkjZ4LuDn5r (prj_NtW13t9fbFligQ3pWV4DdUxW5Mub), both READY / production / iad1. Web and runtime root return HTTP 200; anonymous /api/auth/get-session returns 200. Runtime /health is 404, so this is not an agent-execution health proof.

Vercel project environment metadata lists DATABASE_URL as sensitive and withholds its value; both the connector's decrypt request and CLI env run cannot retrieve that production value. Current readable project config confirms BETTER_AUTH_URL=[forge-app-mauve.vercel.app](<http://forge-app-mauve.vercel.app>) and EVE_AGENT_RUNTIME_URL=[forge-agent-runtime.vercel.app](<http://forge-agent-runtime.vercel.app>). Neither deployment supplies a source SHA. Runtime FORGE_APP_ORIGIN is also withheld. No production storage environment references are configured in the listed project variables. These are unresolved identity/configuration blockers, not inferred matches.

Separately, read-only SQL against the local application's configured Neon URL verifies project raspy-union-96305162 / branch br-muddy-queen-zaeeysjt / neondb / PostgreSQL 18.6, with migration journal latest id 26, hash f75aa12984dcf6bc851fb30dd4faf4d314302b9c529a075e0f1ae1594a8a81f1. The local endpoint is [ep-lingering-bread-zazpwrxp-pooler.c-2.eu-west-2.aws.neon.tech](<http://ep-lingering-bread-zazpwrxp-pooler.c-2.eu-west-2.aws.neon.tech>). This is explicitly NOT proof of the Vercel deployment's database. No serving database was changed. <issue id="43434cc9-588b-4cc9-80ad-2cd1b3cebc64" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-25/identify-the-serving-production-services-and-database">FOR-25</issue> stays In Progress until the complete serving chain is verified.

[Verified serving-environment map and explicit unresolved blockers](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-serving-environment-identity-and-unresolved-production-blockers-ba44f05921ba>). This maps the actual aliases/deployments and distinguishes withheld deployed database identity from the separately verified local Neon identity. Missing SHA and sensitive deployed DB/origin identity remain blockers. No serving chain was guessed or production database changed.

issues.title: Validate service-specific production configuration at startup
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-CONFIG
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want required configuration checked per enabled feature, so that incomplete deployments fail clearly.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Define app/runtime/jobs/release config schemas for development, staging and production; reject fake runtime in production; distinguish required and conditional variables.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §02, §13; E01, E17. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Source-backed: missing optional API/desktop/Calls variables are not universal blockers; Forge uses its own Better Auth.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the service starts, readiness fails with variable names and no values.
* **AC-02** — When their optional credentials are absent, core readiness does not fail solely for those optional settings.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given Calls is enabled without its chosen OAuth config.
* When the service starts.
* Then readiness fails with variable names and no values.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given Calls and desktop release are disabled.
* When their optional credentials are absent.
* Then core readiness does not fail solely for those optional settings.

issues.title: Provision isolated staging and disposable integration-test data
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-STAGING
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a developer, I want an isolated production-like environment, so that migrations and failures can be tested without customer impact.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Separate database branch, bucket, OAuth clients and credentials; provide sanitized fixtures and explicit environment assertions.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §13; R7. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Test setup must refuse the verified production database and bucket.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When integration fixtures are seeded, data exists only in staging and cleanup is bounded to fixture IDs.
* **AC-02** — When a migration/test is started, the environment guard stops before mutation.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given staging configuration and fixture workspaces A/B.
* When integration fixtures are seeded.
* Then data exists only in staging and cleanup is bounded to fixture IDs.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given test configuration resolves to production.
* When a migration/test is started.
* Then the environment guard stops before mutation.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-25](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-25/identify-the-serving-production-services-and-database>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

### Isolated database provisioning — 28 October 2026

Verified both prior schema-only test roots contain zero users, organizations, teams and member counters. Reused our empty branch br-autumn-union-za0opf1e as persistent staging (renamed staging; expiry removed) and created a new empty database forge_staging. Created a separate forge_migration_rehearsal database on temporary branch br-square-sky-za2iavfk. This avoids production row copies, branch deletion and the schema-only root quota. Production/default branch and application environment pointers are unchanged.

Adding a checked-in exact branch/host/database allowlist and SQL branch identity verification before migration DDL. Staging app/runtime hosting, isolated bucket, OAuth/provider sandbox configuration and fixture lifecycle still remain; this provisioning update does not claim full <issue id="90e618ed-b415-45f3-884b-b6b0c981048d" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-27/provision-isolated-staging-and-disposable-integration-test-data">FOR-27</issue> acceptance.

### Database foundation verified

[Staging database and migration guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-isolated-staging-and-serialized-migration-rehearsal-67798d046945>). The new empty staging database now has all 27 versioned migrations; migration entry points accept only exact isolated branch/host/database targets and verify SQL identity before DDL. Existing sample-data integration suites remove only their own fixtures. Hosted app/runtime, object storage and isolated provider/OAuth configuration remain before full completion.

issues.title: Rehearse serialized expand-and-contract database releases
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-MIGRATIONS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want reversible application releases across schema changes, so that deployments do not strand existing users.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Use versioned migrations, one migration owner/lock, bounded resumable backfills and old/new application compatibility; avoid production db:push.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §13; R7; E03. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Schema removal occurs only after old readers/writers have been retired.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When expand migration and new app are deployed then app rolled back, both compatible versions read valid data.
* **AC-02** — When they run concurrently, one applies each migration while the other waits or exits safely.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a sanitized prior schema and previous app version.
* When expand migration and new app are deployed then app rolled back.
* Then both compatible versions read valid data.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given two deployment jobs request migration ownership.
* When they run concurrently.
* Then one applies each migration while the other waits or exits safely.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-27](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-27/provision-isolated-staging-and-disposable-integration-test-data>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

### Implementation started — serialized migration owner

Replacing unguarded migration execution with an explicit direct-connection runner that verifies expected Neon branch, host and database before DDL, acquires one PostgreSQL advisory lock before reading the journal, verifies the applied migration hash prefix and commits pending schema statements and journal entries atomically. Production execution remains disabled until <issue id="43434cc9-588b-4cc9-80ad-2cd1b3cebc64" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-25/identify-the-serving-production-services-and-database">FOR-25</issue>'s serving identity is verified. Rehearsing concurrency and rollback on a dedicated empty database in an existing isolated test branch; no production rows are copied or changed. Staging/provider/resource isolation remains <issue id="90e618ed-b415-45f3-884b-b6b0c981048d" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-27/provision-isolated-staging-and-disposable-integration-test-data">FOR-27</issue>.

### Migration implementation and database rehearsal verified

[Implementation and reproducible operator guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-isolated-staging-and-serialized-migration-rehearsal-67798d046945>). Guarded db:migrate applied all 27 checked-in migrations to the dedicated forge_staging database on persistent staging branch br-autumn-union-za0opf1e. Three real PostgreSQL rehearsal cases passed on forge_migration_rehearsal: independent owners serialize, SQL failure rolls back mutations/journal, exact retry is a no-op, and edited applied history is rejected. Three safety unit cases passed. db:push is disabled in package scripts. Production/default database and local connection pointers are unchanged.

<issue id="e9a165c7-009d-4c13-b8ba-292a9dd38c8d" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-28/rehearse-serialized-expand-and-contract-database-releases">FOR-28</issue> remains In Progress for complete old/new application compatibility, resumable backfill recovery and the hosted staging release rehearsal. No production migration acceptance is implied.

### Expand-read compatibility checkpoint

Isolated staging and rehearsal now apply the complete 29-migration history, including the billing-grace expansion and provider-subscription workspace binding. The serialized migration-owner/failure/edited-history cases pass. Entitlement readers use validated whole-row JSON so the old table can be read before expansion; a direct read-only compatibility probe against the configured legacy database succeeded without writes. Full hosted old/new release and backfill rollback rehearsal remains open.

### Cancellation expansion rehearsal

The full history now has 30 migrations on isolated staging/rehearsal. Migration 0029 adds a constrained frozen cancellation cutoff and updates only the member-counter helper. The three PostgreSQL owner/concurrency/failure/history checks passed against the full history. Previously applied migrations were unchanged. Hosted old/new release, resumable backfill and rollback rehearsal remain open; production execution remains disabled.

issues.title: Correlate requests, commands, jobs and failures without payload leaks
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-OBSERVABILITY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want actionable telemetry, so that I can diagnose failures without reading private content.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Add request/command/run/deployment IDs; error capture and latency/queue/lease/spend metrics; redact prompts, tokens, signed URLs and private bodies.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §13; R12. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Diagnostics carry identifiers and bounded error codes, not secrets or raw user content.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the operator follows its correlation ID, request, command and worker failure can be connected.
* **AC-02** — When logs and error events are captured, none of those sensitive values appears.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an issue write fails downstream.
* When the operator follows its correlation ID.
* Then request, command and worker failure can be connected.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given fixtures contain a token, transcript and signed URL.
* When logs and error events are captured.
* Then none of those sensitive values appears.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Expose readiness checks and actionable operational alerts
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-HEALTH
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an on-call operator, I want dependency and freshness alerts, so that silent failures are detected before users report them.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Separate liveness/readiness; verify schema/dependencies; synthetic account/issue journey; alerts for stale jobs, outbox lag, failed uploads and DB saturation.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §13; R8, R12. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Health thresholds follow accepted objectives and never expose configuration secrets publicly.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When readiness is requested, readiness is unhealthy with a safe diagnostic code.
* **AC-02** — When the alert rule evaluates, the configured operator receives a testable alert and runbook link.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given required migrations or database connectivity are missing.
* When readiness is requested.
* Then readiness is unhealthy with a safe diagnostic code.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a scheduled job misses its accepted freshness threshold.
* When the alert rule evaluates.
* Then the configured operator receives a testable alert and runbook link.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-29](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-29/correlate-requests-commands-jobs-and-failures-without-payload-leaks>), [FOR-24](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-24/agree-capacity-service-and-recovery-objectives>).

issues.title: Enforce tenant-safe identifiers and relationships in the database
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-TENANT_SCHEMA
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want invalid cross-workspace relationships rejected, so that every access path protects my data.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Add scoped uniqueness/foreign-key or equivalent transaction checks for workspace/team/resource relationships; immutable IDs and parent-cycle validation.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §05; R1; E03. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A client-supplied workspace ID cannot grant access; private-team policy applies to aggregates too.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When a relation is inserted through a service or direct test transaction, the relation is rejected.
* **AC-02** — When the parent is changed, the cycle is rejected and previous relations remain.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given issue A and project B belong to different workspaces.
* When a relation is inserted through a service or direct test transaction.
* Then the relation is rejected.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a parent chain would point back to its child.
* When the parent is changed.
* Then the cycle is rejected and previous relations remain.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-21](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-21/decide-project-team-and-shared-resource-visibility-rules>), [FOR-28](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-28/rehearse-serialized-expand-and-contract-database-releases>).

issues.title: Commit commands, receipts, audit and outbox events atomically
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-COMMANDS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a user, I want a retried write to have one durable effect, so that uncertain network responses never duplicate work.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Introduce transaction-aware repositories; bind command ID/input hash; commit business mutation, receipt, history and outbox together; migrate public API wrapper.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §07; R3; E06-E07. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** An expired lease is ambiguous until reconciled, not automatic permission to repeat a mutation.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the same command ID/input is retried, one object and one event exist and the original result is returned.
* **AC-02** — When the second request is submitted, a typed conflict is returned without a second mutation.
* **AC-03** — Given two processes replay one command and faults occur before commit, after business mutation inside the transaction and after commit, when the command is retried at each boundary, then all pre-commit writes roll back together and post-commit retries resolve one durable result without duplicate business/history/outbox rows.
* **AC-04** — Given a command succeeded before its actor lost resource access, when the same receipt key is replayed after revocation, then current authorization is checked before returning protected result data and the business effect is not repeated.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a create command commits but its response is lost.
* When the same command ID/input is retried.
* Then one object and one event exist and the original result is returned.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a command key is reused with different input.
* When the second request is submitted.
* Then a typed conflict is returned without a second mutation.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given two processes replay one command and faults occur before commit, after business mutation inside the transaction and after commit.
* When the command is retried at each boundary.
* Then all pre-commit writes roll back together and post-commit retries resolve one durable result without duplicate business/history/outbox rows.

**AT-04 → AC-04**

* Given a command succeeded before its actor lost resource access.
* When the same receipt key is replayed after revocation.
* Then current authorization is checked before returning protected result data and the business effect is not repeated.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-31](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-31/enforce-tenant-safe-identifiers-and-relationships-in-the-database>).

Required for core production.

Blocking links describe prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation, contract design and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently where interfaces are agreed. Related links are coordination or conditional enablement work, not automatic blockers.

**Completion evidence:** every AC has a corresponding AT specification above. Attach results for the named commit/environment and relevant artifact. Resolve open policy choices before coding them; no passing test, estimate, owner assignment or delivery date is implied.

issues.title: Deliver external effects with recoverable outbox processing
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-OUTBOX
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want resumable event delivery, so that provider outages do not lose committed business work.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Own outbox row selection, event schema/version, provider idempotency/reference and ambiguous-effect reconciliation. Reuse [FOR-64](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-64/run-leased-resumable-background-jobs-with-operator-recovery>) for leases, bounded batches, backoff, dead letters and operator recovery. Never hold database transactions during network calls. Producer commands persist their event atomically through [FOR-32](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-32/commit-commands-receipts-audit-and-outbox-events-atomically>); they need not wait for this delivery worker before their own command tests can pass.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §07, §10; R3, R8. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Delivery is at least once; consumers deduplicate and ambiguous provider responses are reconciled.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the lease expires and processing resumes, provider identity is reconciled and the business effect is not blindly repeated.
* **AC-02** — When the retry budget is exhausted, the item enters an inspectable failure state and alerts without blocking unrelated items.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an outbox worker crashes after a provider accepts an effect.
* When the lease expires and processing resumes.
* Then provider identity is reconciled and the business effect is not blindly repeated.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a provider keeps failing.
* When the retry budget is exhausted.
* Then the item enters an inspectable failure state and alerts without blocking unrelated items.

## Dependencies and completion
