issues.title: Store all agent and issue files durably in private object storage
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-PRIVATE_STORAGE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a user, I want files to survive redeploys, so that saved attachments remain available from any device.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Replace the blob adapter for both agent artifacts and attachments; shared interface for issue/document files; persist checksum and workspace/resource metadata.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §09; R5; E10. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Private buckets and non-guessable keys are required; metadata persistence alone is not file durability.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When instance B reads it after A is replaced, identical checksum/content is returned.
* **AC-02** — When they request its storage URL, private content is denied.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an authorized file is stored by app instance A.
* When instance B reads it after A is replaced.
* Then identical checksum/content is returned.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an anonymous visitor knows an object key.
* When they request its storage URL.
* Then private content is denied.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-26](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-26/validate-service-specific-production-configuration-at-startup>), [FOR-31](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-31/enforce-tenant-safe-identifiers-and-relationships-in-the-database>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Upload files directly with validated upload intents and finalize
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-UPLOAD
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a user, I want reliable file uploads with clear limits, so that valid files do not fail at the hosting boundary.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Authorize upload intent, reserve quota, direct-upload bytes, validate actual object size/checksum/type, finalize idempotently; never send large base64 bodies through app functions.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §09; R5; E10, W1. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Only ready validated objects may be attached; client MIME/size are not trusted.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the direct upload is finalized twice, one ready attachment exists with verified checksum and no oversized app request.
* **AC-02** — When finalize is attempted, the file is rejected, quota reconciled and no usable attachment is exposed.
* **AC-03** — Given an upload intent exists but membership is revoked or the target is deleted before finalize, when a late finalize or attachment command is submitted, then current authorization/target checks deny publication, no usable attachment appears and reserved quota/orphan cleanup remains recoverable.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a permitted 5 MiB fixture and authorized user.
* When the direct upload is finalized twice.
* Then one ready attachment exists with verified checksum and no oversized app request.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the stored object exceeds the intent or has a bad checksum.
* When finalize is attempted.
* Then the file is rejected, quota reconciled and no usable attachment is exposed.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given an upload intent exists but membership is revoked or the target is deleted before finalize.
* When a late finalize or attachment command is submitted.
* Then current authorization/target checks deny publication, no usable attachment appears and reserved quota/orphan cleanup remains recoverable.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-34](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-34/store-all-agent-and-issue-files-durably-in-private-object-storage>), [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>).

issues.title: Authorize file downloads and isolate untrusted previews
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-FILE_ACCESS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a team member, I want private files shared only with authorized people, so that links and previews cannot leak team content.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Issue short-lived downloads after resource authorization; choose documented revocation window or authenticated proxy; isolate active HTML/SVG and bound extraction.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §09; R1, R5. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Permission checks apply when issuing a grant; existing URL lifetime must match the accepted revocation policy.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When A requests a download, a bounded grant returns the correct file with safe headers.
* **AC-02** — When B requests the file or the preview renders, B is denied and preview code cannot execute in the Forge application origin.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given member A can read a private issue attachment.
* When A requests a download.
* Then a bounded grant returns the correct file with safe headers.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given member B cannot read the issue or a preview contains active script.
* When B requests the file or the preview renders.
* Then B is denied and preview code cannot execute in the Forge application origin.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-35](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-35/upload-files-directly-with-validated-upload-intents-and-finalize>).

issues.title: Reconcile orphaned files and retry durable deletion
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-FILE_RETENTION
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want file lifecycle reconciliation, so that failed uploads and deletions do not leave inaccessible or retained data indefinitely.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Track pending/ready/rejected/deleting states; reconcile metadata and objects; implement tombstones, bounded sweeps and policy-specific lifetimes.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §09; R5, R7. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Deletion completion requires durable progress; a deleted DB row alone is not proof of byte deletion.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the lifecycle worker runs, expired orphan and deleted bytes are removed according to policy.
* **AC-02** — When the next worker resumes, deletion retries and completes without losing its progress record.
* **AC-03** — Given pending uploads, expired artifacts and deletion tombstones exist in isolated storage, when the configured scheduler invokes a bounded sweep twice, then eligible bytes and quota reservations reconcile without duplicates and freshness is visible to monitoring.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an upload never finalizes and an attachment is deleted.
* When the lifecycle worker runs.
* Then expired orphan and deleted bytes are removed according to policy.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given storage deletion fails after a tombstone is written.
* When the next worker resumes.
* Then deletion retries and completes without losing its progress record.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given pending uploads, expired artifacts and deletion tombstones exist in isolated storage.
* When the configured scheduler invokes a bounded sweep twice.
* Then eligible bytes and quota reservations reconcile without duplicates and freshness is visible to monitoring.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-34](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-34/store-all-agent-and-issue-files-durably-in-private-object-storage>), [FOR-23](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-23/define-retention-and-accountworkspace-deletion-behavior>), [FOR-64](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-64/run-leased-resumable-background-jobs-with-operator-recovery>).

issues.title: Rehearse recovery of database, files and encryption keys
issues.description:
**Type:** Release gate · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-RESTORE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want a proven restoration procedure, so that a backup can actually recover the product.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Restore into isolation; reconcile DB schema/rows/object checksums and key availability; run authenticated journeys; record measured RPO/RTO.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §13; R7. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Restoration evidence must meet accepted objectives; configuration alone does not close this gate.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When it is restored into an isolated environment, the app reads all three and measured loss/time meet accepted objectives.
* **AC-02** — When reconciliation runs, the gate fails with explicit missing items rather than a successful backup claim.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a dated backup containing issues, files and encrypted test credentials.
* When it is restored into an isolated environment.
* Then the app reads all three and measured loss/time meet accepted objectives.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a file or key is missing from the restored set.
* When reconciliation runs.
* Then the gate fails with explicit missing items rather than a successful backup claim.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Enforce one authorization policy across UI, API, tools and jobs
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-AUTHZ
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want every access path to apply the same permissions, so that hidden routes cannot bypass team privacy.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Centralize Actor/resource checks before pagination, search snippets, export, aggregation, file grants and deferred commands. Verify the foundation using real Postgres fixtures and currently enabled adapters. Every later API/tool/job adapter must reuse this policy and add parity evidence at its own enablement gate; the foundation does not wait for every optional transport to be built. Recheck current membership at deferred execution.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §05, §12; R1, R9; E04, E13. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Use current membership, role, scope and resource policy; never accept client recipient checks as authorization.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the same forbidden read/write is attempted through every supported transport, each denies access before exposing data or effects.
* **AC-02** — When the deferred job executes, authorization is rechecked and the effect is denied.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given workspace A/B and private team B fixtures.
* When the same forbidden read/write is attempted through every supported transport.
* Then each denies access before exposing data or effects.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a member loses access while a job waits.
* When the deferred job executes.
* Then authorization is rechecked and the effect is denied.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-31](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-31/enforce-tenant-safe-identifiers-and-relationships-in-the-database>).

Required for core production.

Blocking links describe prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation, contract design and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently where interfaces are agreed. Related links are coordination or conditional enablement work, not automatic blockers.

**Completion evidence:** every AC has a corresponding AT specification above. Attach results for the named commit/environment and relevant artifact. Resolve open policy choices before coding them; no passing test, estimate, owner assignment or delivery date is implied.

### Implementation started — private-team read boundaries

Confirmed owners/admins may read all private teams within their workspace, including through read-only API credentials with teams:read. Regular nonmembers must not receive private-team metadata through direct lookup or paginated lists. Implementing SQL visibility filtering before pagination and aligning directory readers with the same role policy. This is an authorization slice; tenant-safe canonical schema, remaining resource adapters, deferred revocation checks and release evidence still remain.

### Team read boundaries verified

[Confirmed policy and fixture matrix](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-resource-visibility-policy-and-implementation-fixtures-caf8d571259a>). SQL now filters team directory, direct lookup and API pagination before LIMIT/cursors. Regular private-team nonmembers receive no private metadata; read-only owner/admin credentials retain their confirmed private-team read access with teams:read, without requiring teams:write. Six real PostgreSQL cases passed for pagination, cursor exclusion, direct ID/slug lookup, directories, cross-workspace denial and scope enforcement. Twelve executable resource-policy fixtures and 30 existing team/API handler checks passed. Full app verification: 1,269 tests plus 4 workflow tests; production build passed.

Projects/issues/initiatives/documents still require canonical scoped queries and enabled-adapter parity. <issue id="55e64c7b-7034-4ced-bf17-6c30cd33e38b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs">FOR-39</issue> remains In Progress rather than treating pure policy fixtures as complete authorization enforcement.

issues.title: Manage shared issue statuses, labels and workflow transitions
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-ISSUE_DEFS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a team admin, I want shared workflow definitions, so that teammates classify and transition issues consistently.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist status types/order, label scope and transition rules; safely migrate/delete referenced definitions; reuse in all issue controls.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 areas 6-7, §05; E02-E03. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Only authorized admins change definitions; referenced values cannot silently become invalid.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When an admin creates status Ready and label Mobile, both see the same definitions after reload.
* **AC-02** — When an admin removes it without a replacement, the action is rejected or requires an explicit migration choice.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given two users share team Engineering.
* When an admin creates status Ready and label Mobile.
* Then both see the same definitions after reload.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a status is still assigned to issues.
* When an admin removes it without a replacement.
* Then the action is rejected or requires an explicit migration choice.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>), [FOR-32](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-32/commit-commands-receipts-audit-and-outbox-events-atomically>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Create canonical issues from every composer
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-ISSUE_CREATE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a team member, I want a shared issue with a stable identity, so that my teammates can act on work I create.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Create UUID and transactionally allocated team number; validate assignee/relations; route full and inline composers to one command; integrate [FOR-138](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-138/apply-personal-auto-assignment-during-canonical-issue-creation>) through this canonical command. The personal automation story depends on this foundation; core creation must still preserve explicit assignment intent.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §05; R2; E02-E03. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Creation retries return the same issue; explicit assignment intent is preserved.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When a user creates an issue and the other reloads, both see one matching ID and team number.
* **AC-02** — When creation runs concurrently, distinct commands get unique numbers and a retry creates no extra issue.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given two independent browsers in Engineering.
* When a user creates an issue and the other reloads.
* Then both see one matching ID and team number.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given two requests race for the next team number or replay one command.
* When creation runs concurrently.
* Then distinct commands get unique numbers and a retry creates no extra issue.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-40](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-40/manage-shared-issue-statuses-labels-and-workflow-transitions>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

## Screenshot active-issue limit refinement

Source: [Forge plan matrix](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b>). **BR-02:** Free allows 250 non-archived issues workspace-wide; paid plans have no commercial issue cap. Server plan and canonical active count are authority; reserve/check capacity atomically with issue creation through UI, API, agent, duplicate/create and imports.
**AC-03 → BR-02:** A Free workspace at 249 can create issue 250; further creation is denied without a partial issue, event, notification or import record. Concurrent writers cannot exceed 250. Archived issues do not count; a forged paid plan cannot bypass the cap.
**AT-03 → AC-03:** Given 249 non-archived Free issues plus archived fixtures, when two distinct creates run concurrently against real Postgres, then exactly one succeeds and active count is 250. Replay the winner and assert no duplicate. Exercise every enabled create/import transport and a genuine paid fixture with more than 250 active issues. Restore/archive transitions are covered by <issue id="b19f24b0-4beb-409e-ae59-da8a5a137c46" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-45/delete-and-restore-issues-with-consistent-downstream-state">FOR-45</issue>. This is a required test specification, not passing evidence.

issues.title: Edit issue properties with visible conflict resolution
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-ISSUE_EDIT
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want concurrent edits reconciled, so that another person's changes are not silently overwritten.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Version-precondition updates, typed conflicts, optimistic pending/error states, safe bulk results and explicit reassignment rules; provide the version-checked command used by [FOR-139](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-139/assign-unowned-issues-when-their-actor-moves-them-to-started>); personal automation is implemented after this foundation, avoiding a circular dependency.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §05; R2. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** An outdated expectedVersion cannot overwrite the current record.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When one saves then the other saves a conflicting change, the second receives the newest authorized version and a visible resolution choice.
* **AC-02** — When the client receives its result, pending UI is reconciled and each failed item retains a retryable draft.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given two users loaded issue version 3.
* When one saves then the other saves a conflicting change.
* Then the second receives the newest authorized version and a visible resolution choice.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a save or bulk operation fails.
* When the client receives its result.
* Then pending UI is reconciled and each failed item retains a retryable draft.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-41](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-41/create-canonical-issues-from-every-composer>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-ISSUE_LIST
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

issues.title: Manage parent, sub-issue and dependency relationships
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-ISSUE_RELATIONS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want explicit related and blocking work, so that dependencies are visible and valid.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist typed links/subissues; validate workspace/team visibility, cycles and deletion behavior; show reciprocal relationships.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §05; R1-R2. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Forbidden cross-tenant references and cyclic parent chains are rejected.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When A is marked blocked by B, A and B show reciprocal blocking information after reload.
* **AC-02** — When A is assigned B as parent, the cycle is rejected without corrupting either issue.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given issues A and B in an authorized team.
* When A is marked blocked by B.
* Then A and B show reciprocal blocking information after reload.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given A is already an ancestor of B.
* When A is assigned B as parent.
* Then the cycle is rejected without corrupting either issue.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-42](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-42/edit-issue-properties-with-visible-conflict-resolution>).

issues.title: Delete and restore issues with consistent downstream state
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-ISSUE_DELETE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an authorized teammate, I want recoverable deletion, so that mistakes can be corrected without stale search or links.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Use deletion markers and policy-driven purge; update search, lists, subscriptions, relations and files; preserve audit history.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §05; R2, R10. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Only authorized actors delete/restore; purge semantics follow the agreed policy.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When it is deleted then restored within the allowed period, normal queries hide it while deleted and restored authorized content reappears.
* **AC-02** — When the issue is requested, a safe not-found result appears without orphaned private content.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an issue has comments and subscriptions.
* When it is deleted then restored within the allowed period.
* Then normal queries hide it while deleted and restored authorized content reappears.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given another user follows an old link after purge.
* When the issue is requested.
* Then a safe not-found result appears without orphaned private content.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-42](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-42/edit-issue-properties-with-visible-conflict-resolution>), [FOR-23](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-23/define-retention-and-accountworkspace-deletion-behavior>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

## Screenshot active-issue capacity during restore/archive

Source: [Forge plan matrix](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b>); Free permits 250 non-archived issues. **BR-02:** Restoring/unarchiving an issue must obey the same atomic active-issue capacity as <issue id="1b7d62ce-f7de-4a13-8400-3b4f6708ec59" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-41/create-canonical-issues-from-every-composer">FOR-41</issue>; archiving releases capacity exactly once. Do not delete archived records or reset counts to work around limits.
**AC-04 → BR-02:** Unarchive/restore that reintroduces an active issue is refused at capacity with the original record preserved. Replayed archive/restore does not duplicate quota changes, and concurrent restore/create cannot exceed 250.
**AT-04 → AC-04:** Given Free has 250 active issues and one archived issue, when the archived issue is unarchived, then it remains archived and the active count stays 250. Archive one active issue, then concurrently unarchive and create: exactly one may consume the released slot. Repeat operations and verify no negative/double accounting. Recheck actor/workspace authorization and the live plan. This is a required test specification, not passing evidence.

issues.title: Discuss issues with durable comments and mentions
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-COMMENTS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want shared comments and mentions, so that discussion reaches the right people and survives reloads.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist validated rich text, author/edit metadata and eligible mention targets through the canonical command. Emit activity/notification outbox rows atomically; actual asynchronous fan-out belongs to [FOR-33](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-33/deliver-external-effects-with-recoverable-outbox-processing>) and [FOR-65](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-65/deliver-authorized-issue-events-into-a-shared-inbox>). Preserve failed drafts. Use a shared safe rich-text renderer and validate links/nodes at the trust boundary; browser/imported text must not become executable markup.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 4, §05, §10. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Mention targets must have eligible access; clients cannot forge authors or notification recipients.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When Alice comments and mentions Bob then reloads, one authored comment and mention event remain visible.
* **AC-02** — When the comment command is processed, the retry deduplicates and forbidden recipient disclosure is prevented.
* **AC-03** — Given stored comment fixtures include script nodes, event-handler attributes and unsafe links, when the comment is validated and rendered after reload, then unsupported content is rejected or safely rendered without script execution, unsafe navigation or private-data disclosure.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an issue is visible to Alice and Bob.
* When Alice comments and mentions Bob then reloads.
* Then one authored comment and mention event remain visible.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a retry follows a lost response or a mention targets a forbidden user.
* When the comment command is processed.
* Then the retry deduplicates and forbidden recipient disclosure is prevented.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given stored comment fixtures include script nodes, event-handler attributes and unsafe links.
* When the comment is validated and rendered after reload.
* Then unsupported content is rejected or safely rendered without script execution, unsafe navigation or private-data disclosure.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-41](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-41/create-canonical-issues-from-every-composer>).

Required for core production.

issues.title: React to comments and subscribe to issue activity
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-REACTIONS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want reactions and subscription controls to sync, so that acknowledgement and notification preferences are reliable.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist per-user reaction uniqueness and subscriptions; define assignment/mention behavior separately from optional comment updates.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 4, §10; E11. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A user changes only their own reaction/subscription; unsubscribing does not delete discussion.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When Bob opens a second browser, the same subscription and one reaction are shown.
* **AC-02** — When later comment and mention events arrive, comment notifications follow subscription policy while direct mentions follow the agreed rule; no duplicate reaction is added.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given Bob subscribes to issue A and reacts to its comment.
* When Bob opens a second browser.
* Then the same subscription and one reaction are shown.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given Bob unsubscribes and the same reaction request is retried.
* When later comment and mention events arrive.
* Then comment notifications follow subscription policy while direct mentions follow the agreed rule; no duplicate reaction is added.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Attach durable files to issues and comments
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-ISSUE_FILES
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want issue attachments accessible to permitted collaborators, so that supporting evidence is shared reliably.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Bind ready upload intents to issue/comment commands; authorized download and detach flows; preserve file checksums and lifecycle links.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 4, §09. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Unready uploads and files owned by another unauthorized resource cannot be attached.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the file is attached and another member opens it after redeploy, the same verified content is available.
* **AC-02** — When attachment or download is attempted, the request is denied without exposing bytes.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a ready upload and authorized issue.
* When the file is attached and another member opens it after redeploy.
* Then the same verified content is available.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an upload is pending or its issue is inaccessible.
* When attachment or download is attempted.
* Then the request is denied without exposing bytes.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-36](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-36/authorize-file-downloads-and-isolate-untrusted-previews>), [FOR-46](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-46/discuss-issues-with-durable-comments-and-mentions>).

**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-ACTIVITY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want reliable issue history, so that I understand who changed work and when.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Read immutable committed activity with stable cursors and trustworthy attribution. This slice owns the history projection/UI for property changes and comments; relationship, reaction and import producers append the same versioned activity contract when those features land. Do not add a second audit writer or block the base history view on every future producer. Distinguish imported historical attribution and never trust arbitrary client authors/timestamps.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §05, §07; R3. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** History is generated by authorized commands, not arbitrary client authors/timestamps.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When a collaborator opens its activity, events appear in deterministic order with trustworthy attribution.
* **AC-02** — When history is loaded, the original event appears once and no forged actor is accepted.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an issue changes status then receives a comment.
* When a collaborator opens its activity.
* Then events appear in deterministic order with trustworthy attribution.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the same command is retried.
* When history is loaded.
* Then the original event appears once and no forged actor is accepted.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-42](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-42/edit-issue-properties-with-visible-conflict-resolution>), [FOR-46](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-46/discuss-issues-with-durable-comments-and-mentions>).

Required for core production.

Blocking links describe prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation, contract design and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently where interfaces are agreed. Related links are coordination or conditional enablement work, not automatic blockers.

**Completion evidence:** every AC has a corresponding AT specification above. Attach results for the named commit/environment and relevant artifact. Resolve open policy choices before coding them; no passing test, estimate, owner assignment or delivery date is implied.

issues.title: Triage incoming work through the canonical issue lifecycle
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-TRIAGE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a triager, I want to accept, assign or decline incoming work, so that triage and team issues stay consistent.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Replace separate local triage data; map triage decisions to shared issue state, history and events; preserve valid source references.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 areas 4-7, §05. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Triage does not create a second independent copy of the same issue.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When a triager accepts and assigns it, the same issue ID appears in team work with matching history.
* **AC-02** — When their commands race, one decision commits and the other gets a visible conflict.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an incoming canonical issue in triage.
* When a triager accepts and assigns it.
* Then the same issue ID appears in team work with matching history.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given two triagers decide on the same version.
* When their commands race.
* Then one decision commits and the other gets a visible conflict.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-42](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-42/edit-issue-properties-with-visible-conflict-resolution>), [FOR-43](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-43/find-and-filter-shared-issues-with-bounded-server-queries>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Use shared assigned, created and subscribed issue views
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-MY_ISSUES
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want My issues to reflect shared activity, so that my personal queue stays accurate across devices.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Query the canonical service for supported tabs and filters; share edits/details with team views; refresh on authorized events.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 5, §05. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** The current actor is server-derived and revoked/private items disappear from personal queues.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When Bob opens My issues on another device, the issue appears with the same ID and editable state.
* **AC-02** — When the queue refreshes or receives invalidation, the private issue and its cached details are removed.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given Bob is assigned an issue by Alice.
* When Bob opens My issues on another device.
* Then the issue appears with the same ID and editable state.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given Bob loses team access.
* When the queue refreshes or receives invalidation.
* Then the private issue and its cached details are removed.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-43](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-43/find-and-filter-shared-issues-with-bounded-server-queries>), [FOR-47](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-47/react-to-comments-and-subscribe-to-issue-activity>).
Required for the core production release.

Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Prevent account/workspace switches from revealing stale data
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-CACHE_SCOPE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a user of multiple accounts, I want cached data scoped correctly, so that one session cannot show another's content.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Include actor/workspace in query keys; clear protected cache on logout/switch; cancel old requests and handle late responses; define offline drafts.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §06, §12; R1, R9. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Late responses from a previous scope must not repopulate the active scope.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the user signs into B before A's slow request completes, B sees no A data before or after the response arrives.
* **AC-02** — When connectivity is lost, the UI retains a labeled unsaved draft and never claims a server commit.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given account A has private cached issues.
* When the user signs into B before A's slow request completes.
* Then B sees no A data before or after the response arrives.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a user writes while offline.
* When connectivity is lost.
* Then the UI retains a labeled unsaved draft and never claims a server commit.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-43](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-43/find-and-filter-shared-issues-with-bounded-server-queries>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Preview and back up browser data before importing
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-IMPORT_PREVIEW
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an existing user, I want a dry-run migration preview and backup, so that I know what will move before my data changes.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Enumerate legacy store versions/scopes; preserve malformed raw bytes; show counts, references, destination, exclusions and conflicts; offer local backup.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §06; R2. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Preview is read-only and never auto-uploads every origin key on login.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the user previews migration, counts/invalid records and destination choices appear while all originals remain unchanged.
* **AC-02** — When the user attempts import, confirmation of those specific choices is required before upload.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given legacy issues, labels and a malformed document payload exist.
* When the user previews migration.
* Then counts/invalid records and destination choices appear while all originals remain unchanged.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given ownership or destination is ambiguous.
* When the user attempts import.
* Then confirmation of those specific choices is required before upload.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-22](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-22/decide-ownership-and-conflict-rules-for-legacy-browser-data>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Create shared projects and link canonical issues
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-PROJECTS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a project lead, I want shared project ownership and issue membership, so that a project represents the team's real work.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist projects, status/lead/dates, teams and issue membership; shared directory/detail and version checks; minimal project records precede import.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 8, §05. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Project and issue relations follow the approved multi-team visibility model.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When Bob opens its directory/detail, the project and canonical issue membership match.
* **AC-02** — When the request is processed, the relation is denied without leaking private membership or counts.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given Alice creates a project and links an issue.
* When Bob opens its directory/detail.
* Then the project and canonical issue membership match.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an inaccessible team issue is linked.
* When the request is processed.
* Then the relation is denied without leaking private membership or counts.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Plan shared current and upcoming cycles
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-CYCLES
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a team member, I want shared cycle membership and dates, so that planning is consistent across devices.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist cycle windows/timezone and issue membership; replace legacy cycle-only issue records with canonical IDs; validate date ordering and team compatibility.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 9, §05. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Cycle membership cannot create a duplicate issue or cross an unauthorized team boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When another member opens the cycle, the same issue and dates appear.
* **AC-02** — When the command runs, it is rejected or conflicts without silently losing the newer assignment.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a canonical issue is assigned to an upcoming cycle.
* When another member opens the cycle.
* Then the same issue and dates appear.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a cycle assignment is invalid or races with another edit.
* When the command runs.
* Then it is rejected or conflicts without silently losing the newer assignment.

## Dependencies and completion

* When another member opens the cycle.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-IMPORT_EXECUTE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an existing user, I want an interrupted import to resume safely, so that browser history becomes shared without duplication.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Versioned manifests, source fingerprints, legacy-to-server ID maps, ordered batches, validated historical data and file checksums; quarantine invalid records. Import only enabled core domains in this slice; preserve/exclude document and view records until their separately linked migration work is ready.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §06; R2. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Import uniqueness and duplicate detection apply across retries and overlapping browser profiles.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the same manifest resumes, each accepted entity appears once with valid remapped links.
* **AC-02** — When reconciliation detects the difference, the user reviews the delta/conflict before existing server data is altered.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an import stops halfway through related issues and files.
* When the same manifest resumes.
* Then each accepted entity appears once with valid remapped links.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the source snapshot changes or a duplicate arrives in another import.
* When reconciliation detects the difference.
* Then the user reviews the delta/conflict before existing server data is altered.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-53](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-53/preview-and-back-up-browser-data-before-importing>), [FOR-44](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-44/manage-parent-sub-issue-and-dependency-relationships>), [FOR-48](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-48/attach-durable-files-to-issues-and-comments>), [FOR-54](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-54/create-shared-projects-and-link-canonical-issues>), [FOR-55](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-55/plan-shared-current-and-upcoming-cycles>).
Required for the core production release.

issues.title: Reconcile migration results and switch every issue entry point
issues.description:
**Type:** Release gate · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-CUTOVER
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want a verified cutover, so that users do not split work between local and server stores.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Compare counts/relationships/checksums, report rejects, retain backup, enable scoped server authority together; document rollback to preserved data.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §06, §14; R2. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** No indefinite dual-write authority; cleanup is explicit and only follows reconciliation.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the workspace cuts over, all composers, lists, My issues and triage use canonical IDs.
* **AC-02** — When the cutover gate is evaluated, unresolved discrepancies block completion and source data remains recoverable.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a completed manifest and reconciled files.
* When the workspace cuts over.
* Then all composers, lists, My issues and triage use canonical IDs.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given some entities failed import.
* When the cutover gate is evaluated.
* Then unresolved discrepancies block completion and source data remains recoverable.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Manage project milestones, updates and shared metadata
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PROJECT_PROGRESS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a project lead, I want durable milestones and updates, so that collaborators see the same progress and decisions.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist milestones, project statuses/labels and authored updates; derive progress from canonical issues; version changes and activity.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 8, §14. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Project progress must be derived from authorized real data rather than local aggregates.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When one is completed and a lead posts an update, authorized collaborators see matching progress and attributed update.
* **AC-02** — When the update/query executes, conflicts are surfaced and hidden work is not disclosed.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a milestone has two visible issues.
* When one is completed and a lead posts an update.
* Then authorized collaborators see matching progress and attributed update.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a stale editor changes a milestone or a private issue affects progress.
* When the update/query executes.
* Then conflicts are surfaced and hidden work is not disclosed.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-54](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-54/create-shared-projects-and-link-canonical-issues>), [FOR-49](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-49/show-attributable-issue-history-from-committed-changes>).

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-INITIATIVES
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace lead, I want shared initiatives, so that strategic progress is based on real projects.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist initiative metadata, project links and status; compute authorized rollups; version directory/detail updates.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 10, §14. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

* **AC-02** — When they request initiative details and totals, the visibility policy is applied to both records and aggregates.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-VIEWS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want saved filters and favorites across devices, so that I can return to useful work views.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Version validated filter definitions and sharing scope; server favorites by actor; execute filters through authorized domain queries.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 11, §06. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Saving a shared filter grants no additional access to its underlying records.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When Bob and Alice open them on new devices, visibility and personal favorites match their owners and sharing choices.
* **AC-02** — When it executes, validation gives a safe error/fallback and no hidden records are returned.

* When Bob and Alice open them on new devices.

* Given a saved filter contains an unknown field or inaccessible IDs.

issues.title: Create and edit shared documents with revision conflicts
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-DOCUMENTS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want shared documents and recoverable revisions, so that written context survives device changes and concurrent edits.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist validated Tiptap JSON, plain-text projection, title/icon/owner/timestamps and revisions; resource-scoped access; failed-draft retry.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 12, §05; E02. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Concurrent co-editing is not promised; stale saves must never silently replace newer text.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the save succeeds, Bob sees the same content and revision metadata.
* **AC-02** — When the server checks its version, a conflict preserves both the current content and Bob's draft.
* **AC-03** — Given stored rich-text JSON includes unsafe nodes, event attributes or executable links, when a document is saved, imported and rendered, then validation and the shared renderer prevent executable content while preserving supported formatting and the author's recoverable draft.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given Alice edits a document and Bob opens it elsewhere.
* When the save succeeds.
* Then Bob sees the same content and revision metadata.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given Bob saves an older revision.
* When the server checks its version.
* Then a conflict preserves both the current content and Bob's draft.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given stored rich-text JSON includes unsafe nodes, event attributes or executable links.
* When a document is saved, imported and rendered.
* Then validation and the shared renderer prevent executable content while preserving supported formatting and the author's recoverable draft.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-32](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-32/commit-commands-receipts-audit-and-outbox-events-atomically>), [FOR-36](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-36/authorize-file-downloads-and-isolate-untrusted-previews>).

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Concurrent co-editing is not promised; stale saves must never silently replace newer text.

* **AC-02** — When the server checks its version, a conflict preserves both the current content and Bob's draft.

* When the server checks its version.

* When a document is saved, imported and rendered.

issues.title: Instantiate server templates through canonical commands
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-TEMPLATES
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a team member, I want templates to create real issues and projects, so that reusable setups work consistently.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Reuse existing template tables/defaults; validate current references, scope and chosen revision at application time; call issue/project commands.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 15, §05; E03. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A template never grants access or bypasses current assignment/status validation.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When a user creates from it twice with one retried command, one result per distinct command is created with expected values.
* **AC-02** — When the template is applied, a repairable validation result appears and no invalid object is created.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an accessible template with current references.
* When a user creates from it twice with one retried command.
* Then one result per distinct command is created with expected values.

issues.title: Run leased, resumable background jobs with operator recovery
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-JOBS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want duplicate-safe background jobs, so that crashes and scheduler overlap do not corrupt work.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Own the shared durable job substrate: identity, scheduled time, lease/fencing, checkpoint, retry/dead-letter state and operator replay commands. Reuse existing Workflow SDK patterns where applicable. Publish safe metrics/events and test recovery using deterministic fixtures. Outbox delivery in [FOR-33](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-33/deliver-external-effects-with-recoverable-outbox-processing>), retention and notification jobs consume this substrate rather than implementing separate lease engines. Final scheduler freshness thresholds and alert delivery are verified in [FOR-30](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-30/expose-readiness-checks-and-actionable-operational-alerts>); they are release evidence, not a prerequisite for building the runner.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §10; R8; E16. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A scheduler trigger is not proof of success; execution ownership and freshness are observable.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the job is retried after lease expiry, one logical effect completes and checkpoints prevent replayed mutations.
* **AC-02** — When the operator inspects its state, an actionable failure and safe recovery command are available.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given two workers receive the same job and one crashes.
* When the job is retried after lease expiry.
* Then one logical effect completes and checkpoints prevent replayed mutations.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a permanently failing job exhausts retries.
* When the operator inspects its state.
* Then an actionable failure and safe recovery command are available.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-32](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-32/commit-commands-receipts-audit-and-outbox-events-atomically>), [FOR-29](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-29/correlate-requests-commands-jobs-and-failures-without-payload-leaks>).

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-INBOX
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want relevant assignments, mentions and subscribed updates, so that I know when my work needs attention.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist recipient inbox entries from committed events; group/dedupe issue activity; apply current access, self-event and subscription rules.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §10; R1, R8; E11. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Delivery recipients are determined server-side; client publishInboxUpdate is not authorization.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When committed events are delivered twice out of order, Bob sees ordered relevant activity once with the newest snapshot.
* **AC-02** — When the worker evaluates recipients, the private update is not delivered or exposed.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given Bob subscribes to an issue and is mentioned.
* When committed events are delivered twice out of order.
* Then Bob sees ordered relevant activity once with the newest snapshot.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given Bob loses access before delivery.
* When the worker evaluates recipients.
* Then the private update is not delivered or exposed.

issues.title: Sync inbox read, snooze and delete state across devices
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** [FOR-65](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-65/deliver-authorized-issue-events-into-a-shared-inbox>)\_STATE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want inbox actions to follow me across devices, so that handled work does not repeatedly distract me.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Own per-user inbox-item state only: read/unread, snooze deadline, hide/delete state, bulk-command results and replay cursor reconciliation. Issue subscriptions are owned by [FOR-47](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-47/react-to-comments-and-subscribe-to-issue-activity>); channel/type delivery preferences and priority-inbox classification are owned by [FOR-145](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-145/persist-notification-channel-choices-and-enforce-delivery-preferences>). Reading or deleting an inbox item must not change subscription or delivery consent.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 13, §10. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Deleting an inbox item never deletes its issue; snooze expiry follows the agreed timezone/deadline contract.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When he opens B and the snooze deadline passes, read state matches and the snoozed item returns according to policy.
* **AC-02** — When inbox replay runs, events deduplicate and a user-deleted notification resurfaces only under the defined new-event rule.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given Bob reads and snoozes items on device A.
* When he opens B and the snooze deadline passes.
* Then read state matches and the snoozed item returns according to policy.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given Bob reconnects after receiving duplicate events.
* When inbox replay runs.
* Then events deduplicate and a user-deleted notification resurfaces only under the defined new-event rule.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-65](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-65/deliver-authorized-issue-events-into-a-shared-inbox>).

issues.title: Deliver transactional notifications with bounce and retry handling
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want dependable notification email, so that important work reaches me when Forge is closed.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Separate mail effects from inbox state; provider idempotency/reference, retries, suppression/bounces, opt-out and access-safe content.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §10, §13. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

issues.title: Generate one canonical issue for each recurring occurrence
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-RECURRENCE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a team lead, I want recurring work generated reliably, so that schedules remain useful through downtime and time changes.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Add next occurrence/timezone/DST policy and unique schedule+occurrence identity; decide catch-up and template revision; invoke the canonical issue command. Basic recurring generation has no cycle requirement. If a schedule/template explicitly selects a cycle, use the canonical cycle validator and gate that option until [FOR-55](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-55/plan-shared-current-and-upcoming-cycles>) is ready; never create a second cycle store.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §10; R8; E03. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Disabled/deleted schedules and unauthorized teams must not generate work.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When duplicate workers process the due occurrence, one issue is created at the documented local-time interpretation.
* **AC-02** — When catch-up processing resumes, only policy-eligible occurrences are generated once and skipped ones are explained.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a Europe/Paris schedule spans a daylight-saving change.
* When duplicate workers process the due occurrence.
* Then one issue is created at the documented local-time interpretation.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a week of downtime or a disabled schedule occurs.
* When catch-up processing resumes.
* Then only policy-eligible occurrences are generated once and skipped ones are explained.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Close cycles and carry unfinished work without duplication
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-CYCLE_ROLLOVER
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a team lead, I want predictable cycle rollover, so that unfinished work and historical progress remain understandable.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Implement timezone-aware boundaries, carryover policy, historical membership and idempotent rollover commands; expose upcoming/current state.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §10; R8. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Rollover changes membership of canonical issues rather than cloning them.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When rollover runs twice, history is preserved and the configured carryover happens once.
* **AC-02** — When processing resumes, version rules prevent lost updates and the cycle reaches one consistent state.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a cycle ends with one completed and one unfinished issue.
* When rollover runs twice.
* Then history is preserved and the configured carryover happens once.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an issue changes during rollover or the worker crashes.
* When processing resumes.
* Then version rules prevent lost updates and the cycle reaches one consistent state.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-64](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-64/run-leased-resumable-background-jobs-with-operator-recovery>), [FOR-55](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-55/plan-shared-current-and-upcoming-cycles>).
