issues.title: Rotate encrypted provider credentials without losing access
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-KEY_ROTATION
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want versioned key rotation, so that Calls and BYOK credentials remain recoverable while keys change.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Add key IDs/keyring, current-write/older-read support, resumable re-encryption, completeness checks, recovery and old-key retirement; inspect possible secret exposure without assuming it from titles.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §12; R13; E15. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Do not replace the single environment key before every retained ciphertext can be decrypted or re-encrypted.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When key B is introduced and re-encryption is interrupted then resumed, old/new records remain readable and new writes use B.
* **AC-02** — When operator attempts retirement, retirement is blocked and the missing migration coverage is reported.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given credentials exist under old key A.
* When key B is introduced and re-encryption is interrupted then resumed.
* Then old/new records remain readable and new writes use B.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given some retained ciphertext still requires A.
* When operator attempts retirement.
* Then retirement is blocked and the missing migration coverage is reported.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-26](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-26/validate-service-specific-production-configuration-at-startup>), [FOR-27](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-27/provision-isolated-staging-and-disposable-integration-test-data>).

issues.title: Connect, reconnect and disconnect meeting providers in production
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-CALLS_OAUTH
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace admin, I want reliable meeting-provider authorization, so that imports use the right account and permissions.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Validate existing Google/Teams/Zoom flows with selected supported providers; bind state/PKCE, callback origins, encrypted tokens and refresh races; show setup/reconnect errors.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §10, §12; E12, E15. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Provider-specific consent and required permissions must be explicit; disconnect revokes Forge-held access.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When OAuth callback completes, the correct workspace/team connection is stored without browser token exposure.
* **AC-02** — When callback is attempted, authorization fails without changing the existing connection.
* **AC-03** — Given a connected provider token expires or the user disconnects during refresh, when refresh/reconnect jobs race or a later sync is attempted, then one safe token state survives, disconnected credentials cannot be reused and the UI shows the real reconnect state.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an admin authorizes a configured provider.
* When OAuth callback completes.
* Then the correct workspace/team connection is stored without browser token exposure.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given state is replayed, expired or bound to another user.
* When callback is attempted.
* Then authorization fails without changing the existing connection.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given a connected provider token expires or the user disconnects during refresh.
* When refresh/reconnect jobs race or a later sync is attempted.
* Then one safe token state survives, disconnected credentials cannot be reused and the UI shows the real reconnect state.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-70](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-70/rotate-encrypted-provider-credentials-without-losing-access>), [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>).

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-CALLS_SYNC
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

issues.title: Convert call actions into linked canonical issues
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-CALL_TO_ISSUE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a meeting participant, I want an action converted into a shared issue, so that follow-up work is tracked beyond the recap.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Create durable call-action/issue relation inside the command flow; choose authorized team/project; show bidirectional links and retry states.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §06, §10; E12. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Retrying conversion returns the same issue; call visibility does not bypass destination issue permissions.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the user creates an issue then retries after a lost response, one canonical issue and stable backlink exist.
* **AC-02** — When conversion is submitted, it is denied and the call action is not marked as successfully converted.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an accessible call action.
* When the user creates an issue then retries after a lost response.
* Then one canonical issue and stable backlink exist.

issues.title: Apply explicit retention to raw and derived meeting data
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-CALL_RETENTION
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want meeting-data expiry to match the stated policy, so that sensitive summaries are not accidentally retained forever.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Extend/verify sweeps for transcripts, summaries, decisions, notes/actions and exports according to their separate policies; handle backups and re-import tombstones.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §10; R10; E12. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Current transcript clearing alone does not implement deletion of derived content.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When each class reaches its accepted expiry, the correct data is removed or retained with an auditable reason.
* **AC-02** — When sync runs again, the documented re-import policy prevents unintended resurrection.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a call has raw transcript, summary, actions and export.
* When each class reaches its accepted expiry.
* Then the correct data is removed or retained with an auditable reason.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an expired provider call is rediscovered.
* When sync runs again.
* Then the documented re-import policy prevents unintended resurrection.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Define provider, spending and execution admission policy
issues.description:
**Type:** Product decision · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_POLICY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want explicit agent limits and provider choices, so that use and spend stay within an accepted boundary.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Decide per-user/workspace/global-provider cap scope, budget periods, unknown pricing behavior, disconnect/deadline policy, allowed capabilities and sandbox backend.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §08; R4, R6; E08. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Unknown custom pricing is not automatically free; numeric caps are choices, not invented commitments.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the policy is approved, each has an eligibility, accounting and concurrency rule.
* **AC-02** — When its production enablement is reviewed, it remains disabled or has an explicitly bounded accepted policy.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given managed, BYOK and custom models are available.
* When the policy is approved.
* Then each has an eligibility, accounting and concurrency rule.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a provider cost or execution ownership is unknown.
* When its production enablement is reviewed.
* Then it remains disabled or has an explicitly bounded accepted policy.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-24](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-24/agree-capacity-service-and-recovery-objectives>).

Required before enabling this slice. Conditional extensions are governed by the accepted release manifest and their stated evidence checks; an excluded feature stays unavailable and is not marked implemented.

Blocking links describe prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation, contract design and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently where interfaces are agreed. Related links are coordination or conditional enablement work, not automatic blockers.

**Completion evidence:** every AC has a corresponding AT specification above. Attach results for the named commit/environment and relevant artifact. Resolve open policy choices before coding them; no passing test, estimate, owner assignment or delivery date is implied.

## Confirmed budget policy and implementation start · 28 October 2026

User confirmed US$5 per active member/month for Free, Starter and Plus, pooled at workspace level. Paid overage requires explicit owner/admin opt-in and a separate monthly cap; it is off by default. Preparing shared allowance/admission arithmetic in integer USD millionths, including recorded spend, outstanding reservations and the proposed run reservation. Full transactional admission and settlement remain <issue id="8fa7eb8a-25fc-47b5-8459-9bcd3d62ff2b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-76/atomically-admit-runs-and-reserve-provider-spend">FOR-76</issue>, and commercial overage pricing/payment authorization remains under refinement.

### Included pool and overage contract implemented locally · 28 October 2026

`workspace-ai-budget.ts` defines **5,000,000 USD millionths per active member/month** for the standard plans, independent of EUR/USD subscription billing. Overage defaults disabled. Enabled policy requires an explicit finite nonnegative monthly cap, plus separate server-confirmed authority to incur paid usage. The pure admission evaluator accounts for settled cost + outstanding reservations + proposed reservation; it denies exhaustion, over-cap exposure, malformed accounting and overflow. Membership changes alter available allowance without erasing settled consumption. No API charges or usage invoices are issued by this code.

Verification: **5 billing files / 28 tests passed**, app TypeScript passed, billing ESLint and diff checks passed. Quota row locking, atomic reservation/run creation, settlement, actual paid-overage invoicing/authorization and reset boundaries remain to be integrated. These issues remain In Progress; the helper alone is not race-safe enforcement.

### Confirmed allowance reset policy · 28 October 2026

User chose **workspace billing anniversaries** for paid monthly AI allowance resets, and the **workspace signup anniversary** for Free. Calendar-month/UTC-first-day resets must not be used as a substitute. Implementing period calculations and boundary fixtures; subscription anchors must come from trusted provider state and Free anchors from workspace creation, never the current actor's signup.

### Confirmed period, overage rate and BYOK policy · 28 October 2026

* Paid allowance resets use each workspace's billing anniversary; Free uses its workspace signup anniversary.
* Paid overage is charged at the underlying model/provider cost, with **no markup**. Existing opt-in and capped-authorization requirements still apply.
* **BYOK is excluded from Forge allowance and overage billing**; members pay their provider directly. Direct customer provider subscriptions are likewise excluded by the billing-mode contract.
* New runs persist the server-resolved billing mode; client usage events cannot choose their payer. Missing payer/pricing on historical rows requires reconciliation before invoicing.

Calendar-month environment caps are existing operational controls, distinct from the new commercial anniversary ledger. Seat-change proration is the next pending policy decision.

### Plan-aware allowance and admission preparation verified · 28 October 2026

Implemented locally (uncommitted/undeployed, base `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`): fixed Free US$5/workspace pool, paid per-member pool, explicit standard-plan validation, no usable Free overage even with stale paid opt-in/authorization, Free five-member capacity arithmetic with batch/overflow checks, and trusted plan/feature/payer usage classification. Paid Calls/Signals and BYOK bypass the allowance constraint and reserve **zero** customer allowance even when the agent pool is exhausted; independent operational admission still applies. Free Calls/Signals consume its fixed pool. Internal provider costs are not erased.

Verification: **9 billing test files / 155 tests passed**, app TypeScript, changed-file ESLint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Tests cover fixed Free pool through membership changes, stale paid overage refusal, fifth/sixth/batch membership boundaries, paid membership, unknown plan/feature/payer rejection, paid Calls/Signals after exhaustion and BYOK exclusion.

No live membership or commercial usage transaction is wired yet. <issue id="708503bd-17d3-4ba8-89a9-d0e38cdd86ae" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-153/enforce-the-free-workspace-member-limit-across-every-join-path">FOR-153</issue> owns atomic member admission; <issue id="e99eba3f-77ee-4e94-8927-69f1ddb44396" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-154/enforce-free-and-starter-team-capacity-across-creation-and-imports">FOR-154</issue> owns team capacity; <issue id="760e2e73-688b-42f0-a425-879963f74ff4" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-35/upload-files-directly-with-validated-upload-intents-and-finalize">FOR-35</issue>/<issue id="1b7d62ce-f7de-4a13-8400-3b4f6708ec59" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-41/create-canonical-issues-from-every-composer">FOR-41</issue>/<issue id="b19f24b0-4beb-409e-ae59-da8a5a137c46" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-45/delete-and-restore-issues-with-consistent-downstream-state">FOR-45</issue> were extended for upload and active-issue limits, reusing existing stories. <issue id="8fa7eb8a-25fc-47b5-8459-9bcd3d62ff2b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-76/atomically-admit-runs-and-reserve-provider-spend">FOR-76</issue> stays In Progress for locking, authoritative plan/period snapshots, reservation/settlement persistence and late-usage reconciliation. Source matrix: [https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b>)

### Final trial usage policy and local contract verification

User confirmed one fixed **US$5 workspace pool for the 14-day trial**, with **Calls and Signals metered against it**. Trial allowance does not scale with members, refill at a calendar-month boundary or permit overage. BYOK remains excluded. Budget/charge policy now requires a trusted `standard`/`trial` access phase and rejects missing/unknown classifications. A workspace-scoped trial-period helper preserves the original 14-day half-open window and refuses usage exactly at expiry; it does not start a new pool. Paid Calls/Signals exemptions apply only outside trial. Card-free trial start/expiry persistence and UI are not implemented by these helpers.

Focused billing verification: **9 files / 164 tests passed**; app TypeScript, billing ESLint, formatting and diff checks passed. Broader app run: 210 files / 1,241 tests passed, with one review-screen emoji-picker test failure currently being rechecked. No live billing/membership changes; uncommitted and undeployed.

### Current implementation checkpoint · 28 October 2026

The user confirmed trial eligibility **once per workspace**, across all creators/admins and both Starter/Plus. Persist one immutable workspace-scoped redemption; retries, switching trial tier, different admins and trial expiry cannot create another trial. Enforce uniqueness and start/usage-grant writes atomically, with no payment details or automatic conversion.

Current local verification: **211 app test files / 1,242 tests passed on rerun**, including **9 billing files / 164 tests**. TypeScript, billing ESLint, formatting and diff checks passed. The first full run had one review-screen emoji-picker failure; its isolated rerun and the second full run passed without modifying that screen. Source changes remain uncommitted and undeployed; no live trial, membership transaction or provider charge was changed.

Fixed Free/trial pools, no Free/trial overage, trusted plan/phase/feature/payer classification, trial-period bounds and hosted-trial suppression are prepared. Durable trial redemption/expiry, membership transactions, authoritative entitlement projection and live billing remain open; helper tests are not their completion evidence.

### Current concurrency policy — user revision, 28 October 2026

The user explicitly superseded the earlier 3/user, 20/workspace and 10/provider choice: **no Forge run-count concurrency cap per user, workspace or provider**, on any plan or trial. Removed the three policy fields, count-based admission branches, provider-count query and sample environment variables. Old FORGE_AGENT\_\*\_CONCURRENT_RUNS values are ignored rather than accidentally restoring caps on deployment. Spending allowances, explicit capped paid overage and execution/token bounds remain separate policies.

Regression evidence: the coordinator starts and completes 30 parallel fake-runtime runs for the same user/workspace/provider; admission accepts an active-run count of 1,000,000 with stale legacy cap settings. Exhausted spending budgets still reject. Focused agent verification: 5 files / 32 tests passed. No live model calls or deployment was performed. Atomic reservation/settlement remains required by <issue id="8fa7eb8a-25fc-47b5-8459-9bcd3d62ff2b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-76/atomically-admit-runs-and-reserve-provider-spend">FOR-76</issue>.

### Funded provider scope confirmed — 28 October 2026

The user selected **all supported providers** for Forge-funded usage from the included workspace allowance. The current built-in catalog includes OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, MiniMax, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek and Kimi. Keep provider-specific credentials, price/cost reconciliation and release verification mandatory for each enabled provider. BYOK and provider-paid subscriptions remain excluded from Forge allowance/overage under the earlier confirmed payer rule. This decision does not establish that each provider is already provisioned or production-verified.

**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_ADMISSION
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want atomic spending admission and reservations, so that simultaneous agent requests cannot overspend the shared workspace allowance or approved paid-overage cap.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Lock spending rows consistently; reserve funds and insert the run in one transaction; settle terminal runs idempotently. Forge imposes no per-user, per-workspace or per-provider run-count concurrency cap. Preserve original-period exposure for in-flight runs across the workspace billing anniversary.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §08; R4; E08. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (user-confirmed concurrency policy and implementation rule):** No Forge run-count concurrency caps. Cost reservations cover in-flight provider exposure atomically against the trusted workspace billing period, including runs crossing its renewal boundary. A new period cannot erase an earlier reservation or charge twice.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When two distinct starts compete for funds sufficient for only one proposed reservation, exactly one run and reservation commit; the loser leaves neither. Retry of the same command replays one durable result.
* **AC-02** — When a start occurs after the workspace billing anniversary, the earlier run retains its original reservation/settlement period. Active-run count does not reject the new run; spending admission uses the correct new period.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given the available spending pool can fund only one proposed reservation and two processes start distinct runs together.
* When admission executes.
* Then exactly one run is admitted and one reservation exists.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a reserved run began before the workspace billing anniversary.
* When another start occurs in the next workspace billing period.
* Then the old run retains its original spending reservation, the new run uses the new period, and neither is rejected solely by the number of active runs.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-75](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-75/define-provider-spending-and-execution-admission-policy>), [FOR-32](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-32/commit-commands-receipts-audit-and-outbox-events-atomically>).
Required before enabling this feature. A narrower release may defer it only by recording the scope decision and enforcing the feature gate.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. ### Included pool and overage contract implemented locally · 28 October 2026

The pure admission evaluator accounts for settled cost + outstanding reservations + proposed reservation; it denies exhaustion, over-cap exposure, malformed accounting and overflow. Membership changes alter available allowance without erasing settled consumption. No API charges or usage invoices are issued by this code.

Source matrix: [https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b>)

### Final trial usage policy and local contract verification

User confirmed one fixed **US$5 workspace pool for the 14-day trial**, with **Calls and Signals metered against it**. Trial allowance does not scale with members, refill at a calendar-month boundary or permit overage. BYOK remains excluded. Budget/charge policy now requires a trusted `standard`/`trial` access phase and rejects missing/unknown classifications. Paid Calls/Signals exemptions apply only outside trial. Card-free trial start/expiry persistence and UI are not implemented by these helpers.

Focused billing verification: **9 files / 164 tests passed**; app TypeScript, billing ESLint, formatting and diff checks passed. Broader app run: 210 files / 1,241 tests passed, with one review-screen emoji-picker test failure currently being rechecked. No live billing/membership changes; uncommitted and undeployed.

### Current implementation checkpoint · 28 October 2026

The user confirmed trial eligibility **once per workspace**, across all creators/admins and both Starter/Plus. Persist one immutable workspace-scoped redemption; retries, switching trial tier, different admins and trial expiry cannot create another trial. Enforce uniqueness and start/usage-grant writes atomically, with no payment details or automatic conversion.

Current local verification: **211 app test files / 1,242 tests passed on rerun**, including **9 billing files / 164 tests**. TypeScript, billing ESLint, formatting and diff checks passed. The first full run had one review-screen emoji-picker failure; its isolated rerun and the second full run passed without modifying that screen. Source changes remain uncommitted and undeployed; no live trial, membership transaction or provider charge was changed.

Fixed Free/trial pools, no Free/trial overage, trusted plan/phase/feature/payer classification, trial-period bounds and hosted-trial suppression are prepared. Durable trial redemption/expiry, membership transactions, authoritative entitlement projection and live billing remain open; helper tests are not their completion evidence.

### Current concurrency policy — user revision, 28 October 2026

The user explicitly superseded the earlier 3/user, 20/workspace and 10/provider choice: **no Forge run-count concurrency cap per user, workspace or provider**, on any plan or trial. Removed the three policy fields, count-based admission branches, provider-count query and sample environment variables. ### First paid-period accounting — user decision, 28 October 2026

A Free/trial workspace's first paid subscription period starts a fresh US$5-per-active-member pool; prior Free/trial consumption is not deducted. Preserve prior-period ledger rows and in-flight reservations, settle those against the original period, and key the new grant to the authoritative paid period so retry/replayed events cannot grant twice. Paid-tier switches do not constitute a new first-purchase grant.

The user confirmed billing-currency overage/caps, usage-time conversion and the latest published ECB daily reference with no spread. Included-pool/provider cost stays USD. Enabled caps now require an explicit currency matching the trusted subscription; settled/reserved overage balances are separate in billing currency. Disabled policies stay disabled; exhausted caps stay exhausted; no payment authority is minted.

Overall issue remains In Progress: this is pure prepared arithmetic; atomic quota/run reservation, policy/quote/shadow persistence with paid binding, settlement/recovery and actual provider invoice flows are still required.

Listed Starter EUR/USD 10 and Plus EUR/USD 16 per member are before tax; add applicable tax at checkout. The checkout adapter now fetches the approved monthly product and validates its one active flat seat-based catalog price, explicit exclusive tax behavior, exact currency/per-seat price and uncapped tier. It refuses inherited/inclusive/location tax settings, ambiguous prices, archived/nonmonthly/capped products, then rechecks trusted workspace/country/member context. Discount codes/provider trials are disabled and no ad-hoc price override is sent. The replacement verifier requires resolved exclusive tax with matching net/tax/total proof. The pinned CheckoutCreate has no tax-behavior override; catalog preflight enforces the rule.

Current checks: **1,553 app + 4 workflow tests; 62 PostgreSQL billing + 17 real-auth member cases; 3 full-history migration fault cases; 36 isolated migrations**, typecheck, scoped lint/format/diff and production build including protected Workflow handlers pass. Actual Polar sandbox credentials are missing; a secure local sandbox configuration request is pending. No provider catalog/checkout/setting was changed, no billing/public action enabled and no serving-data migration/deployment occurred. Overall issue remains In Progress.

These contracts still require atomic membership admission and reservation/settlement integration; helper tests alone will not close <issue id="8fa7eb8a-25fc-47b5-8459-9bcd3d62ff2b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-76/atomically-admit-runs-and-reserve-provider-spend">FOR-76</issue>.

### Plan-aware allowance and admission preparation verified · 28 October 2026

Implemented locally (uncommitted/undeployed, base `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`): fixed Free US$5/workspace pool, paid per-member pool, explicit standard-plan validation, no usable Free overage even with stale paid opt-in/authorization, Free five-member capacity arithmetic with batch/overflow checks, and trusted plan/feature/payer usage classification. Paid Calls/Signals and BYOK bypass the allowance constraint and reserve **zero** customer allowance even when the agent pool is exhausted; independent operational admission still applies. Free Calls/Signals consume its fixed pool. Internal provider costs are not erased.

Verification: **9 billing test files / 155 tests passed**, app TypeScript, changed-file ESLint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Tests cover fixed Free pool through membership changes, stale paid overage refusal, fifth/sixth/batch membership boundaries, paid membership, unknown plan/feature/payer rejection, paid Calls/Signals after exhaustion and BYOK exclusion.

No live membership or commercial usage transaction is wired yet. <issue id="708503bd-17d3-4ba8-89a9-d0e38cdd86ae" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-153/enforce-the-free-workspace-member-limit-across-every-join-path">FOR-153</issue> owns atomic member admission; <issue id="e99eba3f-77ee-4e94-8927-69f1ddb44396" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-154/enforce-free-and-starter-team-capacity-across-creation-and-imports">FOR-154</issue> owns team capacity; <issue id="760e2e73-688b-42f0-a425-879963f74ff4" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-35/upload-files-directly-with-validated-upload-intents-and-finalize">FOR-35</issue>/<issue id="1b7d62ce-f7de-4a13-8400-3b4f6708ec59" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-41/create-canonical-issues-from-every-composer">FOR-41</issue>/<issue id="b19f24b0-4beb-409e-ae59-da8a5a137c46" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-45/delete-and-restore-issues-with-consistent-downstream-state">FOR-45</issue> were extended for upload and active-issue limits, reusing existing stories. <issue id="8fa7eb8a-25fc-47b5-8459-9bcd3d62ff2b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-76/atomically-admit-runs-and-reserve-provider-spend">FOR-76</issue> stays In Progress for locking, authoritative plan/period snapshots, reservation/settlement persistence and late-usage reconciliation. Source matrix: [https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b>)

### Final trial usage policy and local contract verification

User confirmed one fixed **US$5 workspace pool for the 14-day trial**, with **Calls and Signals metered against it**. Trial allowance does not scale with members, refill at a calendar-month boundary or permit overage. BYOK remains excluded. Budget/charge policy now requires a trusted `standard`/`trial` access phase and rejects missing/unknown classifications. A workspace-scoped trial-period helper preserves the original 14-day half-open window and refuses usage exactly at expiry; it does not start a new pool. Paid Calls/Signals exemptions apply only outside trial. Card-free trial start/expiry persistence and UI are not implemented by these helpers.

Focused billing verification: **9 files / 164 tests passed**; app TypeScript, billing ESLint, formatting and diff checks passed. Broader app run: 210 files / 1,241 tests passed, with one review-screen emoji-picker test failure currently being rechecked. No live billing/membership changes; uncommitted and undeployed.

### Current implementation checkpoint · 28 October 2026

The user confirmed trial eligibility **once per workspace**, across all creators/admins and both Starter/Plus. Persist one immutable workspace-scoped redemption; retries, switching trial tier, different admins and trial expiry cannot create another trial. Enforce uniqueness and start/usage-grant writes atomically, with no payment details or automatic conversion.

Current local verification: **211 app test files / 1,242 tests passed on rerun**, including **9 billing files / 164 tests**. TypeScript, billing ESLint, formatting and diff checks passed. The first full run had one review-screen emoji-picker failure; its isolated rerun and the second full run passed without modifying that screen. Source changes remain uncommitted and undeployed; no live trial, membership transaction or provider charge was changed.

Fixed Free/trial pools, no Free/trial overage, trusted plan/phase/feature/payer classification, trial-period bounds and hosted-trial suppression are prepared. Durable trial redemption/expiry, membership transactions, authoritative entitlement projection and live billing remain open; helper tests are not their completion evidence.

### Current concurrency policy — user revision, 28 October 2026

The user explicitly superseded the earlier 3/user, 20/workspace and 10/provider choice: **no Forge run-count concurrency cap per user, workspace or provider**, on any plan or trial. Removed the three policy fields, count-based admission branches, provider-count query and sample environment variables. Old FORGE_AGENT\_\*\_CONCURRENT_RUNS values are ignored rather than accidentally restoring caps on deployment. Spending allowances, explicit capped paid overage and execution/token bounds remain separate policies.

Regression evidence: the coordinator starts and completes 30 parallel fake-runtime runs for the same user/workspace/provider; admission accepts an active-run count of 1,000,000 with stale legacy cap settings. Exhausted spending budgets still reject. Focused agent verification: 5 files / 32 tests passed. No live model calls or deployment was performed. Atomic reservation/settlement remains required by <issue id="8fa7eb8a-25fc-47b5-8459-9bcd3d62ff2b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-76/atomically-admit-runs-and-reserve-provider-spend">FOR-76</issue>.

### First paid-period accounting — user decision, 28 October 2026

A Free/trial workspace's first paid subscription period starts a fresh US$5-per-active-member pool; prior Free/trial consumption is not deducted. Preserve prior-period ledger rows and in-flight reservations, settle those against the original period, and key the new grant to the authoritative paid period so retry/replayed events cannot grant twice. Paid-tier switches do not constitute a new first-purchase grant.

### Currency-safe overage prerequisites — implemented · 29 October 2026

The user confirmed billing-currency overage/caps, usage-time conversion and the latest published ECB daily reference with no spread. Included-pool/provider cost stays USD. Enabled caps now require an explicit currency matching the trusted subscription; settled/reserved overage balances are separate in billing currency. EUR caps are never summed with USD allowance or compared with USD spend. Only incremental cost beyond the pool is converted. Preserve opt-in/payment authority, Free/trial prohibition, BYOK and paid Calls/Signals exclusions.

Prepared helpers retain source/rate/time/quote ID and exact rational amounts; bigint intermediates avoid precision overflow. Reservations round up at micro-unit precision, settlement half-up; invoice writer must aggregate and apply final minor-unit rounding once. Missing/unavailable/future/stale EUR rates fail closed. The bounded fixed-origin ECB reader sends no credentials/customer data and was verified read-only against the live source. [Implementation and delivery limits](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-paid-ai-overage-currency-and-usage-time-ecb-conversion-408511e4f5c1>).

Verified: **1,451 app + 4 workflow tests**, typecheck, changed-file ESLint/Prettier, diff and production build including protected Workflow handlers. Twenty-three new cases cover USD/EUR units, inverse rate, exact cap with settled/reserved EUR spend, frozen replay, rounding/overflow, exclusions and bounded/invalid source data. No schema migration, model call, live payment/invoice/provider setting, push or deployment.

This completes the prepared currency/arithmetic slice. <issue id="8fa7eb8a-25fc-47b5-8459-9bcd3d62ff2b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-76/atomically-admit-runs-and-reserve-provider-spend">FOR-76</issue> remains In Progress: authoritative plan/period/payer/rate snapshots, dual-currency balances, admission and reservation/run persistence still need one atomic ledger transaction, idempotent settlement/recovery and actual provider/invoice evidence. Pure helper tests do not prove that contract. Existing isolated database baseline remains commit 1ba1ff8 (34 migrations, billing 52, real-auth membership 17, migration faults 3), not rerun for this pure-helper change.

### Currency-cutover cap and committed capacity — confirmed prepared arithmetic · 29 October 2026

The user selected automatic conversion of an existing opted-in cap at the latest published ECB reference rate. Freeze the rate when verified paid currency cutover commits; a late checkout retains the original commercial period. planOverageCurrencyCutover converts USD→EUR by division and EUR→USD by multiplication using bigint fractions. Round cap down and carried settled/reserved capacity up to a currency millionth, retaining exact fractions and quote. Disabled policies stay disabled; exhausted caps stay exhausted; no payment authority is minted.

Carry prior spending/reservations as target-currency **capacity shadows**, preserving original charges, usage-time quotes, invoice currency and settlement identity. This prevents late checkout/currency changes from restoring spent capacity or charging it twice. Replay must reuse the transition quote under the ledger lock; late old-currency settlements adjust the retained shadow with that quote.

**Prepared checks passing:** 18 new cutover cases cover both directions, prior commitments, conservative rounding, disabled/zero/exhausted policies, frozen repeatability, unavailable/malformed/stale/future rates, source mismatch, period boundaries and overflow. Verified checkpoint: **1,541 app + 4 workflow tests; 62 isolated PostgreSQL billing + 17 real-auth membership cases; 3 full-history migration ownership/fault cases**. Migration 0035 was rehearsed through all 36 migrations before the one pending expansion was applied to exact isolated staging. Typecheck and scoped lint/format pass; final build verification is being recorded in the linked guide/checkpoint. No live provider effect, public billing enablement or serving-data migration.

[Money and persistence boundaries](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-paid-ai-overage-currency-and-usage-time-ecb-conversion-408511e4f5c1>). Overall issue remains In Progress: this is pure prepared arithmetic; atomic quota/run reservation, policy/quote/shadow persistence with paid binding, settlement/recovery and actual provider invoice flows are still required.

### Before-tax checkout policy confirmed and prepared — 29 October 2026

Listed Starter EUR/USD 10 and Plus EUR/USD 16 per member are before tax; add applicable tax at checkout. The checkout adapter now fetches the approved monthly product and validates its one active flat seat-based catalog price, explicit exclusive tax behavior, exact currency/per-seat price and uncapped tier. It refuses inherited/inclusive/location tax settings, ambiguous prices, archived/nonmonthly/capped products, then rechecks trusted workspace/country/member context. Discount codes/provider trials are disabled and no ad-hoc price override is sent. The replacement verifier requires resolved exclusive tax with matching net/tax/total proof. The pinned CheckoutCreate has no tax-behavior override; catalog preflight enforces the rule.

Current checks: **1,553 app + 4 workflow tests; 62 PostgreSQL billing + 17 real-auth member cases; 3 full-history migration fault cases; 36 isolated migrations**, typecheck, scoped lint/format/diff and production build including protected Workflow handlers pass. Actual Polar sandbox credentials are missing; a secure local sandbox configuration request is pending. No provider catalog/checkout/setting was changed, no billing/public action enabled and no serving-data migration/deployment occurred. Overall issue remains In Progress.

issues.title: Keep one run execution alive across stream reconnects and redeploys
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_RECOVERY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an agent user, I want interrupted conversations to resume, so that closing a tab does not duplicate work or lose progress.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Separate durable execution from SSE delivery; persist runtime ownership/cursor, heartbeat lease and takeover protocol; verify deployed function duration and backend capabilities.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §08; R6; E09. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A browser reconnect attaches to the existing run and never silently starts a second writer.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the tab disconnects and the application redeploys, reconnection resumes the same execution with no duplicated tool effect.
* **AC-02** — When another worker takes over, the old owner is fenced and one valid executor remains.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an active run has persisted events.
* When the tab disconnects and the application redeploys.
* Then reconnection resumes the same execution with no duplicated tool effect.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the execution lease expires.
* When another worker takes over.
* Then the old owner is fenced and one valid executor remains.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-76](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-76/atomically-admit-runs-and-reserve-provider-spend>), [FOR-64](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-64/run-leased-resumable-background-jobs-with-operator-recovery>).
Required before enabling this feature. A narrower release may defer it only by recording the scope decision and enforcing the feature gate.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Cancel and time-bound runs with reliable quota settlement
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_CANCEL
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an agent user, I want cancellation to stop further work, so that I retain control over execution and spend.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist cancellation and deadlines; propagate to provider/sandbox/tools; define approval-wait behavior; reconcile late usage and release reservations once.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §08; R4, R6. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Cancellation forbids new material effects after the defined boundary; uncertain effects remain reconciled, not hidden.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the user cancels, the run reaches a terminal state and no new tool write starts.
* **AC-02** — When accounting reconciles, actual usage is recorded and the reservation is released once.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a run is streaming or waiting for approval.
* When the user cancels.
* Then the run reaches a terminal state and no new tool write starts.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given provider usage arrives after cancellation or settlement retries.
* When accounting reconciles.
* Then actual usage is recorded and the reservation is released once.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-77](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-77/keep-one-run-execution-alive-across-stream-reconnects-and-redeploys>).

issues.title: Replay agent events and history with bounded stable cursors
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_REPLAY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an agent user, I want long conversations to reopen reliably, so that history does not become slow or skip events.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Add page limits/indexes, source-event deduplication, stable thread-wide cursor semantics and contention benchmarks for sequence allocation.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §08; R6, R12; E09. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A per-run sequence is not a globally unique thread cursor.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the client paginates then reconnects, every event is delivered in stable order without gaps or duplicate rendering.
* **AC-02** — When events are persisted, source identities deduplicate and bounded retry failures are observable.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a thread has multiple runs and more than one event page.
* When the client paginates then reconnects.
* Then every event is delivered in stable order without gaps or duplicate rendering.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given two writers contend to append.
* When events are persisted.
* Then source identities deduplicate and bounded retry failures are observable.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Execute approved agent writes with crash-safe command receipts
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_APPROVAL
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an agent user, I want approval bound to the exact proposed change, so that retries cannot alter or repeat my authorization.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Bind actor/workspace/run/capability version/input hash/expiry; atomic consume+command where possible or recoverable claimed state; recheck membership at execution.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §07, §11; R3; E07. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Expired or changed-input approval is invalid; ambiguous effects need reconciliation before retry.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the invocation retries, the original result returns without another mutation or new approval consumption.
* **AC-02** — When the approved tool executes, execution is denied and the reason is shown.
* **AC-03** — Given execution crashes immediately after approval consumption or after a provider accepts an effect, when the same invocation resumes, then a durable execution identity reconciles the known/uncertain outcome without silently releasing approval or blindly repeating the effect.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an exact-input write is approved and its response is lost after commit.
* When the invocation retries.
* Then the original result returns without another mutation or new approval consumption.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the input changes or membership is revoked.
* When the approved tool executes.
* Then execution is denied and the reason is shown.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given execution crashes immediately after approval consumption or after a provider accepts an effect.
* When the same invocation resumes.
* Then a durable execution identity reconciles the known/uncertain outcome without silently releasing approval or blindly repeating the effect.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>), [FOR-77](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-77/keep-one-run-execution-alive-across-stream-reconnects-and-redeploys>).

Required before enabling this slice. Conditional extensions are governed by the accepted release manifest and their stated evidence checks; an excluded feature stays unavailable and is not marked implemented.

Blocking links describe prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation, contract design and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently where interfaces are agreed. Related links are coordination or conditional enablement work, not automatic blockers.

**Completion evidence:** every AC has a corresponding AT specification above. Attach results for the named commit/environment and relevant artifact. Resolve open policy choices before coding them; no passing test, estimate, owner assignment or delivery date is implied.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §07, §11; R3; E07. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Expired or changed-input approval is invalid; ambiguous effects need reconciliation before retry.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the invocation retries, the original result returns without another mutation or new approval consumption.

* When the invocation retries.
* Then the original result returns without another mutation or new approval consumption.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the input changes or membership is revoked.
* When the approved tool executes.
* Then execution is denied and the reason is shown.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given execution crashes immediately after approval consumption or after a provider accepts an effect.
* When the same invocation resumes.
* Then a durable execution identity reconciles the known/uncertain outcome without silently releasing approval or blindly repeating the effect.

**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_TOOLS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want Forge to work on real shared objects, so that agent assistance can advance my team's work.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Add typed issue search/get/create/update/comment and project tools over shared services; bounded outputs, exact-input previews and canonical deep links; update instructions.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §11; E07, E18. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Retrieved text cannot grant permissions or change approval policy; tools do not write localStorage.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When they approve the exact preview, one shared issue is created with an attributable event and canonical link.
* **AC-02** — When the tool chain follows that text, authorization denies access and no hidden data is emitted.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an authorized user asks Forge to create an issue.
* When they approve the exact preview.
* Then one shared issue is created with an attributable event and canonical link.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an issue body instructs the agent to read another workspace.
* When the tool chain follows that text.
* Then authorization denies access and no hidden data is emitted.

issues.title: Let Forge use authorized cycles and inbox context
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_DOMAIN_READS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a user, I want Forge to read my cycles and inbox context, so that it can help me prioritize current work.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Add bounded typed read capabilities for enabled cycles and the actor's inbox. Preserve per-resource access, canonical source links and freshness. Document reading is owned by [FOR-151](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-151/let-forge-read-authorized-documents-with-source-references>) and Calls recaps by [FOR-152](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-152/let-forge-read-authorized-call-recaps-with-provenance>), with independent enablement. Read context never changes state or grants write authority.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §11; E07, E12. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A summary or search index must not broaden access beyond the original object.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given authorized cycle and personal inbox fixtures with documents/Calls disabled, when Forge answers a planning question, then it uses only bounded accessible planning/inbox context with canonical source references.
* **AC-02** — Given a private cycle or another user's inbox entry, when the same retrieval is attempted, then that source is denied without exposing protected metadata.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given authorized cycle and personal inbox fixtures with documents/Calls disabled.
* When Forge answers a planning question.
* Then it uses only bounded accessible planning/inbox context with canonical source references.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a private cycle or another user's inbox entry.
* When the same retrieval is attempted.
* Then that source is denied without exposing protected metadata.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-81](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-81/let-forge-search-create-and-update-shared-issues-and-projects>), [FOR-55](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-55/plan-shared-current-and-upcoming-cycles>), [FOR-65](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-65/deliver-authorized-issue-events-into-a-shared-inbox>).

issues.title: Use durable attachments and artifacts throughout an agent run
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_FILES
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an agent user, I want run files available after reconnect, so that I can continue work and retrieve its output.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Switch both attachment resolution and artifact output to shared storage; bound model-context transfer and downstream payloads; user-visible failed upload/output states.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §09; R5; E10. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A durable browser upload does not remove provider request/context limits.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When it reconnects on another instance, both remain authorized and checksum-valid.
* **AC-02** — When the run resolves it, a bounded actionable error occurs without leaking credentials or hanging.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a run receives a ready attachment and creates an artifact.
* When it reconnects on another instance.
* Then both remain authorized and checksum-valid.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a file is oversized for the chosen provider or was deleted.
* When the run resolves it.
* Then a bounded actionable error occurs without leaking credentials or hanging.

issues.title: Apply versioned personal guidance and team skills to runs
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-SKILLS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want my selected guidance applied consistently, so that Forge follows the right team conventions across devices.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist actor/workspace/team-scoped instructions; authorized publication, size limits and explicit applicable selection; snapshot revisions in run context; wire beyond UI flag.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §12; R14; E14. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Skill text is lower-trust than system and authorization policy and cannot grant a tool permission.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When a run starts then the skill changes, the run records and uses its selected revision while later runs use the new one.
* **AC-02** — When the agent follows its guidance, the tool boundary denies it and skill text is not copied into general diagnostics.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an authorized team skill revision is selected.
* When a run starts then the skill changes.
* Then the run records and uses its selected revision while later runs use the new one.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a skill requests another workspace's data.
* When the agent follows its guidance.
* Then the tool boundary denies it and skill text is not copied into general diagnostics.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.description:
**Type:** Release gate · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_LIVE_GATE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a release owner, I want live agent evidence, so that fixture success is not mistaken for production readiness.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Run capped tests with test credentials against chosen provider/runtime/sandbox; deny-all egress, no credential injection, prompt-injection and unauthorized-write evals; confirm runtime build/provenance.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §08, §11, §13; R12; E17-E18. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Each enabled provider/execution mode needs evidence; optional domain tools need their own prerequisites first.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When release evals exercise read, approved write, cancel and reconnect, evidence ties passing outcomes and bounded spend to the candidate.
* **AC-02** — When the gate is evaluated, that execution mode is disabled or release is blocked.
* **AC-03** — Given the release manifest selects a subset of skills, planning, document, Calls or outbound-connector tools, when candidate tool discovery and execution are checked, then each enabled extension has its matching implementation evidence; omitted extensions are unavailable, and the base agent does not require every optional domain.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given the candidate deployment and enabled model/sandbox matrix.
* When release evals exercise read, approved write, cancel and reconnect.
* Then evidence ties passing outcomes and bounded spend to the candidate.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the sandbox can access forbidden egress or an enabled provider fails.
* When the gate is evaluated.
* Then that execution mode is disabled or release is blocked.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given the release manifest selects a subset of skills, planning, document, Calls or outbound-connector tools.
* When candidate tool discovery and execution are checked.
* Then each enabled extension has its matching implementation evidence; omitted extensions are unavailable, and the base agent does not require every optional domain.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-API_SCOPES
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an integration owner, I want narrowly scoped API credentials, so that automations receive only the access they need.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Extend API scopes beyond teams; validate current membership and credential revocation; separate session/API actors, CORS and public enablement flag.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §11; R1, R9; E04. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A scope permits an operation only within current resource access; API keys never become browser sessions.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When it reads an allowed issue then attempts creation, read succeeds and write is denied.
* **AC-02** — When the next API request is made, access is denied without waiting for a stale client cache.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a credential has issues:read only.
* When it reads an allowed issue then attempts creation.
* Then read succeeds and write is denied.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the user is removed or the key revoked.
* When the next API request is made.
* Then access is denied without waiting for a stale client cache.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>), [FOR-26](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-26/validate-service-specific-production-configuration-at-startup>).
Required before enabling this feature. A narrower release may defer it only by recording the scope decision and enforcing the feature gate.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-API_ISSUES
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an integration developer, I want a predictable issue API, so that my tools can create and maintain shared work.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Add oRPC/OpenAPI issue list/search/get/create/update/comment contracts, stable pagination, validation/typed errors, expectedVersion and documented idempotency.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §11; E04, E06. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** UI and API call the same commands and return consistent access/conflict outcomes.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When it creates, reads, comments and edits an issue, all operations target one canonical issue and documented response shapes.
* **AC-02** — When the API processes it, typed errors or the original result are returned without duplicate work.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an authorized client follows the published contract.
* When it creates, reads, comments and edits an issue.
* Then all operations target one canonical issue and documented response shapes.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a stale version, invalid cursor or replayed command is sent.
* When the API processes it.
* Then typed errors or the original result are returned without duplicate work.

issues.title: Expose basic projects, cycles and labels through the API
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-API_PLANNING
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an API client developer, I want basic projects, cycles and labels through shared contracts, so that I can organize canonical issues from my integration.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Publish bounded contracts/scopes for basic project metadata, cycle membership and labels using the corresponding shared services. Apply current visibility, expected-version and error rules. Advanced milestones/updates and initiatives belong to [FOR-150](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-150/expose-enabled-initiative-and-advanced-project-metadata-through-the>) and are not silently exposed by this slice.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §11; §03 areas 7-10. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** API enablement must not expose a domain whose implementation/release gate is incomplete.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given basic planning enabled with a scoped client, when it reads/updates allowed projects, cycles and labels, then canonical IDs and validation/conflict behavior match the UI.
* **AC-02** — Given a private project or disabled advanced planning endpoint, when the client requests records or aggregates, then hidden identifiers/counts do not leak and advanced scope remains unavailable.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given basic planning enabled with a scoped client.
* When it reads/updates allowed projects, cycles and labels.
* Then canonical IDs and validation/conflict behavior match the UI.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

issues.title: Deliver signed and replayable outbound webhooks
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-WEBHOOKS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an integration developer, I want verifiable change events, so that my systems can synchronize reliably.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Version events, stable IDs, signing timestamp/rotation, bounded retries and redelivery; safe destination validation against redirects/private addresses; minimize payload.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §11; R3, R8. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Events are at least once and consumers deduplicate; webhook URLs cannot be used for internal network access.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When delivery retries and the signing key rotates, the receiver can verify signatures and deduplicate the stable event ID.
* **AC-02** — When registration/delivery is attempted, it is rejected and no internal request is sent.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a subscribed issue event and a valid public receiver.
* When delivery retries and the signing key rotates.
* Then the receiver can verify signatures and deduplicate the stable event ID.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a URL resolves or redirects to a private address.
* When registration/delivery is attempted.
* Then it is rejected and no internal request is sent.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-86](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-86/authorize-public-api-access-with-explicit-resource-scopes>), [FOR-33](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-33/deliver-external-effects-with-recoverable-outbox-processing>).

**Type:** Product decision · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-MCP_POLICY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want explicit MCP delegation rules, so that external agents cannot inherit unintended authority.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Pin protocol/transport and supported clients; choose OAuth/resource discovery and optional manual-key mode; decide delegated writes versus pending-action approvals; separate outbound connectors.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §11; R11; W2. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Tool annotations and another client's confirmation are not Forge authorization by themselves.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the policy is approved, token audience, scopes, revocation and write approval interaction are specified.
* **AC-02** — When it requests an approved write, the design uses a new explicit execution identity rather than forging an internal run.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given read and write MCP use cases for supported clients.
* When the policy is approved.
* Then token audience, scopes, revocation and write approval interaction are specified.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a client has no Forge run identity.
* When it requests an approved write.
* Then the design uses a new explicit execution identity rather than forging an internal run.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-20](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates>).
Required before enabling this feature. A narrower release may defer it only by recording the scope decision and enforcing the feature gate.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-MCP_READ
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a user of an external assistant, I want authorized Forge search and reads, so that I can use team context in my chosen client.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Implement the selected MCP transport, resource/auth metadata, audience/scopes and per-request authorization; use [FOR-43](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-43/find-and-filter-shared-issues-with-bounded-server-queries>) and canonical reads directly with bounded typed outputs. Reuse credential/resource-scope policy from [FOR-86](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-86/authorize-public-api-access-with-explicit-resource-scopes>) without requiring the public issue mutation endpoints or agent runtime. Verify supported-client compatibility, reconnects and disabled-surface behavior.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §11; R11; W2. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Tokens intended for another resource are rejected; API-key mode is not claimed as universal OAuth compatibility.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When it searches and fetches a permitted issue, the negotiated protocol returns bounded canonical results.
* **AC-02** — When a tool request arrives, authentication fails and no issue data is returned.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a supported client authorizes issues:read.
* When it searches and fetches a permitted issue.
* Then the negotiated protocol returns bounded canonical results.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an expired, wrong-audience or revoked token is used.
* When a tool request arrives.
* Then authentication fails and no issue data is returned.

## Dependencies and completion
