issues.title: Execute MCP writes through explicit delegation or pending approvals
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-MCP_WRITE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace member, I want controlled MCP changes, so that external assistants can act without bypassing Forge's policy.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Implement the authorization exchange accepted in [FOR-91](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-91/choose-external-mcp-transport-client-support-and-write-authority>): narrowly scoped delegation or an explicit pending-action approval. Bind actor, workspace, operation/version, exact input hash, expiry and independent execution identity. Invoke the canonical issue mutation/receipt/audit services exposed by [FOR-87](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-87/expose-issue-search-reads-and-mutations-through-versioned-contracts>). Reuse approval primitives conceptually with [FOR-80](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-80/execute-approved-agent-writes-with-crash-safe-command-receipts>) but never require or fabricate its internal run ID. Recheck current access on execution; reconcile ambiguous outcomes before retry.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §11; R3, R11. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A read-only or mismatched approval token cannot authorize a material write.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the required exact-input authorization is completed, one canonical mutation commits with client/user attribution.
* **AC-02** — When execution is attempted, invalid authority is denied and a valid retry returns the original result.
* **AC-03** — Given the internal agent runtime is disabled but the accepted external write mode is configured, when a supported client submits and authorizes an issue mutation, then one attributable command completes using external execution identity and changed/expired authority is denied without starting a model run.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a supported external client proposes a scoped issue change.
* When the required exact-input authorization is completed.
* Then one canonical mutation commits with client/user attribution.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given input changes, membership is revoked or the response is retried.
* When execution is attempted.
* Then invalid authority is denied and a valid retry returns the original result.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given the internal agent runtime is disabled but the accepted external write mode is configured.
* When a supported client submits and authorizes an issue mutation.
* Then one attributable command completes using external execution identity and changed/expired authority is denied without starting a model run.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-92](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-92/provide-interoperable-read-only-forge-mcp-access>), [FOR-87](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-87/expose-issue-search-reads-and-mutations-through-versioned-contracts>).

issues.title: Connect external MCP tools to Forge with explicit trust controls
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Later expansion · **Backlog key:** FPR-MCP_CONNECTORS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace admin, I want reviewed external tool connections, so that Forge can use approved systems without exposing credentials.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Define connection ownership, isolated credentials, destination validation, discovery/version drift, permission prompts, allowlists and disable controls. Attach permitted bounded read tools to the run context without requiring team skills. Remote descriptions/results remain untrusted. Material writes stay unavailable until the accepted approval policy and [FOR-80](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-80/execute-approved-agent-writes-with-crash-safe-command-receipts>) evidence exist for that execution mode; this read-first connector scope does not silently authorize writes.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §11; optional outbound connector scope. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Remote tool descriptions and results are untrusted and cannot expand Forge's permissions.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When Forge discovers and invokes a permitted read tool, credentials remain server-side and the operation is attributed.
* **AC-02** — When the connector refreshes, unsafe destination is blocked and new authority requires explicit review.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an admin configures an approved endpoint.
* When Forge discovers and invokes a permitted read tool.
* Then credentials remain server-side and the operation is attributed.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the endpoint redirects privately or adds a material write tool.
* When the connector refreshes.
* Then unsafe destination is blocked and new authority requires explicit review.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-SYNC
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a teammate, I want committed changes to appear in open views, so that I do not work from stale state.

issues.title: Recover password access with single-use verified reset flows
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-AUTH_RECOVERY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an account holder, I want to recover access safely, so that a forgotten password does not permanently lock me out.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Implement request/reset mail, generic response, single-use expiry, password change, session policy and completion notice through the existing account-auth service. Define verification policy before enablement. Workspace/team authorization and the canonical issue schema are not prerequisites for this account-level flow.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §12; R9; E13. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Reset responses must not reveal account existence; reset secrets cannot be logged.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the holder changes their password, new sign-in succeeds and sessions follow the recorded policy.
* **AC-02** — When reset is attempted, a safe generic response appears and no account change occurs.
* **AC-03** — Given mail delivery fails or a reset request is retried, when the user requests recovery, then the response remains enumeration-safe, delivery failures are observable and the chosen retry path cannot issue an already-consumed reset token.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a registered test account and valid reset link.
* When the holder changes their password.
* Then new sign-in succeeds and sessions follow the recorded policy.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the link is reused/expired or the email is unknown.
* When reset is attempted.
* Then a safe generic response appears and no account change occurs.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given mail delivery fails or a reset request is retried.
* When the user requests recovery.
* Then the response remains enumeration-safe, delivery failures are observable and the chosen retry path cannot issue an already-consumed reset token.

## Dependencies and completion

Required for core production.

issues.title: Verify signup, email change, account linking and workspace invitations
issues.description:
**Type:** Release gate · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-AUTH_LIFECYCLE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a new teammate, I want reliable onboarding and invitations, so that I enter the correct workspace with the intended role.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Decide verified-email sign-in policy; test the existing configured mail sender with failure/retry evidence independently of the issue-domain job runner, invitation workflow, role claims, expiry/replay, email change and explicit linking in staging and deployed candidate.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 areas 1-2, §12; E13. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Invitations cannot be replayed to gain a different role/workspace; account linking requires explicit authority.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When signup/verification and acceptance complete, the intended membership and role persist after reload.
* **AC-02** — When acceptance or linking is attempted, access is denied without altering another account.
* **AC-03** — Given a fresh authenticated account has no workspace and then retries interrupted setup, when it creates a workspace and first team or joins an allowed invitation/domain, then one authorized membership/bootstrap result remains, reload reaches the real workspace empty state, and failure cannot strand an orphaned setup or grant an extra role.
* **AC-04** — Given email change or account linking targets another identity, when the flow is attempted with missing, expired or replayed ownership proof, then only the explicitly verified owner can complete it and sessions follow the recorded security policy.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a fresh test user receives a valid workspace invite.
* When signup/verification and acceptance complete.
* Then the intended membership and role persist after reload.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an invite is expired/reused or email/account ownership does not match.
* When acceptance or linking is attempted.
* Then access is denied without altering another account.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given a fresh authenticated account has no workspace and then retries interrupted setup.
* When it creates a workspace and first team or joins an allowed invitation/domain.
* Then one authorized membership/bootstrap result remains, reload reaches the real workspace empty state, and failure cannot strand an orphaned setup or grant an extra role.

**AT-04 → AC-04**

* Given email change or account linking targets another identity.
* When the flow is attempted with missing, expired or replayed ownership proof.
* Then only the explicitly verified owner can complete it and sessions follow the recorded security policy.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-96](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-96/recover-password-access-with-single-use-verified-reset-flows>).

Required for core production.

Blocking links describe prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation, contract design and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently where interfaces are agreed. Related links are coordination or conditional enablement work, not automatic blockers.

**Completion evidence:** every AC has a corresponding AT specification above. Attach results for the named commit/environment and relevant artifact. Resolve open policy choices before coding them; no passing test, estimate, owner assignment or delivery date is implied.

## Confirmed policy and implementation start · 28 October 2026

User requires verified email before workspace creation or Forge agent use for the public web/agent/macOS release. Implementing this enforcement slice now. The full release gate stays open until recovery, invitation/linking and deployed end-to-end evidence also pass.

## Verification-policy implementation evidence · 28 October 2026

Completed the local enforcement slice in the working tree based on `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`; uncommitted and undeployed.

* Password signup sends verification mail; unverified password sign-in is denied by the installed Better Auth configuration.
* Workspace creation uses the organization plugin's server-side verified-user policy. A test through the actual auth HTTP handler proves that an old unverified session, even with a supplied owner ID, gets 403 before any organization insert.
* Invitation acceptance explicitly requires verified email. Protected membership/session boundaries fail closed for unverified users, so old sessions cannot reach agent actions. Agent endpoints return `403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` before executing domain operations.
* Signup displays a verification notice when no session is issued. Explicit resend handles failure/retry and retains desktop authorization parameters in its login callback. Unverified sign-in exposes the same resend path.
* Focused auth/client/agent/mail/UI suite: **9 files / 49 tests passed**.
* Full default app Vitest suite: **200 files / 1,073 tests passed**. App TypeScript check passed. ESLint on changed auth files passed with two pre-existing `require-await` warnings in the agent transport test fixture; no lint errors. `git diff --check` passed.
* Implementation guide: `docs/email-verification-policy.md`.

**Remaining for this release gate:** deployed verification/resend/mail delivery, email-change and account-linking ownership flows, complete invitation/bootstrap/recovery behavior, and packaged macOS authorization checks. <issue id="0de68eed-860c-4aec-8c56-e69b7ba70627" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-97/verify-signup-email-change-account-linking-and-workspace-invitations">FOR-97</issue> remains In Progress; the local enforcement slice is not production certification.

issues.title: Revoke member access across sessions, files, keys and active runs
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-REVOCATION
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace admin, I want removal and role changes to take effect consistently, so that former access cannot linger in other surfaces.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Exercise old tabs, queued jobs, keys, file grants and agent approvals/runs when enabled; define short-lived URL revocation window and cancellation behavior.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §12; R1, R9. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Revocation is checked at execution and grant time; any accepted delay is documented.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When an admin removes Bob, new reads/writes and queued effects are denied and cached protected content is cleared.
* **AC-02** — When revocation occurs, the accepted URL window and run cancellation policy are enforced and tested.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given Bob has a live tab, API credential and pending job.
* When an admin removes Bob.
* Then new reads/writes and queued effects are denied and cached protected content is cleared.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given Bob has an existing file grant or optional active agent run.
* When revocation occurs.
* Then the accepted URL window and run cancellation policy are enforced and tested.

issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-ABUSE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want shared abuse controls, so that parallel requests cannot exhaust service capacity or email delivery.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Verify installed auth limiter; implement distributed limits for recovery/sign-in/invites/uploads/search/model discovery/run starts; safe 429/retry guidance and store-outage behavior.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §12; R9. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

issues.title: Delete accounts and workspaces with auditable purge progress
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-DELETION
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an authorized owner, I want a complete deletion workflow, so that removal includes dependent data and retained files.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Revoke access first, tombstone, purge DB/object/search/export data with checkpoints and retries; apply retention/backup exceptions and prevent unintended restore resurrection.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §10, §12; R10. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Only explicitly authorized deletion requests execute; progress distinguishes requested, purging and completed.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When its authorized deletion is confirmed and processed, the defined data classes are purged with an auditable completion record.
* **AC-02** — When processing resumes, remaining work completes without losing progress or restoring access.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a fixture workspace has issues, files and derived content.
* When its authorized deletion is confirmed and processed.
* Then the defined data classes are purged with an auditable completion record.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a worker/storage failure interrupts purge.
* When processing resumes.
* Then remaining work completes without losing progress or restoring access.

issues.title: Validate custom emoji uploads and workspace-scoped rendering
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-EMOJI
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a team member, I want safe shared custom emojis, so that expression does not break rendering or cross workspace boundaries.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Verify existing schema and create/delete paths; enforce image content/size/name policy, safe previews and historical deletion rendering.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 17; E03. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Custom emoji bytes and names must not introduce executable content or duplicate active names.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When another member uses it and later it is deleted, rendering is consistent and historical content has a defined fallback.
* **AC-02** — When validation runs, it is rejected without storing unsafe usable content.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an admin uploads a valid unique emoji.
* When another member uses it and later it is deleted.
* Then rendering is consistent and historical content has a defined fallback.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an oversized/active-content image or duplicate name is submitted.
* When validation runs.
* Then it is rejected without storing unsafe usable content.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Sync editable profile extras across authorized sessions
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PROFILE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an account holder, I want editable profile extras to follow me across devices, so that colleagues see consistent account information.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist and validate allowed profile fields through authenticated account commands, with field ownership and safe avatar/content handling. Reuse the authorization, version-precondition and command patterns directly; do not wait for cosmetic preference synchronization or mix private settings into the public profile record.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 30, §06. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Users may edit only allowed fields on their own account; profile changes cannot modify roles or workspace membership.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When another authenticated session reloads, the same validated values appear.
* **AC-02** — When the update is processed, it is denied without changing protected fields.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a user updates permitted profile fields.
* When another authenticated session reloads.
* Then the same validated values appear.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a user submits another account ID or protected role field.
* When the update is processed.
* Then it is denied without changing protected fields.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>), [FOR-32](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-32/commit-commands-receipts-audit-and-outbox-events-atomically>).

issues.title: Disable unfinished features consistently across UI and server routes
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-FEATURE_GATES
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a user, I want available features to work as described, so that previews and placeholders never masquerade as saved production behavior.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Inventory all preview/toast-only screens; gate server endpoints, navigation/deep links, agent/API tools and sample data; correct export success copy; per-workspace rollout controls.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §02-03, §14; E05. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Every deferred module must be inaccessible for real writes and any sample data must be labeled fictional.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When a user opens navigation, deep link or direct API, the agreed unavailable/preview behavior is consistent and no false success appears.
* **AC-02** — When another workspace requests it, server checks deny access despite a visible or forged client flag.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given Signals, Reviews, Insights or billing is deferred.
* When a user opens navigation, deep link or direct API.
* Then the agreed unavailable/preview behavior is consistent and no false success appears.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given one module is enabled for a test workspace only.
* When another workspace requests it.
* Then server checks deny access despite a visible or forged client flag.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Manage authorized external connections and applications
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-CONNECTOR_REGISTRY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace admin, I want connected apps with visible permissions and health, so that I can control external data access.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist connection ownership, scopes, credential references, sync status and revocation; define supported app providers; distinguish actual Calls OAuth from other placeholders.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 28, §14. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Disconnect must disable future sync/tools; available providers are explicit rather than implied by mock accounts.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the connection is listed then disconnected, health/permissions are visible and further use stops.
* **AC-02** — When the operation runs, unauthorized mutation fails or a clear reconnect state appears.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an admin authorizes a supported app with stated scopes.
* When the connection is listed then disconnected.
* Then health/permissions are visible and further use stops.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a nonadmin changes shared credentials or a provider token expires.
* When the operation runs.
* Then unauthorized mutation fails or a clear reconnect state appears.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>), [FOR-70](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-70/rotate-encrypted-provider-credentials-without-losing-access>), [FOR-103](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-103/disable-unfinished-features-consistently-across-ui-and-server-routes>).
Required before enabling this feature. A narrower release may defer it only by recording the scope decision and enforcing the feature gate.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Ingest real analytics signals with traceable evidence
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Later expansion · **Backlog key:** FPR-SIGNALS_INGEST
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a product teammate, I want signals from approved analytics accounts, so that insights are based on real evidence.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Choose supported providers/datasets; OAuth/API ingestion, tenant/account separation, checkpointed windows, deduplication, metric definitions and freshness; keep sample preview separate.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 24, §14; E05. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

issues.title: Connect pull requests and publish attributable review feedback
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Later expansion · **Backlog key:** FPR-REVIEWS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a developer, I want reviews of accessible pull requests, so that feedback relates to the code I am actually shipping.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Choose a supported Git provider and fetch authorized PR/diff/head/checks with freshness. Link issues and bind feedback to the reviewed head. Publication requires the user's explicit exact-content/destination authorization; persist its actor/input/head identity and enqueue via [FOR-33](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-33/deliver-external-effects-with-recoverable-outbox-processing>) with a stable provider reference so retries reconcile safely. Autonomous agent posting is outside this story and needs separate agent approval evidence. Do not require a model run merely to post user-approved feedback.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 25, §14. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Do not post AI suggestions automatically or use stale line locations after head changes.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When a user reviews it and explicitly approves posting feedback, comments reference H and the correct author/diff locations.
* **AC-02** — When feedback is submitted, posting is paused for refresh or denied without sending stale/private content.
* **AC-03** — Given the provider accepted feedback but the application lost its response, when the same user-authorized publication is retried, then the provider reference is reconciled and no duplicate comment is blindly posted.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an accessible PR at head H.
* When a user reviews it and explicitly approves posting feedback.
* Then comments reference H and the correct author/diff locations.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the PR head changes or access is revoked.
* When feedback is submitted.
* Then posting is paused for refresh or denied without sending stale/private content.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given the provider accepted feedback but the application lost its response.
* When the same user-authorized publication is retried.
* Then the provider reference is reconciled and no duplicate comment is blindly posted.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-104](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-104/manage-authorized-external-connections-and-applications>), [FOR-33](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-33/deliver-external-effects-with-recoverable-outbox-processing>).

Required before enabling this slice. Conditional extensions are governed by the accepted release manifest and their stated evidence checks; an excluded feature stays unavailable and is not marked implemented.

**Conditional or coordination links:** [FOR-80](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-80/execute-approved-agent-writes-with-crash-safe-command-receipts>). Read the implementation guidance and accepted release manifest for which of these must pass when enabled.

Blocking links describe prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation, contract design and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently where interfaces are agreed. Related links are coordination or conditional enablement work, not automatic blockers.

issues.title: Agree plans, entitlements and subscription lifecycle rules
issues.description:
**Type:** Product decision · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-BILLING_POLICY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a product owner, I want explicit paid-plan rules, so that checkout and access implement the same commercial contract.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Choose provider, plan entitlements, prices/currency, trial, grace/cancel/refund and seat rules; define event ordering and reconciliation; do not invent prices.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 27, §14. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A free pilot may defer billing; charging requires accepted rules and billing release evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the commercial policy is reviewed, each entitlement and lifecycle transition has an accepted rule.
* **AC-02** — When expected access is specified, the resulting rights and user communications are unambiguous.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given proposed plans and paid features.
* When the commercial policy is reviewed.
* Then each entitlement and lifecycle transition has an accepted rule.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a cancellation, failed payment or seat reduction occurs.
* When expected access is specified.
* Then the resulting rights and user communications are unambiguous.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-20](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates>).
Required before enabling this feature. A narrower release may defer it only by recording the scope decision and enforcing the feature gate.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

## Confirmed provider and implementation start · 28 October 2026

User chose **Polar**, with both free and paid subscriptions in the first public web/agent/macOS release. Existing $12/user UI copy is placeholder data, not approved pricing. Resolve charging unit, actual plan prices, free/paid limits, trial/grace/cancel/seat rules one decision at a time. Preparing the Polar integration contract while these decisions are resolved.

### Confirmed charging unit

User chose **per-workspace subscriptions with usage limits shared by members**. Superseded by the later decision below: the subscription belongs to the workspace and is priced per active member. Price/currency are confirmed below; shared limits remain undecided.

### Final confirmed pricing model · 28 October 2026

This supersedes the earlier flat-workspace interpretation. One subscription belongs to each workspace, priced **per active user per month**, with a workspace-shared usage pool that grows per active member.

* Free plan is available at launch.
* Starter: **€10/user/month in Europe; $10/user/month elsewhere**.
* Plus: **€16/user/month in Europe; $16/user/month elsewhere**.
* Enterprise: custom pricing, outside self-serve checkout.
* User explicitly confirmed equal numeric EUR/USD amounts, not FX conversion.
* All active members, including owners/admins, count toward the subscription and pooled allowance. Pending invitations do not count.

Still required: actual per-member AI allowance for each tier, billing-country/currency resolution, proration/seat changes and trial/grace/cancellation policy. No usage numbers or lifecycle rules are inferred.

### Confirmed AI allowance and overage policy · 28 October 2026

All standard tiers (Free, Starter, Plus) contribute **US$5 per active member per month**, pooled across the workspace. This is denominated in USD regardless of subscription invoice currency. Pending invitations contribute nothing. Paid overage is supported with a **separate monthly workspace spending cap**, but stays disabled until a workspace owner/admin explicitly opts in and sets that cap. No automatic cap amount or overage unit price is approved by this decision.

### Overage consent confirmed

User explicitly requires overage to stay off until a workspace owner/admin opts in and sets a monthly workspace cap. The included US$5/member pool and paid-overage cap are separate. Usage reset boundary is the next pending decision. Overage rate, billable usage basis, proration/seat changes and payment authorization/invoicing must be specified before enabling charges.

### Confirmed period, overage rate and BYOK policy · 28 October 2026

* Paid allowance resets use each workspace's billing anniversary; Free uses its workspace signup anniversary.
* Paid overage is charged at the underlying model/provider cost, with **no markup**. Existing opt-in and capped-authorization requirements still apply.
* **BYOK is excluded from Forge allowance and overage billing**; members pay their provider directly. Direct customer provider subscriptions are likewise excluded by the billing-mode contract.
* New runs persist the server-resolved billing mode; client usage events cannot choose their payer. Missing payer/pricing on historical rows requires reconciliation before invoicing.

Calendar-month environment caps are existing operational controls, distinct from the new commercial anniversary ledger. Seat-change proration is the next pending policy decision.

### Confirmed seat-change timing · 28 October 2026

User selected **apply member seat charges/credits at the next renewal**. No mid-cycle seat proration. Preserve the current billed-seat snapshot and schedule the active-member quantity for renewal. Existing US$5-per-active-member shared allowance policy remains separate. Preparing provider scheduling/reconciliation tests; no live subscription is modified.

### Confirmed pricing-currency authority · 28 October 2026

EUR/USD pricing must be selected from the **workspace billing address country**, per the user's decision. IP geolocation, browser locale, personal appearance preferences and client-supplied currency are not pricing authority. The exact European country set is being clarified separately. Existing subscription currency changes require an explicit lifecycle policy; a country edit must not silently reprice an existing subscription.

### Confirmed EUR country group · 28 October 2026

User selected **EU/EEA countries, the UK and Switzerland** for EUR pricing. Use explicit billing-country codes for the 27 EU countries plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, United Kingdom (`GB`) and Switzerland (`CH`); all other valid supported billing-country codes use USD. This is the chosen commercial region, independent of the eurozone or browser locale. Invalid/missing countries require correction, not a silent USD fallback. New-checkout currency is derived from the persisted workspace billing address country. Existing subscription currency changes remain an unresolved lifecycle case.

### Free plan correction and screenshot reference · 28 October 2026

User explicitly changed Free to **at most 5 active members** and a **fixed US$5 monthly workspace AI allowance**, independent of member count. This supersedes the earlier US$5-per-member statement for Free only. Starter and Plus keep US$5 per active member. Calls and Signals consume the Free workspace allowance; on paid plans those features do not debit the shared AI allowance or generate allowance-based overage. Provider costs/operational controls still require internal tracking; exclusion does not itself promise unlimited throughput.

User supplied three Linear Plans screenshots as the remaining feature-allocation reference. Draft interpretation: screenshot Basic → Forge Starter, Business → Forge Plus, preserve Enterprise as custom. Explicit Forge overrides win: Free 5 members, fixed US$5 pool and Free-only Calls/Signals metering; existing confirmed monthly EUR/USD prices remain monthly even though the screenshot says billed yearly. Record a source-transcribed feature matrix and distinguish entitlement availability from delivered feature capability and contractual/compliance claims.

### Current standard-plan policy and feature reference

Free: **maximum 5 active members, fixed US$5/month per workspace, no paid overage**. This explicitly supersedes the earlier per-member Free allowance. Starter/Plus: US$5 per active member with the approved opt-in/payment/cap controls for paid overage. Calls and Signals draw allowance on Free; on paid plans they neither debit the AI pool nor generate allowance-based overage. Keep internal provider telemetry and operational limits.

The user supplied Linear Plans screenshots for remaining allocations: Basic → Starter and Business → Plus. Source-transcribed matrix, explicit Forge overrides, numeric limits, enterprise/compliance caveats and open lifecycle questions are documented in [Forge launch plans — entitlements and usage policy](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b>). Confirmed monthly billing takes precedence over the reference's yearly copy. A commercial allocation is not proof that the feature has shipped or passed its release gate.

### Member grandfathering on downgrade confirmed · 28 October 2026

User selected **keep existing access; block new joins** when a paid workspace returns to Free above five active members. Do not evict members or force selection of five. New admissions remain blocked at five or more; below five, capacity becomes available. Idempotent access/retry by an existing member is not a new admission. Role/privacy checks and explicit member removal still apply. Usage becomes the fixed Free US$5 pool with no overage, preserving already consumed usage rather than resetting it; exact period/plan-change carryover still needs ledger rules.

### Free trial confirmed · 28 October 2026

User confirmed **14-day free trials for Starter and Plus**. Payment collection/automatic conversion choice, eligibility/redemption, trial usage and repeat-trial protection still require completion before enabling public checkout.

Prepared adapter contract: trusted server context must explicitly resolve boolean trial eligibility; eligible checkout requests exactly 14 days, while ineligible checkout explicitly disables provider/product-default trials. Missing or invalid eligibility refuses checkout creation. No browser-provided duration or trial toggle is authoritative. No live trial, checkout or charge was started. Latest billing suite: **9 files / 162 tests passed**, including both paid trial tiers, ineligible/default-trial suppression and invalid eligibility refusal. This does not verify live trial conversion.

The user additionally confirmed that valid payment grace permits included AI and paid overage under the existing opt-in/cap. An unpaid first subscription receives no grace; provider recovery clears the failure episode. The implementation record is linked from <issue id="125b71bf-f1b7-46d5-b456-b81d02b0c0d0" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-111/reconcile-payment-events-into-server-enforced-entitlements">FOR-111</issue>. Cancellation, refunds and other unresolved lifecycle policies still prevent this overall decision issue from being Done.

### Cancellation timing confirmed — 28 October 2026

The user selected **keep paid access until the current billing period ends** when a workspace owner cancels. Schedule cancellation with the provider; preserve paid access through the paid-through boundary and resolve to Free at that exact boundary. Preserve existing members under the confirmed downgrade rule. Cancellation cannot extend an unpaid grace period or mint a new allowance. Implementing the provider command, durable cancellation boundary, current-state reconciliation and read/member-insertion parity. Refunds and exceptional immediate revocations remain separate unresolved policies.

### Full subscription-period refund confirmed — 28 October 2026

The user selected **end paid access immediately** when the charge for the current subscription period is fully refunded. Existing workspace members retain access under Free; further joins and paid features follow Free limits. Do not erase prior usage, reservations, receipts or billing history. This rule concerns a full refund of the current subscription period, not partial refunds, AI-overage refunds or an old paid period. Implement a durable refunded-period denial so newer/delayed subscription-active events cannot regrant the refunded term.

### Full-refund access rule implemented and verified

A verified full refund of the current subscription-period charge ends paid access immediately; preserve existing workspace members and history and apply Free admission limits. The term cannot grant later failed-renewal grace. A genuinely paid, nonoverlapping later period remains separate. Partial refunds, exceptional revocation and pause rules still need decisions, so this policy issue remains In Progress. [Implementation and release limits](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-full-refund-access-revocation-and-durable-reconciliation-f7b2de8c955e>).

### Partial subscription-period refund confirmed — 28 October 2026

The user selected keeping paid access unchanged after a partial refund of the current subscription-period charge. A partial refund neither revokes nor restores access, changes the paid period or grace clock, nor grants another AI pool. A later cumulative full refund still follows immediate revocation. <issue id="125b71bf-f1b7-46d5-b456-b81d02b0c0d0" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-111/reconcile-payment-events-into-server-enforced-entitlements">FOR-111</issue> implementation is continuing with verified amounts, durable receipt/audit and partial-to-full ordering tests.

### Partial-refund access rule implemented and verified

Verified positive partial subscription-period refunds keep paid access unchanged. They write an atomic audit/receipt without creating/updating entitlement state, advancing paid/grace boundaries or clearing any full-refund denial. Cumulative full refunds trigger immediate revocation, including after replaying the original partial event. App/workflow and isolated staging checks pass. Exceptional immediate termination and pause policy remain open; this overall policy issue stays In Progress.

### Immediate provider termination confirmed — 28 October 2026

The user selected ending paid access immediately when Polar immediately terminates a subscription, even during the seven-day payment grace period. Normal owner cancellation remains scheduled for period end. Preserve existing workspace members, consumption, reservations and billing history; resolve new paid access/capacity as Free. A terminal subscription must not be reactivated by delayed or replayed active/past-due/cancellation snapshots.

### Immediate provider termination implemented and verified

Current verified Polar terminal state ends paid access immediately, including during grace. This includes final unpaid status after provider retry exhaustion. Normal scheduled cancellation remains period-end. Existing members/history are retained. The earliest terminal marker persists independently of ordinary provider-version ordering; later active/grace/cancellation/partial-refund updates cannot reopen that subscription. [Implementation and release limits](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-immediate-subscription-termination-and-access-enforcement-af59bd14d245>). The confirmed termination access slice is verified; this overall decision issue remains In Progress for paid plan-transition, pause and other remaining commercial rules.

### Paid tier-change timing confirmed — 28 October 2026

The user selected immediate Starter→Plus upgrades with proration, and Plus→Starter downgrades at the next renewal. Existing member seat changes still take effect only at renewal; a tier change must not accelerate seat changes, alter currency, mint another trial or create another first-purchase AI pool. Implementing trusted owner/admin commands, provider-state verification, pending-seat preservation and receipt/audit reconciliation. Any unverified charge/provider result stays pending, not successful.

### Failed upgrade payment confirmed

If the prorated payment for a Starter→Plus upgrade fails, retain Starter access until payment succeeds. This is not permission to grant Plus during the renewal-payment grace period. Preserve the current paid period, existing usage and the separately confirmed renewal-only seat policy. Provider plan/status alone must not turn an unpaid upgrade invoice into Plus access.

### Full refund of the upgrade-only charge confirmed

The user selected returning to Starter for the rest of the already-paid period when only the prorated Plus-upgrade charge is fully refunded. This differs from refunding the base subscription-period charge, which ends all paid access. Verify an unrefunded/partially refunded paid Starter base-period invoice, preserve its paid-through boundary and all consumption, and never regrant Plus from a delayed proof for the refunded upgrade invoice. A separately verified newer paid Plus grant remains separate.

### Paid-tier timing, failed payment and upgrade-only refund — implementation checkpoint

Implemented and staging-verified: immediate prorated upgrades after paid invoice verification; renewal-time downgrades; preservation of billed seats/currency/period and future membership quantity; Starter retention on failed upgrade payment; and Starter fallback for the verified already-paid period after refunding only the upgrade charge. A full base-period refund or terminal subscription still ends paid access. The subsequent 29 October decision confirms Starter at the next renewal after a full upgrade-only refund; the follow-up below implements it. [Implementation guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-paid-tier-changes-payment-proof-and-upgrade-refunds-d1a96dfa65d7>). Overall policy issue remains In Progress.

### Upgrade-refund renewal confirmed · 29 October 2026

After fully refunding only the prorated Plus-upgrade charge, retain the verified already-paid Starter base period and renew on Starter. The pending renewal keeps existing billed/scheduled seats, currency and anniversary. No extra charge, credit, trial or pool is created by restoring Starter. A separately verified newer paid Plus purchase may supersede this old refund intent; a stale refund must not override it.

Implemented prepared backend flow: signed refund → durable restriction/receipt → current provider/binding check → explicit next-period Starter schedule → locked confirmation/audit/receipt. Failure remains retryable, including a lost response or audit outage. No new migration or public billing enablement. [Guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-paid-tier-changes-payment-proof-and-upgrade-refunds-d1a96dfa65d7>).

### No subscription pausing at launch — confirmed and implemented · 29 October 2026

The user chose no subscription pause/resume at launch. Use the approved period-end cancellation path. Do not expose pause/resume in Forge billing or the customer-facing Polar portal; provider configuration is an actual sandbox/candidate release gate, not a claimed live setting change.

Unexpected provider pauses now receive a durable access cutoff: verified actual pause time, or original period end for a scheduled pause. Preserve current paid access before that scheduled boundary; deny paid features/overage/capacity at and after it, with existing sessions retained. Ordinary active/resumed events cannot clear the exception; verified operational repair/replacement remains release work. [Implemented safeguards](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-cancellation-policy-and-unsupported-provider-pauses-c6f800e9e3f7>).

This policy slice is complete; remaining commercial choices include currency transitions/overage conversion and team/issue/upload over-capacity behavior. Overall policy issue remains In Progress.

### Overage currency and FX — confirmed · 29 October 2026

EUR subscriptions use EUR for paid AI overage and the separate cap; USD subscriptions use USD. Included AI pools remain USD under the existing plan rules. Fix the FX rate when the provider usage is incurred, using the latest published ECB daily reference rate with no added spread. Capture it before usage, retain the original source/rate/time, and never reprice that usage at invoice time. ECB is an agreed reference conversion, not a representation of actual bank/payment-provider FX execution.

Prepared conversion, bounded server source and currency-aware cap arithmetic are implemented and verified. [Guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-paid-ai-overage-currency-and-usage-time-ecb-conversion-408511e4f5c1>). Atomic ledger/quote retention, invoice allocation and real billing remain gated. The commercial rule for an existing subscription changing between EUR/USD country regions still needs a decision. Overall policy issue stays In Progress.

### Currency move and replacement checkout grace — confirmed · 29 October 2026

An existing paid workspace moving between EUR/USD billing-country regions switches currency at its next renewal. The user approved a **7-day replacement-checkout grace period** if checkout is incomplete by that boundary. Freeze the deadline at original renewal + 168 hours; edits/retries cannot restart it. Current paid-period charges, consumption, reservations and invoice/FX units remain unchanged.

Pinned Polar 2026-10 has no currency update parameter; product changes retain the old currency, and paid creation requires checkout. The provider-verified durable request path is implemented, but no unsupported currency PATCH, automatic checkout, paid replacement or grace access is claimed. [Guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-renewal-currency-changes-replacement-checkout-and-grace-a37b6a97beb3>). The late-checkout billing-anniversary rule remains the next required decision. Overall issue stays In Progress.

### Original anniversary, cap carryover and grandfathered capacity — confirmed · 29 October 2026

Late replacement payment within the fixed seven-day checkout grace keeps the original monthly anniversary and commercial usage period. Persist the original UTC day and recover it only from adjacent verified monthly boundaries. Clamp short months while retaining the original day; do not silently drift the 31st to the 28th. Replacement payment is subscription continuation, with no new trial or first-purchase pool.

The user selected automatic conversion of an existing opted-in overage cap at the latest published ECB rate, frozen at verified cutover. Carry consumed/reserved capacity in the same commercial period; preserve original invoice/reservation/usage-time units and rates. Disabled/exhausted overage must not become new spending authority. Prepared arithmetic is implemented; the atomic cutover/ledger executor is still required.

The user also confirmed that team and active-issue downgrades retain existing access and block new creation/import/unarchiving above the new cap. Do not delete or conceal content. <issue id="e99eba3f-77ee-4e94-8927-69f1ddb44396" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-154/enforce-free-and-starter-team-capacity-across-creation-and-imports">FOR-154</issue> has the team transition specification; active-issue enforcement must cover its authoritative persistence/commands.

[Guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-renewal-currency-changes-replacement-checkout-and-grace-a37b6a97beb3>). Before-tax pricing is confirmed below. Overall issue remains In Progress.

### Before-tax checkout policy confirmed and prepared — 29 October 2026

Listed Starter EUR/USD 10 and Plus EUR/USD 16 per member are before tax; add applicable tax at checkout. The checkout adapter now fetches the approved monthly product and validates its one active flat seat-based catalog price, explicit exclusive tax behavior, exact currency/per-seat price and uncapped tier. It refuses inherited/inclusive/location tax settings, ambiguous prices, archived/nonmonthly/capped products, then rechecks trusted workspace/country/member context. Discount codes/provider trials are disabled and no ad-hoc price override is sent. The replacement verifier requires resolved exclusive tax with matching net/tax/total proof. The pinned CheckoutCreate has no tax-behavior override; catalog preflight enforces the rule.

Current checks: **1,553 app + 4 workflow tests; 62 PostgreSQL billing + 17 real-auth member cases; 3 full-history migration fault cases; 36 isolated migrations**, typecheck, scoped lint/format/diff and production build including protected Workflow handlers pass. Actual Polar sandbox credentials are missing; a secure local sandbox configuration request is pending. No provider catalog/checkout/setting was changed, no billing/public action enabled and no serving-data migration/deployment occurred. Overall issue remains In Progress.

issues.title: Start subscription checkout and manage billing from Forge
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-CHECKOUT
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace billing admin, I want hosted checkout and billing management, so that I can purchase and maintain the intended plan.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Create server-owned customer/workspace mapping and provider checkout/portal sessions; validate price IDs and actor role; render pending/cancel/error states.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §14; billing expansion. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A checkout success redirect is not authority to grant paid access.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When checkout completes and redirects, the UI shows pending/confirmed status based on server state without trusting query parameters.
* **AC-02** — When the request is made, it is denied and no cross-workspace billing access is created.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an authorized billing admin selects an approved plan.
* When checkout completes and redirects.
* Then the UI shows pending/confirmed status based on server state without trusting query parameters.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a member tampers with plan/price or opens another workspace's portal.
* When the request is made.
* Then it is denied and no cross-workspace billing access is created.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-109](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-109/agree-plans-entitlements-and-subscription-lifecycle-rules>), [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>).
Required before enabling this feature. A narrower release may defer it only by recording the scope decision and enforcing the feature gate.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

## Provider foundation started · 28 October 2026

Preparing a server-only Polar SDK adapter with explicit environment/configuration and workspace customer identity. Updated charging unit: one workspace subscription priced per active member, with shared usage that scales with membership. Commercial policy and full authorization/command prerequisites remain open; only contract/adapter work is starting, not live checkout or granting entitlements.

## Adapter preparation evidence · 28 October 2026

Implemented locally (uncommitted/undeployed): pinned `@polar-sh/sdk@1.0.2`, API export `2026-10`; explicit disabled-by-default billing configuration, sandbox/production selection, HTTPS production app origin validation, server-only credentials, strict configured product ID and safe configuration diagnostics.

`workspaceBillingIdentity` binds the Polar external customer to the authenticated workspace, requiring an owner/admin session. Checkout uses the server-owned product with no client amount/member/seat override; portal uses that same external workspace ID. Hosted destinations require HTTPS. Checkout returns pending and never changes entitlements.

Verification: **2 test files / 14 tests passed**, app TypeScript passed, billing-file ESLint passed, `git diff --check` passed. Tests cover disabled/missing/unsafe config, credential redaction, scope/role denial, cross-workspace customer identity, provider failure, hosted URLs and pending checkout.

Guide: `docs/polar-billing.md`; environment names documented in `.env.example` with billing disabled. No remote account changes, checkout or charge occurred. Polar connector discovery returned no available integration; the app adapter uses the official SDK.

**Still In Progress:** approved price/currency and limits, production product/account setup, stable customer mapping and checkout receipts/reconciliation, protected application routes/UI, and billing release evidence. <issue id="125b71bf-f1b7-46d5-b456-b81d02b0c0d0" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-111/reconcile-payment-events-into-server-enforced-entitlements">FOR-111</issue> owns webhook/entitlement reconciliation; this adapter does not satisfy its gate.

### Adapter updated for confirmed member pricing

Prepared Starter/Plus × EUR/USD product mapping, selected-tier validation, and trusted server-resolved checkout seats. Pending invitations are excluded by counting accepted member rows; all accepted roles count. Checkout fixes the quantity to the resolved membership and rejects invalid/cross-workspace context. Price contract records 10/16 per user monthly and keeps Enterprise outside self-serve checkout. Shared-pool arithmetic supports growth per active member without inventing the actual allowance.

Catalog amount/currency/seat-pricing validation, authoritative country resolution, seat-update/proration lifecycle, receipts/reconciliation and public routes/UI remain required before real checkout. The old flat-workspace foundation text is superseded; no live checkout/charge occurred.

Latest member-pricing verification: **4 files / 22 tests passed**, plus app TypeScript and billing-file lint. Tests include monthly 10/16 × active-user arithmetic, safe shared-pool growth, Enterprise exclusion, accepted-member SQL scope, exact tier/currency product selection, server-controlled seat bounds and refusal of cross-workspace/invalid billing context. Monthly AI allowances are still awaiting the user's next decision; fixture usage values are not commercial policy.

### Renewal-only member seat changes started · 28 October 2026

Confirmed: changes in active membership affect subscription seat charges at the next renewal, with no mid-cycle charge or credit. Preparing Polar `proration_behavior: next_period` seat scheduling, server-resolved member quantities, workspace/subscription ownership checks, and repeated/conflicting update handling. Current billed seats remain separate from the US$5-per-current-active-member usage allowance. Routes, durable scheduling/reconciliation and live provider verification remain open.

### Renewal seat adapter verified locally · 28 October 2026

Implemented `PolarSeatRenewalScheduler` in `apps/forge/src/application/billing/polar-seat-renewal.server.ts`, using the pinned Polar 2026-10 SDK and explicit `proration_behavior: next_period`. It reads a trusted subscription/member context, checks owner/admin authority, workspace external customer ownership, configured product/currency, monthly interval and valid period, and refuses unsupported lifecycle states or conflicting pending changes. It supports increases/decreases, repeated requests without duplicate writes, replacing a seat-only schedule, withdrawing it when membership returns to the billed quantity, and re-reading provider state after an uncertain timeout. Provider responses must preserve current billed seats, amount, period and product before success is reported.

Verification: **billing suite 8 files / 70 tests passed**, including **30 renewal seat cases**; app TypeScript, changed-file ESLint and `git diff --check` passed. Local working tree remains **uncommitted and undeployed**, based on `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`; no live subscription or charge was modified. Guide: `docs/polar-billing.md`.

This completes the adapter slice only. <issue id="882acdf1-dff1-4c20-bbeb-6e77cc81f8d9" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-110/start-subscription-checkout-and-manage-billing-from-forge">FOR-110</issue> **remains In Progress.** Public checkout/portal routes/UI, server billing-country resolution and catalog verification remain open. Membership integration must use a durable outbox and serialize subscription changes; <issue id="125b71bf-f1b7-46d5-b456-b81d02b0c0d0" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-111/reconcile-payment-events-into-server-enforced-entitlements">FOR-111</issue> still owns signed webhooks, period-boundary/event reconciliation and entitlement projection. No atomic or live-billing guarantee is claimed.

### Billing-country currency selection started · 28 October 2026

User confirmed workspace billing address country as the currency source. EUR applies to EU/EEA countries, the UK and Switzerland; USD elsewhere. Implementing country validation and server-derived currency/product choice, removing the separate caller-resolved currency field from checkout context. Missing or unsupported billing countries must fail before provider checkout creation. Checkout will pass its billing country to Polar and require an address. Existing subscription currency migration remains separate from new-checkout pricing.

### Billing-country selection verified locally · 28 October 2026

Implemented `billing-country.ts`: valid country-code inputs match the pinned Polar API, with trim/uppercase normalization and no fallback for missing/invalid/unsupported countries. Explicit EUR region is EU27 + IS/LI/NO + GB/CH (32 countries); other accepted billing-country codes use USD. `WorkspaceBillingContext` now carries server-resolved `billingCountry`, replacing its separate `currency` field. Checkout derives catalog product and currency from that country, passes it in `customer_billing_address`, requires a billing address, and records the country snapshot in metadata. An obsolete currency override cannot change pricing.

Verification: **9 billing files / 137 tests passed**, including every EUR-country fixture, non-region USD examples, invalid/missing countries, provider input-type compatibility and checkout override rejection. App TypeScript, changed-file ESLint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Local working tree is **uncommitted/undeployed**; no checkout, customer or charge was created. Guide: `docs/polar-billing.md`.

<issue id="882acdf1-dff1-4c20-bbeb-6e77cc81f8d9" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-110/start-subscription-checkout-and-manage-billing-from-forge">FOR-110</issue> **remains In Progress.** The persisted billing profile and trusted country resolver, public routes/UI, provider catalog validation and checkout receipts are not yet wired. Hosted address edits must be reconciled against the intended country/currency/product before confirming entitlements; metadata or a checkout redirect is not proof of paid access. Currency migration for existing subscriptions remains a lifecycle decision.

### Free trial confirmed · 28 October 2026

User confirmed **14-day free trials for Starter and Plus**. Payment collection/automatic conversion choice, eligibility/redemption, trial usage and repeat-trial protection still require completion before enabling public checkout.

Prepared adapter contract: trusted server context must explicitly resolve boolean trial eligibility; eligible checkout requests exactly 14 days, while ineligible checkout explicitly disables provider/product-default trials. Missing or invalid eligibility refuses checkout creation. No browser-provided duration or trial toggle is authoritative. No live trial, checkout or charge was started. Latest billing suite: **9 files / 162 tests passed**, including both paid trial tiers, ineligible/default-trial suppression and invalid eligibility refusal. This does not verify live trial conversion.

### Trial conversion decision — authoritative correction

User selected **no payment details; manual upgrade** for the confirmed 14-day Starter/Plus trial. Forge must manage trial eligibility/start/expiry itself; do not create a Polar subscription or collect a payment method to start the trial, and never charge automatically at expiry. Polar checkout is for a separately initiated paid upgrade.

**This supersedes the earlier hosted-trial preparation.** Checkout now always sends `allow_trial: false` and omits trial duration; even an obsolete `trialEligible`/duration context value cannot enable a hosted trial. Trial duration remains 14 days in the plan contract. No live trial, subscription or charge was created. Application-managed trial persistence, eligibility/redemption, expiry and usage policy remain open. Latest billing suite after this correction: **9 files / 157 tests passed**.

### Current implementation checkpoint · 28 October 2026

The user confirmed trial eligibility **once per workspace**, across all creators/admins and both Starter/Plus. Persist one immutable workspace-scoped redemption; retries, switching trial tier, different admins and trial expiry cannot create another trial. Enforce uniqueness and start/usage-grant writes atomically, with no payment details or automatic conversion.

Current local verification: **211 app test files / 1,242 tests passed on rerun**, including **9 billing files / 164 tests**. TypeScript, billing ESLint, formatting and diff checks passed. The first full run had one review-screen emoji-picker failure; its isolated rerun and the second full run passed without modifying that screen. Source changes remain uncommitted and undeployed; no live trial, membership transaction or provider charge was changed.

Fixed Free/trial pools, no Free/trial overage, trusted plan/phase/feature/payer classification, trial-period bounds and hosted-trial suppression are prepared. Durable trial redemption/expiry, membership transactions, authoritative entitlement projection and live billing remain open; helper tests are not their completion evidence.

### Owner/admin cancellation command prepared

User confirmed paid access continues until billing-period end. [Server command and verification](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-period-end-cancellation-and-retained-access-1ee5ac990eb6>). Implemented server-derived environment/subscription binding, live first-party role checks before the provider write, exact scheduled-cancel request, provider confirmation, accepted-timeout recovery and no repeated write when already scheduled. Live roles are checked again before receipt replay. The backend is verified against isolated staging with provider fixtures; no live cancellation occurred.

This does not close <issue id="882acdf1-dff1-4c20-bbeb-6e77cc81f8d9" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-110/start-subscription-checkout-and-manage-billing-from-forge">FOR-110</issue>: billing UI/public action wiring, checkout/portal rollout, durable effect processing and actual Polar sandbox/candidate flows still remain. The provider method is not exposed as a new unauthenticated public action.

### AC-03 / AT-03 — Trusted paid-tier commands

**AC-03:** A live first-party owner/admin can request Starter↔Plus changes using server-resolved binding, effective paid tier and active-member count. Send immediate upgrade proration explicitly as invoice; send downgrades explicitly for next period. Preserve current billed seats, currency, period and future seat changes. Revalidate role/binding before each provider write. Never report an unverified payment as an applied upgrade. Retrying an observed accepted target or pending downgrade must not invoice again; withdrawing a downgrade must retain the renewal quantity.

**AT-03 passing:** Exact API bodies, pending seat/downgrade composition, timeout recovery, invalid/foreign/dunning/terminal states, live-role revocation before charge, unchanged current period/currency/seats and real database audit-failure recovery. Current checks: **1,392 app + 4 workflow tests; 43 isolated PostgreSQL billing, 16 real-auth membership and 3 migration fault cases; typecheck, changed-file lint/format, diff checks and production build pass.** [Server command and release limits](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-paid-tier-changes-payment-proof-and-upgrade-refunds-d1a96dfa65d7>).

Prepared entry: changeWorkspacePlan → readPlanChangeContext → PolarPlanChanger. No public UI/action or live provider mutation is enabled. This issue remains In Progress for UI/checkout/portal flows, durable workspace serialization/effects, ambiguous outcomes, controlled repeat upgrade after refund, portal policy configuration and actual Polar sandbox/candidate gates.

### AC-04 / AT-04 — Preserve Starter renewal after a fully refunded upgrade

**AC-04:** An owner/admin Plus command cannot reuse the fully refunded upgrade payment or withdraw the refund's Starter renewal schedule. A fresh Plus purchase requires controlled provider adjustment and new verified paid evidence. Normal seat scheduling keeps the pending Starter product; it cannot replace the product change with a seat-only schedule.

**AT-04 passing:** Live context derives the refunded-grant guard from durable workspace/environment/subscription/period history. A repeated Plus request is refused before provider writes. Simulated stale context and delayed paid proof remain fenced by the locked entitlement sink. Existing product/seat composition tests pass. This confirmed slice is complete; public billing and controlled repurchase remain gated. [Guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-paid-tier-changes-payment-proof-and-upgrade-refunds-d1a96dfa65d7>).

### AC-05 / AT-05 — Cancellation is the launch exit path

**AC-05:** No public pause/resume command or billing control is offered at launch. Period-end cancellation remains supported, and must never emit a resume or clear provider pause state. Plan commands persist newly observed provider pause restrictions before refusing writes; the live context refuses a stored exception. Upgrade-refund renewal also refuses unsupported paused bindings. Portal pause/resume controls must be disabled and verified before billing enablement.

**AT-05 backend slice passing:** Separate pause fields and actual paused status; restriction projection before refusing product changes; only cancel_at_period_end=true sent by the cancellation command; strict missing/contradictory provider-state rejection. Shared access/database/auth checks pass. [Guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-cancellation-policy-and-unsupported-provider-pauses-c6f800e9e3f7>). Public UI and actual provider portal/candidate verification remain unfinished launch gates, so this overall issue stays In Progress.

### AC-06 / AT-06 — Provider-verified renewal currency request

**AC-06:** A first-party owner/admin can request a renewal currency change from live provider-confirmed billing country and current binding, with no browser country/currency/price/seat override. Carry approved pending Starter downgrade into the renewal tier; recheck authority/binding after provider reads and transactionally. Persist one requested intent with original renewal boundary and +168-hour checkout deadline, informational current member/approved price snapshot, audit and receipt. Retain superseded/withdrawn history; returning to current currency withdraws the switch. Responses say requires-checkout and providerChangeScheduled=false.

**AT-06 passing:** Real planner/live context/provider read into concurrent PostgreSQL intent/receipt/audit; same-ID replay, actor revocation before cached result, changed-body/binding rejection, country supersession/withdrawal, fixed deadlines, pending tier/quantity snapshot, unchanged entitlements, audit rollback/retry, stale-boundary refusal and observed pause persistence before refusal. Unit API-key/member and provider-state guards pass. [Guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-renewal-currency-changes-replacement-checkout-and-grace-a37b6a97beb3>).

Prepared request slice complete. Overall issue remains In Progress: public action/UI, owned source cancellation, actual replacement checkout, grace entitlement, paid old/new binding proof, late-checkout anniversary, communications/durable effects and Polar sandbox/candidate flows remain gated. No live provider write or billing enablement.

### AC-07 / AT-07 — Original-anniversary replacement payment plan

**AC-07:** A late successful replacement payment retains the original UTC monthly anchor and commercial usage window. Migration 0035 stores original period start/day/next renewal.
