**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-CHECKOUT
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace billing admin, I want hosted checkout and billing management, so that I can purchase and maintain the intended plan.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Create server-owned customer/workspace mapping and provider checkout/portal sessions; validate price IDs and actor role; render pending/cancel/error states.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §14; billing expansion. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A checkout success redirect is not authority to grant paid access.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When checkout completes and redirects, the UI shows pending/confirmed status based on server state without trusting query parameters.
* **AC-02** — When the request is made, it is denied and no cross-workspace billing access is created.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an authorized billing admin selects an approved plan.
* When checkout completes and redirects.
* Then the UI shows pending/confirmed status based on server state without trusting query parameters.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a member tampers with plan/price or opens another workspace's portal.
* When the request is made.
* Then it is denied and no cross-workspace billing access is created.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-109](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-109/agree-plans-entitlements-and-subscription-lifecycle-rules>), [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>).
Required before enabling this feature. A narrower release may defer it only by recording the scope decision and enforcing the feature gate.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

## Provider foundation started · 28 October 2026

Preparing a server-only Polar SDK adapter with explicit environment/configuration and workspace customer identity. Updated charging unit: one workspace subscription priced per active member, with shared usage that scales with membership. Commercial policy and full authorization/command prerequisites remain open; only contract/adapter work is starting, not live checkout or granting entitlements.

## Adapter preparation evidence · 28 October 2026

Implemented locally (uncommitted/undeployed): pinned `@polar-sh/sdk@1.0.2`, API export `2026-10`; explicit disabled-by-default billing configuration, sandbox/production selection, HTTPS production app origin validation, server-only credentials, strict configured product ID and safe configuration diagnostics.

`workspaceBillingIdentity` binds the Polar external customer to the authenticated workspace, requiring an owner/admin session. Checkout uses the server-owned product with no client amount/member/seat override; portal uses that same external workspace ID. Hosted destinations require HTTPS. Checkout returns pending and never changes entitlements.

Verification: **2 test files / 14 tests passed**, app TypeScript passed, billing-file ESLint passed, `git diff --check` passed. Tests cover disabled/missing/unsafe config, credential redaction, scope/role denial, cross-workspace customer identity, provider failure, hosted URLs and pending checkout.

Guide: `docs/polar-billing.md`; environment names documented in `.env.example` with billing disabled. No remote account changes, checkout or charge occurred. Polar connector discovery returned no available integration; the app adapter uses the official SDK.

**Still In Progress:** approved price/currency and limits, production product/account setup, stable customer mapping and checkout receipts/reconciliation, protected application routes/UI, and billing release evidence. <issue id="125b71bf-f1b7-46d5-b456-b81d02b0c0d0" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-111/reconcile-payment-events-into-server-enforced-entitlements">FOR-111</issue> owns webhook/entitlement reconciliation; this adapter does not satisfy its gate.

Pending invitations are excluded by counting accepted member rows; all accepted roles count. Checkout fixes the quantity to the resolved membership and rejects invalid/cross-workspace context. issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-ENTITLEMENTS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a paying workspace owner, I want plan access to match my subscription, so that retries or delayed webhooks do not remove or invent access.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Verify webhook signatures/raw bodies; stable event IDs, ordering, provider reconciliation and auditable entitlement projection; enforce in services.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §14; billing expansion. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Duplicate/out-of-order events are idempotent; policy governs grace/cancel/refund behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When they are verified and reconciled, one correct entitlement state matches the provider and accepted policy.
* **AC-02** — When access is evaluated, no unauthorized entitlement is granted.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given payment events arrive twice and out of order.
* When they are verified and reconciled.
* Then one correct entitlement state matches the provider and accepted policy.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a forged event or old success redirect claims payment.
* When access is evaluated.
* Then no unauthorized entitlement is granted.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-110](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-110/start-subscription-checkout-and-manage-billing-from-forge>), [FOR-33](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-33/deliver-external-effects-with-recoverable-outbox-processing>).

Required before enabling this slice. Conditional extensions are governed by the accepted release manifest and their stated evidence checks; an excluded feature stays unavailable and is not marked implemented.

Blocking links describe prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation, contract design and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently where interfaces are agreed. Related links are coordination or conditional enablement work, not automatic blockers.

**Completion evidence:** every AC has a corresponding AT specification above. Attach results for the named commit/environment and relevant artifact. Resolve open policy choices before coding them; no passing test, estimate, owner assignment or delivery date is implied.

## Current plan projection and usage integration contract

Use [Forge launch plans](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b>). Explicitly migrate legacy basic → Starter and business → Plus; extend the existing entitlement source, not another paid-access authority. Plan availability must remain separate from feature readiness, role/privacy authorization and enterprise agreements.

**AC-03:** Reconciled plan snapshots apply fixed Free US$5/workspace, no Free overage, Starter/Plus US$5/member, the 5-member Free cap and screenshot resource/feature allocations. Enterprise allowances require explicit custom terms. Pending invitations do not mint credits or billed seats.
**AT-03:** Given repeat/out-of-order upgrade/downgrade events, existing consumed usage and stale paid overage opt-in, when projection/admission is evaluated as Free, then the pool is US$5, overage is zero, existing consumption remains and new member admission follows <issue id="708503bd-17d3-4ba8-89a9-d0e38cdd86ae" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-153/enforce-the-free-workspace-member-limit-across-every-join-path">FOR-153</issue>. Do not infer an eviction/grace policy before it is decided.

**AC-04:** Trusted server plan/feature/payer snapshots control both reservation and settlement. Paid Calls/Signals neither debit the agent allowance nor generate its overage and are not denied solely because that pool is exhausted; operational controls still apply. Free Calls/Signals consume its fixed pool; BYOK remains excluded.
**AT-04:** Given a paid workspace has exhausted its agent pool, when a Calls/Signals operation is admitted and settled, then it uses zero allowance reservation/charge while retaining internal provider-cost telemetry. Repeat on Free with no allowance remaining and assert refusal of metered work. Forged feature/plan/payer and historical unknown classifications cannot silently bypass billing. Helper tests alone do not satisfy ledger/provider integration.

### Implementation started — failed-renewal access lifecycle

The user confirmed 7 days of paid-access grace after failed renewal. Implementing durable first-failure/grace-expiry state and a shared time-aware entitlement reader, with exact expiry tests and database/auth member-admission parity. Repeated or delayed provider events cannot mint initial paid access or extend the original failure episode. Production billing remains gated while signed receipts, reconciliation and remaining lifecycle policies are completed.

### Grace-period AI policy confirmed

During the 7-day failed-renewal grace period, the user permits included AI allowance **and paid overage under the existing explicit opt-in and finite cap**. No new overage authorization or cap is created by entering grace. At expiry, access resolves as Free; existing members retain access and new joins follow Free capacity. Enforcement must use the same persisted original failure/grace timestamps across feature checks and membership insertion, not a webhook-delivery-relative timeout.

### Durable grace and signed reconciliation implemented — isolated staging verified

[Implementation, trust boundaries and rollout guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-failed-renewal-grace-and-subscription-reconciliation-d97d91c24bf1>). The server now verifies exact webhook bytes with the pinned Polar SDK, validates event identity, fetches authoritative subscription state, checks customer/workspace/catalog/currency/cadence and atomically writes entitlement state, digest receipt and audit. Replayed IDs cannot alter bytes or workspace identity; older versions are stale, conflicting equal versions are refused. Prior paid activation is required for grace, original failure cannot move later on retry, recovery clears it, and expiry resolves as Free without a webhook/sweep. Existing overage opt-in/cap remains required; card-free trials gain no overage authority.

Migrations 0027/0028 were applied only to isolated forge_staging, now 29 migrations. Eight real PostgreSQL cases passed for signed concurrent duplicate delivery, no restart, recovery/stale events, initial unpaid refusal, expiry/override denial, conflicting receipts/versions, rollback on audit failure, cross-workspace subscription binding and exactly 168 hours across daylight saving. Require authoritative proof that the old binding has ended before replacing it; do not relax the current subscription-conflict check for arbitrary new IDs.

**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-ENTITLEMENTS
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a paying workspace owner, I want plan access to match my subscription, so that retries or delayed webhooks do not remove or invent access.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Verify webhook signatures/raw bodies; stable event IDs, ordering, provider reconciliation and auditable entitlement projection; enforce in services.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §14; billing expansion. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Duplicate/out-of-order events are idempotent; policy governs grace/cancel/refund behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When they are verified and reconciled, one correct entitlement state matches the provider and accepted policy.
* **AC-02** — When access is evaluated, no unauthorized entitlement is granted.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given payment events arrive twice and out of order.
* When they are verified and reconciled.
* Then one correct entitlement state matches the provider and accepted policy.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a forged event or old success redirect claims payment.
* When access is evaluated.
* Then no unauthorized entitlement is granted.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-110](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-110/start-subscription-checkout-and-manage-billing-from-forge>), [FOR-33](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-33/deliver-external-effects-with-recoverable-outbox-processing>).

Required before enabling this slice. Conditional extensions are governed by the accepted release manifest and their stated evidence checks; an excluded feature stays unavailable and is not marked implemented.

Blocking links describe prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation, contract design and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently where interfaces are agreed. Related links are coordination or conditional enablement work, not automatic blockers.

**Completion evidence:** every AC has a corresponding AT specification above. Attach results for the named commit/environment and relevant artifact. Resolve open policy choices before coding them; no passing test, estimate, owner assignment or delivery date is implied.

## Current plan projection and usage integration contract

Use [Forge launch plans](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b>). Explicitly migrate legacy basic → Starter and business → Plus; extend the existing entitlement source, not another paid-access authority. Plan availability must remain separate from feature readiness, role/privacy authorization and enterprise agreements.

**AC-03:** Reconciled plan snapshots apply fixed Free US$5/workspace, no Free overage, Starter/Plus US$5/member, the 5-member Free cap and screenshot resource/feature allocations. Enterprise allowances require explicit custom terms. Pending invitations do not mint credits or billed seats.
**AT-03:** Given repeat/out-of-order upgrade/downgrade events, existing consumed usage and stale paid overage opt-in, when projection/admission is evaluated as Free, then the pool is US$5, overage is zero, existing consumption remains and new member admission follows <issue id="708503bd-17d3-4ba8-89a9-d0e38cdd86ae" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-153/enforce-the-free-workspace-member-limit-across-every-join-path">FOR-153</issue>. Do not infer an eviction/grace policy before it is decided.

**AC-04:** Trusted server plan/feature/payer snapshots control both reservation and settlement. Paid Calls/Signals neither debit the agent allowance nor generate its overage and are not denied solely because that pool is exhausted; operational controls still apply. Free Calls/Signals consume its fixed pool; BYOK remains excluded.
**AT-04:** Given a paid workspace has exhausted its agent pool, when a Calls/Signals operation is admitted and settled, then it uses zero allowance reservation/charge while retaining internal provider-cost telemetry. Repeat on Free with no allowance remaining and assert refusal of metered work. Forged feature/plan/payer and historical unknown classifications cannot silently bypass billing. Helper tests alone do not satisfy ledger/provider integration.

### Implementation started — failed-renewal access lifecycle

The user confirmed 7 days of paid-access grace after failed renewal. Implementing durable first-failure/grace-expiry state and a shared time-aware entitlement reader, with exact expiry tests and database/auth member-admission parity. Repeated or delayed provider events cannot mint initial paid access or extend the original failure episode. Production billing remains gated while signed receipts, reconciliation and remaining lifecycle policies are completed.

### Grace-period AI policy confirmed

During the 7-day failed-renewal grace period, the user permits included AI allowance **and paid overage under the existing explicit opt-in and finite cap**. No new overage authorization or cap is created by entering grace. At expiry, access resolves as Free; existing members retain access and new joins follow Free capacity. Enforcement must use the same persisted original failure/grace timestamps across feature checks and membership insertion, not a webhook-delivery-relative timeout.

### Durable grace and signed reconciliation implemented — isolated staging verified

[Implementation, trust boundaries and rollout guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-failed-renewal-grace-and-subscription-reconciliation-d97d91c24bf1>). The server now verifies exact webhook bytes with the pinned Polar SDK, validates event identity, fetches authoritative subscription state, checks customer/workspace/catalog/currency/cadence and atomically writes entitlement state, digest receipt and audit. Replayed IDs cannot alter bytes or workspace identity; older versions are stale, conflicting equal versions are refused. Prior paid activation is required for grace, original failure cannot move later on retry, recovery clears it, and expiry resolves as Free without a webhook/sweep. Existing overage opt-in/cap remains required; card-free trials gain no overage authority.

Three migration-owner/fault cases passed against the updated history. Shared entitlement readers tolerate the previous schema; a read-only legacy-database probe succeeded with zero writes.

**AC-05:** After an old subscription has ended and access is Free, a new legitimate paid subscription for the same workspace can be reconciled without losing old receipts/usage or allowing two active subscriptions. Require authoritative proof that the old binding has ended before replacing it; do not relax the current subscription-conflict check for arbitrary new IDs.

**AT-05:** Given a canceled-and-ended workspace and preserved original receipts, when an owner starts a new paid subscription, fetch/verify both the prior terminal state and new paid state, then atomically move the binding and retain history. Repeat with the old subscription still active, a foreign customer, duplicate events and a race; refuse unsafe replacement without granting access or double billing.

The current conflict guard intentionally remains strict until this replacement path is implemented and verified. Coordinate with <issue id="882acdf1-dff1-4c20-bbeb-6e77cc81f8d9" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-110/start-subscription-checkout-and-manage-billing-from-forge">FOR-110</issue> checkout/portal identity and <issue id="8fa7eb8a-25fc-47b5-8459-9bcd3d62ff2b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-76/atomically-admit-runs-and-reserve-provider-spend">FOR-76</issue> period/grant rules; no additional blanket blocker is added.

### Full-refund implementation started

User confirmed immediate loss of paid access on full refund of the current subscription period. Adding provider-verified order/period identity, a durable refunded-period latch, atomic receipt/audit persistence, and shared feature/auth/SQL membership denial. Subscription updates cannot clear that latch; a later genuinely paid period remains separate. Partial/old/overage refunds must not be guessed into this rule. Billing remains release-gated.

### AC-06 / AT-06 — Full subscription-period refund

**AC-06:** Verify a full current-period subscription charge refund from the current Polar order and its dated line item, then deny paid features/capacity for that subscription/environment/period immediately. Preserve member sessions, existing access, usage and history. Retain denial across later active, canceled and grace updates, including overlapping period adjustments; do not let a refunded term bootstrap renewal grace. Duplicate delivery is atomic/idempotent; refunds before activation and concurrent reconciliation must retain the denial. An old refund cannot revoke a nonoverlapping paid period.

**AT-06:** Signed webhook → current order fetch → catalog/customer/full net+tax/period validation → transactional history+audit+receipt; replay/conflict, audit rollback, activation/refund races, later active updates, renewed payment, stale feature overrides, SQL member admission and real-auth session/pending-invite checks. **Passing locally:** 1,325 app + 4 workflow tests; isolated PostgreSQL billing 18, real-auth membership 14 and full-history migration fault 3. Typecheck/lint/build passed; final format check recorded in the checkpoint. All 31 migrations are applied only to isolated staging/rehearsal.

[Full-refund implementation guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-full-refund-access-revocation-and-durable-reconciliation-f7b2de8c955e>). No live provider refund/charge or serving deployment. Partial/mixed/balance-credit invoice allocation, exceptional revocation/pause, binding replacement, periodic reconciliation/outbox, communications, commercial ledger and real Polar release validation remain; keep this issue In Progress and live billing disabled.

### AC-07 / AT-07 — Partial refunds retain access

**AC-07:** A verified positive partial refund of the current subscription-period charge preserves existing paid/grace/cancellation access and its boundaries. Audit and receipt are atomic/idempotent without changing entitlement or full-refund history. A partial refund cannot restore expired/refunded access. If current-order re-fetch shows a cumulative full refund, promote an earlier partial receipt atomically and apply full-period denial; do not depend on a second webhook arriving. Conflicting identities/digests, invalid totals or status/amount contradictions must not be acknowledged.

**AT-07 passing:** Signed partial delivery in active, past-due and scheduled-canceled states leaves complete entitlement state unchanged; duplicates create one receipt/audit; preactivation partials create no entitlement; cumulative full-refund promotion and audit-failure rollback/retry; a late partial snapshot cannot restore denied access. Positive partial total validation and invalid status/net/tax/allocation cases pass. Current evidence: **1,331 app + 4 workflow tests; 24 PostgreSQL billing and 14 real-auth membership cases on isolated staging; TypeScript, changed-file ESLint/Prettier, diff checks and production build pass.** No new migration or live billing mutation/deployment. [Refund implementation guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-full-refund-access-revocation-and-durable-reconciliation-f7b2de8c955e>).

The confirmed partial-refund access slice is complete. This issue remains In Progress for exceptional revocation/pause policy, mixed/prorated/balance-credit invoice allocation, verified subscription binding replacement, periodic reconciliation/outbox/communications, commercial ledger and actual Polar sandbox/release gates; live billing remains disabled.

### AC-08 / AT-08 — Final provider termination overrides paid access and grace

**AC-08:** Verify current terminal Polar state after a signed revoked/updated event, then deny paid features, overage authority and paid member capacity immediately, including during grace. Preserve existing member sessions, grandfathered membership, usage/refund/receipt history and original paid/grace/cancellation clocks. Bind terminal-before-activation safely. Terminal proof can restrict access even with older/equal provider versions and cannot be cleared or moved later by ordinary active/past-due/canceled/uncanceled events. Same-event identity/digest replay may promote previously acknowledged active state to terminal state atomically. A failed audit must roll back marker/receipt changes. The cancellation adapter must reconcile a detected termination without another provider write, including a moved-period race.

**AT-08 passing:** 1,343 app + 4 workflow tests; isolated PostgreSQL billing 31, real-auth membership 15 and complete-history migration fault 3. Includes active/grace/canceled signed termination, preactivation ordering, older/equal restrictive proof, newer active snapshots, cached active-event promotion, audit rollback, feature overrides, member admission, retained sixth-member session and pending invite. TypeScript, changed-file lint/format, diff checks and production build pass. Migration 0031 is applied only to isolated staging/rehearsal (32 migrations each). [Termination implementation guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-immediate-subscription-termination-and-access-enforcement-af59bd14d245>).

The confirmed immediate-termination access slice is complete. Overall issue stays In Progress for paid replacement/reinstatement verification, pause/plan-transition rules, periodic reconciliation/outbox/communications, invoice allocation, commercial ledger and actual Polar sandbox/candidate gates. Live billing remains disabled.

**AC-05 refinement:** Any legitimate paid replacement must verify that the old binding is terminal, retain its receipts/refund/usage history and clear the old terminal latch only as part of an atomic switch to the separately verified new paid subscription. Do not allow an ordinary active snapshot to clear it or silently relax the subscription-conflict guard.

### AC-09 / AT-09 — Payment-backed tier access

**AC-09:** Provider product/status alone cannot elevate existing Starter access to Plus. Verify a paid, non-fully-refunded matching Plus invoice and current period; an unpaid upgrade preserves the old Starter contract and its paid/grace/cancellation boundaries without extending them or creating another pool. Paid evidence can promote a matching version or cached event. An early provider downgrade cannot remove already-paid Plus before renewal. Actor/projection/command audit/receipt persistence is atomic; role revocation is checked before cached command results.

**AT-09 passing:** Signed order-paid → current order/subscription → scoped paid invoice evidence → same-version/cached-event promotion; missing/foreign/unpaid/refunded evidence; stale proof; unchanged original activation/period/grace; downgrade applied only in the new authoritative period; command audit failure followed by recovery without another product invoice; live role revocation. [Guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-paid-tier-changes-payment-proof-and-upgrade-refunds-d1a96dfa65d7>).

### AC-10 / AT-10 — Refund only the upgrade charge

**AC-10:** Fully refunding a prorated Plus-upgrade charge restores only a verified still-paid Starter base period. Keep usage, members, original period and history. Record paid Plus order identity and upgrade-refund identity so delayed payment proof cannot restore the refunded grant, while a genuinely newer paid grant remains separate. Missing base proof removes unproven Plus and returns retryable reconciliation; a replay can fill the base reference. Full base refund/termination still denies paid access. Partial refunds remain unchanged.

**AT-10 passing:** Signed full prorated refund and base create/cycle invoice verification; temporarily unavailable or fully refunded base evidence; replay promotion to Starter; refund before activation; stale paid-proof fencing; newer paid Plus versus old refunds; full-base override; audit rollback; SQL/auth paid-capacity parity; retained sixth-member session and successful later admission after base verification. Migration 0032 is applied only to isolated staging/rehearsal (33 migrations each). Current checks: **1,392 app + 4 workflow tests; billing PostgreSQL 43, real-auth membership 16, migration fault 3; typecheck/lint/format/diff/build pass.** [Implementation and remaining release gates](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-paid-tier-changes-payment-proof-and-upgrade-refunds-d1a96dfa65d7>).

Confirmed access slices are complete; the overall issue stays In Progress. No live invoice/refund/provider setting, push, deployment or serving/default database change. Remaining: controlled repeat-upgrade/provider adjustment, public actions, durable billing effects/serialization, ambiguous outcomes, periodic reconciliation/communications, historical allocations, commercial usage ledger and actual Polar sandbox/candidate evidence. Live billing remains disabled.

### AC-11 / AT-11 — Starter renewal after an upgrade-only refund

**AC-11:** Commit the verified full-upgrade-refund restriction first, then schedule approved same-currency Starter with explicit next-period timing. Preserve current product/charge/billed seats/period and scheduled renewal seats. Persist confirmation and digest-only receipt atomically under the workspace lock. Replays recover accepted writes without issuing a second provider update. Failures keep the signed webhook retryable; base evidence may still be retried independently. Terminal/newly paid/replacement bindings cannot receive an old refund confirmation. Never cancel, uncancel, unpause, reset a period or issue another invoice/credit here.

**AT-11 passing:** Signed webhook through real staging projection/receipt/audit; provider accepted but response lost; confirmation audit constraint failure/rollback then replay; exactly one provider product update and confirmation; unchanged pending seat count; genuine next-term Starter access; stale replay after renewal; newer paid Plus grant during confirmation; required durable refund marker and binding; terminal projection and conflicting lifecycle/period/pending state refusal.

Current verification: **1,412 app + 4 workflow tests; 46 isolated PostgreSQL billing and 16 real-auth membership cases; typecheck, changed-file ESLint/Prettier, diff and production build.** No new schema migration; staging remains at 33. Prior migration fault evidence is unchanged (3 cases). Initial unrelated review emoji-picker timeout passed isolated and final full reruns. [Implementation guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-paid-tier-changes-payment-proof-and-upgrade-refunds-d1a96dfa65d7>).

Confirmed renewal slice is complete. Overall issue remains In Progress for durable external-effect serialization/redrive/reactivation, controlled repurchase, public actions, ledger, remaining policy and Polar sandbox/candidate release gates. No live provider mutation, push, deployment or serving/default database change. Billing stays disabled.

### AC-12 / AT-12 — Unsupported provider pause cannot retain paid rights

**AC-12:** Validate pause_at_period_end, paused_at and resumes_at, including the real provider paused status. Signed paused/resumed events re-fetch current state. Actual pause cuts off paid rights at the verified pause time; scheduled pause keeps existing paid rights only until the original period end. Persist the earliest cutoff with audit/receipt under the workspace lock; cached/stale delivery cannot extend it. Ordinary active/resumed events and later paid periods cannot clear it. No first paid activation/grace is minted from a paused binding. Shared feature/overage policy, JSON reader and SQL member admission agree; existing member sessions remain valid.

**AT-12 passing:** Signed paused/resumed → provider read → restriction/audit/receipt; active/past_due/paused provider states; cached-event promotion; earlier versus later scheduled cutoffs; audit rollback/replay; pause before activation; later active events; retained sixth-member session and pending invitation with new admission blocked. Migration 0033 and all 34 migrations passed on isolated rehearsal/staging; 3 full-history migration ownership/fault cases passed.

Current checks: **1,428 app + 4 workflow tests, 52 isolated PostgreSQL billing and 17 real-auth membership cases**; typecheck, changed-file ESLint/Prettier, diff and production build including protected Workflow handlers. [Implementation and recovery limits](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-cancellation-policy-and-unsupported-provider-pauses-c6f800e9e3f7>).

Confirmed no-pause backend/access slice complete. Overall issue remains In Progress for verified repair/replacement, communications, durable provider effects/redrive, public billing/ledger and Polar sandbox/candidate release checks. No serving/default database, local connection, live provider setting, push or deployment changed. Billing stays disabled.

**AC-12 ordering refinement:** A signed resumed event observed before any pause delivery must not become an unverified first paid activation. Re-fetch current provider state and use its verified modification time as the restrictive cutoff; do not take a date or access claim from the event body. This preserves the no-resume launch policy even when event delivery is reordered. Covered by unit and real PostgreSQL signed-webhook cases.

### AC-13 / AT-13 — Currency intent is never payment or grace proof

A currency request and its status cannot grant paid access, clear a terminal/pause/refund restriction, reset a trial/allowance, or replace subscription identity. The implemented request transaction preserves existing entitlement state and history, locks the workspace and live membership, and commits intent/audit/receipt atomically. Revoked actors cannot use cached requests. A changed source or unfinished request at another boundary requires reconciliation; no renewed +7-day window is invented.

Current checks: **1,465 app + 4 workflow tests; 58 isolated PostgreSQL billing and 17 real-auth membership cases; 3 full-history migration fault cases**. Typecheck, changed-file lint/format, diff and production build including protected Workflow handlers pass. Migration 0034 and all 35 migrations are applied only to isolated staging/rehearsal. [Provider limitation, verified request and unfinished executor](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-renewal-currency-changes-replacement-checkout-and-grace-a37b6a97beb3>).

Overall issue stays In Progress for the separately verified old/new paid binding, actual bounded checkout-grace authority, period/usage/currency reconciliation and remaining ledger/provider-release gates. No provider subscription/checkout/portal mutation, serving/default database, local connection, push or deployment change. Billing remains disabled.

### AC-14 / AT-14 — Preserve paid continuation and original currency evidence

Original anniversary is now confirmed. Durable request anchor fields and safe audited legacy capture preserve the original monthly window. A read-only replacement verifier checks the paid checkout/order/subscription before producing a calendar plan; it explicitly cannot rebind access, clear restrictions, activate grace or mint a first-purchase allowance. Polar's period-end update resets its hidden day; retain the original day and durably repair a short-month following renewal before enabling cutover.

The user selected ECB conversion of existing opted-in caps. Prepared cutover arithmetic carries settled/reserved capacity without repricing historical charges or granting a new cap/payment authority. Atomic policy/quote/capacity persistence must commit once with the verified old/new binding and retain late original-currency settlement identities.

**AT-14 prepared slice passing:** Calendar, payment-response and capacity-conversion tests; four new real PostgreSQL cases cover concurrent legacy capture, audit rollback/retry, SQL partial/invalid anchors and live context revocation/supersession. Verified checkpoint: **1,541 app + 4 workflow tests; 62 isolated PostgreSQL billing + 17 real-auth membership cases; 3 full-history migration ownership/fault cases**. Migration 0035 was rehearsed through all 36 migrations before the one pending expansion was applied to exact isolated staging. Typecheck and scoped lint/format pass; final build verification is being recorded in the linked guide/checkpoint. No live provider effect, public billing enablement or serving-data migration.

[Guide](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-renewal-currency-changes-replacement-checkout-and-grace-a37b6a97beb3>). Overall issue remains In Progress: source-stop evidence, bounded grace authority, actual period adjustment/recurring repair, atomic paid replacement/capacity ledger, communications/redrive and actual provider/candidate flows are unfinished. No request/calendar/payment plan is itself entitlement proof.

### Before-tax checkout policy confirmed and prepared — 29 October 2026

Listed Starter EUR/USD 10 and Plus EUR/USD 16 per member are before tax; add applicable tax at checkout. The checkout adapter now fetches the approved monthly product and validates its one active flat seat-based catalog price, explicit exclusive tax behavior, exact currency/per-seat price and uncapped tier. It refuses inherited/inclusive/location tax settings, ambiguous prices, archived/nonmonthly/capped products, then rechecks trusted workspace/country/member context. Discount codes/provider trials are disabled and no ad-hoc price override is sent. The replacement verifier requires resolved exclusive tax with matching net/tax/total proof. The pinned CheckoutCreate has no tax-behavior override; catalog preflight enforces the rule.

Current checks: **1,553 app + 4 workflow tests; 62 PostgreSQL billing + 17 real-auth member cases; 3 full-history migration fault cases; 36 isolated migrations**, typecheck, scoped lint/format/diff and production build including protected Workflow handlers pass. Actual Polar sandbox credentials are missing; a secure local sandbox configuration request is pending. No provider catalog/checkout/setting was changed, no billing/public action enabled and no serving-data migration/deployment occurred. Overall issue remains In Progress.

issues.title: Verify paid subscription lifecycle before enabling billing
issues.description:
**Type:** Release gate · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-BILLING_GATE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a release owner, I want tested payment transitions, so that charging customers does not rely on a happy-path checkout.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Use provider test mode for activation, renewals, failed payments, cancellation, grace, seat changes and reconciliation outage; audit server access and customer copy.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §14. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Paid launch stays disabled until all accepted commercial transitions have evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the billing test matrix runs, entitlements and user messages match the policy for every case.
* **AC-02** — When billing enablement is requested, the release gate blocks paid launch.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given test subscriptions cover each accepted lifecycle transition.
* When the billing test matrix runs.
* Then entitlements and user messages match the policy for every case.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a provider outage or event mismatch remains unresolved.
* When billing enablement is requested.
* Then the release gate blocks paid launch.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-111](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-111/reconcile-payment-events-into-server-enforced-entitlements>).
Required before enabling this feature. A narrower release may defer it only by recording the scope decision and enforcing the feature gate.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

Current hosted-trial adapter suppression is not proof that Forge's trial service is implemented.

<issue id="708503bd-17d3-4ba8-89a9-d0e38cdd86ae" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-153/enforce-the-free-workspace-member-limit-across-every-join-path">FOR-153</issue>'s atomic database/auth implementation is verified in an isolated schema-only branch (11 PostgreSQL cases; app/workflow/build checks passed). The friendly SDK preflight alone is not atomic enforcement. Implementation/rollout instructions: [https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/atomic-workspace-member-capacity-implementation-and-rollout-a8b750fd4060](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/atomic-workspace-member-capacity-implementation-and-rollout-a8b750fd4060>). This gate and its existing prerequisites remain open.

issues.title: Export authorized workspace data as a reliable background job
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-EXPORT
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want a real data export, so that I can retain or move my work.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Define versioned export schema for enabled domains, snapshot consistency, bounded jobs, status/progress, safe download expiry and retention; replace toast-only completion.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 29, §11; R1, R10. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Only authorized data is exported and completion means an actual downloadable file exists.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When an authorized export completes, a versioned artifact contains the permitted records and valid references.
* **AC-02** — When the job/download is resumed, private download is denied or retry resumes without falsely reporting success.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a fixture workspace has issues, comments and files.
* When an authorized export completes.
* Then a versioned artifact contains the permitted records and valid references.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given access is revoked or the export worker fails midway.
* When the job/download is resumed.
* Then private download is denied or retry resumes without falsely reporting success.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-36](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-36/authorize-file-downloads-and-isolate-untrusted-previews>), [FOR-64](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-64/run-leased-resumable-background-jobs-with-operator-recovery>).

Required before enabling this slice. Conditional extensions are governed by the accepted release manifest and their stated evidence checks; an excluded feature stays unavailable and is not marked implemented.

Blocking links describe prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation, contract design and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently where interfaces are agreed. Related links are coordination or conditional enablement work, not automatic blockers.

**Completion evidence:** every AC has a corresponding AT specification above. Attach results for the named commit/environment and relevant artifact. Resolve open policy choices before coding them; no passing test, estimate, owner assignment or delivery date is implied.

issues.title: Import supported external datasets with preview and reconciliation
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Later expansion · **Backlog key:** FPR-EXTERNAL_IMPORT
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want a validated external import, so that I can move existing work into Forge without losing relationships.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Choose supported format/provider, version schema, mappings, access confirmation, duplicates and manifest-based recovery; bound uploaded content and preserve originals.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 29; separate from browser migration. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Unsupported formats and ambiguous mappings require a preview/choice rather than guessing.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the owner previews and imports it twice with one manifest, accepted records reconcile once with valid mappings.
* **AC-02** — When validation runs, those rows are quarantined with actionable errors and no silent data loss.

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a supported fixture export contains related records.
* When the owner previews and imports it twice with one manifest.
* Then accepted records reconcile once with valid mappings.

issues.title: Meet agreed performance and capacity budgets under realistic load
issues.description:
**Type:** Release gate · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-PERFORMANCE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a release owner, I want measured capacity evidence, so that the first production workspaces do not exceed untested limits.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Run accepted dataset/concurrency/region workload; measure p95 reads/writes, errors, DB pools, query plans and file/event replay; fix bottlenecks and capture evidence.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §13; R12. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Budgets are accepted targets, not assumptions; results include workload and exact deployment.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When load tests run for the agreed duration, all accepted core budgets pass with reproducible measurements.
* **AC-02** — When the gate is reviewed, the failing workload blocks launch until fixed or the scope/target is explicitly revised.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given the approved workload and release candidate.
* When load tests run for the agreed duration.
* Then all accepted core budgets pass with reproducible measurements.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given query latency or error rate exceeds a target.
* When the gate is reviewed.
* Then the failing workload blocks launch until fixed or the scope/target is explicitly revised.

issues.title: Verify keyboard, mobile and failure recovery across core journeys
issues.description:
**Type:** Release gate · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-ACCESSIBILITY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a user with keyboard or mobile access needs, I want usable core flows, so that I can complete work without inaccessible controls.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Test focus/dialog semantics, accessible names/errors, keyboard-only create/edit/comment/upload, narrow viewport and slow/offline recovery; record assistive checks.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §13; R12. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Success requires completing the journey, not only passing an automated accessibility scanner.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When they sign in, create/edit/comment and process inbox items, all actions complete with visible focus and understandable errors.
* **AC-02** — When the user retries a retained draft, no essential action is clipped and no unsaved data is falsely reported saved.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a keyboard-only user on the candidate.
* When they sign in, create/edit/comment and process inbox items.
* Then all actions complete with visible focus and understandable errors.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a narrow viewport and failed network save.
* When the user retries a retained draft.
* Then no essential action is clipped and no unsaved data is falsely reported saved.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-48](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-48/attach-durable-files-to-issues-and-comments>), [FOR-51](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-51/use-shared-assigned-created-and-subscribed-issue-views>), [FOR-66](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-66/sync-read-snooze-delete-and-subscription-state-across-devices>), [FOR-96](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-96/recover-password-access-with-single-use-verified-reset-flows>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Require exact-commit CI checks and controlled production promotion
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-RELEASE_PIPELINE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a release owner, I want enforced deployment gates, so that a Git-sourced deployment cannot bypass required validation.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Configure preview/staging/prod differences, required checks and protected promotion; retain lint/types/test/build/evals; verify deployed SHA and migration compatibility.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §13; R12; E16, E20. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Presence of CI files or a READY deployment does not prove that required checks passed.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When promotion is attempted, production promotion is blocked.
* **AC-02** — When the release is promoted then rolled back in staging, identities match and the previous compatible app works.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a candidate commit fails a required check.
* When promotion is attempted.
* Then production promotion is blocked.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the verified commit passes and its schema is compatible.
* When the release is promoted then rolled back in staging.
* Then identities match and the previous compatible app works.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-26](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-26/validate-service-specific-production-configuration-at-startup>), [FOR-28](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-28/rehearse-serialized-expand-and-contract-database-releases>).

issues.title: Verify dependencies, secrets hygiene and production bundle contents
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-SUPPLY_CHAIN
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an operator, I want inspected release artifacts, so that dependencies and debug surfaces do not introduce unmanaged risk.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Generate dependency/license/SBOM inventory and vulnerability ownership; scan build artifacts for leaked test secrets and devtools; inspect the Notion-title claim only with evidence, rotate confirmed exposed credentials.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §02, §13. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Do not claim secret exposure from a title or devtools inclusion solely from source imports.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When artifact and dependency checks run, findings are classified with owners and required fixes block release.
* **AC-02** — When the artifact is inspected, the report records actual shipped evidence rather than an inferred failure.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a production build and dependency inventory.
* When artifact and dependency checks run.
* Then findings are classified with owners and required fixes block release.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a component is imported in source but stripped in production.
* When the artifact is inspected.
* Then the report records actual shipped evidence rather than an inferred failure.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-117](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-117/require-exact-commit-ci-checks-and-controlled-production-promotion>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Verify desktop login, navigation and IPC trust boundaries
issues.description:
**Type:** Release gate · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-DESKTOP_SECURITY
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a desktop user, I want web-equivalent access protections, so that native integration does not bypass workspace security.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Test packaged login/deep links/session removal, IPC sender checks, navigation/remote content policy and Codex broker credential isolation; provide the safe host boundary used by [FOR-135](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-135/respect-desktop-link-choices-and-open-real-web-settings>) and [FOR-136](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-136/drive-desktop-badges-from-authorized-unread-notification-state>). Packaged preference behavior is verified separately in [FOR-142](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-142/verify-packaged-desktop-preferences-and-web-handoff>); that gate depends on this security foundation.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 31, §13. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Renderer or arbitrary navigation cannot access privileged host capabilities or provider credentials.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When login, deep links and workspace switching are exercised, authorized destinations and state match the web contract.
* **AC-02** — When the action occurs, privilege/access is denied and credentials remain provider-owned.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a signed candidate and valid desktop user.
* When login, deep links and workspace switching are exercised.
* Then authorized destinations and state match the web contract.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given untrusted renderer/navigation tries privileged IPC or a user is removed.
* When the action occurs.
* Then privilege/access is denied and credentials remain provider-owned.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-97](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-97/verify-signup-email-change-account-linking-and-workspace-invitations>), [FOR-98](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-98/revoke-member-access-across-sessions-files-keys-and-active-runs>).
Required before enabling this feature. A narrower release may defer it only by recording the scope decision and enforcing the feature gate.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

issues.title: Prove multi-user isolation and crash recovery on the release candidate
issues.description:
**Type:** Release gate · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-CROSS_SURFACE
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a release owner, I want end-to-end production-like evidence, so that individual unit tests cannot hide integration failures.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Run two-user/multi-workspace/private-team matrix, concurrent writes, restart/redeploy, ambiguous commit retry, migration recovery, files and notifications; use real staging Postgres.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §14; R1-R12. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Tests run against the candidate SHA/deployment and do not mutate real customer data.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the complete core journey and fault matrix executes, shared state, denial, deduplication and recovery gates pass.
* **AC-02** — When results are reviewed, the gate fails with reproduction evidence and a blocking fix.
* **AC-03** — Team/workspace settings, invitations, role changes and workspace security policies enforce the same accepted permissions through direct server requests and the UI.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given the candidate with two independent users and private-team fixtures.
* When the complete core journey and fault matrix executes.
* Then shared state, denial, deduplication and recovery gates pass.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given one worker crash duplicates an effect or a forbidden read succeeds.
* When results are reviewed.
* Then the gate fails with reproduction evidence and a blocking fix.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given workspace A with owner Alice, member Bob and private team P, plus workspace B.
* When both users attempt team create/update/delete, member role changes, invitations and security-policy changes through the UI and direct server routes, including forbidden workspace/team IDs.
* Then allowed actions persist with appropriate audit evidence, denied actions produce no effects or private-data leaks, and removal/deletion behavior matches the agreed policy.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-49](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-49/show-attributable-issue-history-from-committed-changes>), [FOR-45](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-45/delete-and-restore-issues-with-consistent-downstream-state>), [FOR-118](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-118/verify-dependencies-secrets-hygiene-and-production-bundle-contents>), [FOR-116](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-116/verify-keyboard-mobile-and-failure-recovery-across-core-journeys>), [FOR-115](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-115/meet-agreed-performance-and-capacity-budgets-under-realistic-load>), [FOR-57](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-57/reconcile-migration-results-and-switch-every-issue-entry-point>), [FOR-38](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-38/rehearse-recovery-of-database-files-and-encryption-keys>), [FOR-98](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-98/revoke-member-access-across-sessions-files-keys-and-active-runs>), [FOR-149](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-149/enforce-browser-request-origins-and-session-trust-boundaries>).

Required for core production.

## Outcome

issues.title: Approve and execute the controlled core production launch
issues.description:
**Type:** Release gate · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-CORE_LAUNCH
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a product owner, I want a controlled release decision, so that real users enter a demonstrably supportable product.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Review source/commit/deployment evidence and unresolved blockers; verify enabled optional modules satisfy their own gates; controlled rollout, synthetic checks, rollback criteria and monitoring ownership.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §14; all core gates. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** Core launch excludes only explicitly disabled modules. Any enabled optional surface must pass its gate before launch; no automatic inference of approval.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the release owner approves the recorded candidate, controlled rollout executes with monitored success and a rollback path.
* **AC-02** — When go/no-go is evaluated, launch is blocked or the module is explicitly disabled before approval.
* **AC-03** — Every exposed web preference and personal automation has evidence from [FOR-141](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-141/verify-web-preference-behavior-before-exposing-production-controls>); if desktop is distributed, [FOR-142](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-142/verify-packaged-desktop-preferences-and-web-handoff>) and [FOR-120](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-120/ship-verified-signed-macos-packages-and-recoverable-updates>) also pass. Deferred controls are consistently unavailable under the recorded release scope.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given all core prerequisites pass and enabled modules have evidence.
* When the release owner approves the recorded candidate.
* Then controlled rollout executes with monitored success and a rollback path.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an enabled optional module or core check lacks evidence.
* When go/no-go is evaluated.
* Then launch is blocked or the module is explicitly disabled before approval.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given the release manifest lists enabled settings, automation and supported clients.
* When go/no-go checks compare the manifest with the web and desktop preference gates.
* Then every exposed behavior has candidate-specific passing evidence; missing evidence blocks that surface or requires an explicitly recorded and enforced exclusion. A browser-only release does not require desktop evidence.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** relationships identify prerequisites. [FOR-121](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-121/prove-multi-user-isolation-and-crash-recovery-on-the-release-candidate>), [FOR-122](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-122/prepare-support-incident-response-and-tested-rollback-procedures>), [FOR-103](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-103/disable-unfinished-features-consistently-across-ui-and-server-routes>), [FOR-97](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-97/verify-signup-email-change-account-linking-and-workspace-invitations>), [FOR-99](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-99/rate-limit-authentication-and-expensive-operations-across-instances>), [FOR-100](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-100/delete-accounts-and-workspaces-with-auditable-purge-progress>).
Required for the core production release.

**Traceability:** review → BR-01 → AC-01/AC-02/AC-03 → corresponding ATs. Tests above are specifications, not passing results. Attach evidence for the named commit/environment when closing. Resolve open rules, confirm scope and estimate with product/development/QA; no sprint estimate or stakeholder sign-off is implied.

## Selected launch scope · 28 October 2026

User confirmed public signup, web collaboration, Forge agent, macOS distribution, and both free and paid workspace subscriptions through Polar. Agent (<issue id="b3658347-4d0a-418b-a752-41475ccb4ab7" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-85/verify-deployed-providers-sandbox-isolation-and-agent-release-evals">FOR-85</issue>), macOS (<issue id="f629ced8-5de2-4a51-9e08-34b87dcb9e3d" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-120/ship-verified-signed-macos-packages-and-recoverable-updates">FOR-120</issue>) and billing (<issue id="b44ca57a-268a-42d2-9cb3-361e17efbc9b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-112/verify-paid-subscription-lifecycle-before-enabling-billing">FOR-112</issue>) gates are now **native prerequisites** for this selected launch, in addition to the base core requirements. Email verification is required before workspace creation or agent use. Shared workspace billing limits and monthly price/currency remain under refinement in <issue id="bc3fe2de-70c0-4478-9eeb-591d4e49d054" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-109/agree-plans-entitlements-and-subscription-lifecycle-rules">FOR-109</issue>. Earlier audit statements about optional gates describe the base core-only graph before this release selection.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-SLA
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As a workspace admin, I want shared SLA rules to drive issue deadlines, so that response commitments reflect the team's policy.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Persist admin-owned policy, timezone/business hours, qualifying states, pause rules and escalation jobs; define those rules before implementation.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §03 area 30, §06. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** SLA thresholds/business hours are unresolved product choices; device clocks do not determine deadlines.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When a qualifying issue crosses an agreed threshold, the server computes the correct deadline and one escalation.
* **AC-02** — When validation/calculation runs, unauthorized edits fail and the documented timezone policy holds.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a fixture SLA with accepted business hours and timezone.
* When a qualifying issue crosses an agreed threshold.

issues.title: Migrate legacy planning content and shared views when enabled
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-IMPORT_CONTENT
**Specification status:** Proposed from the 28 October 2026 review; not implemented or accepted as a delivery commitment.

## Outcome

As an existing user, I want my preserved documents and views migrated when their modules launch, so that the core cutover does not strand earlier work.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Extend versioned import manifests/mappings to initiatives, milestones, rich-text docs/resources and view definitions; keep personal preference migration in [FOR-144](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-144/import-legacy-personal-preferences-without-overwriting-account-choices>) with its own account ownership/conflict rules; preserve excluded records. Shared-content import must not infer ownership of private preferences.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>) — §06; R2; E02. Baseline code revision: `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Recheck changed code and external state before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation rule; unresolved choices require the linked decision issue):** A deferred module's local records remain intact until its import reconciles; original ownership is not guessed.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — When the modules are enabled and an import resumes, valid records are mapped once with their relationships and original backup retained.
* **AC-02** — When the extension import validates it, the record is quarantined for review without overwriting source or broadening access.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given core migration preserved excluded documents and views.
* When the modules are enabled and an import resumes.
* Then valid records are mapped once with their relationships and original backup retained.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a rich-text record is corrupt or its sharing scope is ambiguous.
* When the extension import validates it.
* Then the record is quarantined for review without overwriting source or broadening access.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_SYNC
**Specification status:** Proposed production-readiness contract; implementation and tests remain to be completed.

## Outcome

As an account holder, I want my personal choices to follow me across sessions, so that Forge behaves consistently on each device.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Inventory every exposed setting and classify it as account-wide, workspace-specific or device-only before defining the record. Derive account identity from the authenticated session; never accept an arbitrary owner ID. Implement validated field patches with a version precondition, stable defaults and a shared web/Electron client. Preserve independent field edits, expose pending/error/retry states and reject stale conflicting writes. Partition caches and queued writes by account and workspace where applicable; discard pending writes on sign-out. Keep OS capability state local. Reuse command authorization and receipts without publishing private preference values into shared activity.

**Evidence and scope:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), §06 (persistence/migration). This self-contained story incorporates the preference requirements identified during backlog review and the user's request to remove reliance on the archived project. Detailed behavior below is a proposed implementation contract; verify the current code before estimating.

## Business rule

**BR-01:** Personal preferences never grant permissions, rewrite team policy or change another user's settings. A setting shown as saved must survive a fresh authenticated session.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given two sessions of one account and a third belonging to another account, when a preference is saved and sessions reload, then both owner sessions read the persisted value; the other account cannot read or write it.
* **AC-02** — Given two clients edit different fields and then race on the same field version, when their patches arrive out of order, then unrelated fields are preserved and stale same-field edits receive a visible conflict instead of silent overwrite.
* **AC-03** — Given a cached preference exists and a save fails offline, when the user reconnects or signs into a different account, then the owner can retry safely, unsaved state is visible, and neither cached values nor queued writes cross accounts.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given two sessions of one account and a third belonging to another account.
* When a preference is saved and sessions reload.
* Then both owner sessions read the persisted value; the other account cannot read or write it.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given two clients edit different fields and then race on the same field version.
* When their patches arrive out of order.
* Then unrelated fields are preserved and stale same-field edits receive a visible conflict instead of silent overwrite.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given a cached preference exists and a save fails offline.
* When the user reconnects or signs into a different account.
* Then the owner can retry safely, unsaved state is visible, and neither cached values nor queued writes cross accounts.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Define preference schemas, scope rules and safe runtime defaults
issues.outcome: As an existing user, I want my valid preferences preserved through upgrades, so that migration cannot corrupt my settings or prevent startup.
issues.guide: Define a versioned runtime schema and one shared defaults registry. Validate each field independently, reject protected fields server-side and ignore unknown read fields without deleting the original payload. Detect unsupported future versions and preserve their data. Before migrating local settings, preserve a recoverable original and bind import consent/ownership to the signed-in account using the migration policy. Apply idempotent field-level import only after conflict preview; never assume shared-device local data belongs to the current account. Persist checkpoints after confirmed server writes and make failed imports resumable.
issues.rule: Corrupt or unsupported preference data must not prevent startup. A migration never silently overwrites newer server settings or destroys its original source.
tests: valid fields coexist with invalid enum/type values and unknown keys
the schema is loaded
valid fields survive, invalid fields fall back independently and the original remains recoverable
legacy local values conflict with newer account values or ownership is ambiguous
migration is offered
a preview and explicit ownership/conflict choice precede writes; cancel leaves both sources unchanged
migration fails after a partial save or receives a future schema version
startup and retry occur
startup remains usable, supported imports resume once without duplicates, and unsupported data is retained
issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_SCHEMA
**Specification status:** Proposed production-readiness contract; implementation and tests remain to be completed.

## Outcome

As a user, I want invalid or future preference data handled safely, so that settings cannot break startup or leak between accounts.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Own the shared versioned runtime schema, defaults registry and scope classification: account-wide, workspace-specific or device-only. Validate fields independently, preserve unknown/future/corrupt original payloads and provide safe typed defaults. Reject protected fields at server boundaries when this contract is integrated. This is a pure schema/adapter contract with fixture tests; it does not upload or migrate browser data to an account. Account synchronization belongs to [FOR-127](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-127/keep-personal-preferences-consistent-across-authenticated-sessions>) and consent/conflict-aware legacy import to [FOR-144](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-144/import-legacy-personal-preferences-without-overwriting-account-choices>).

**Evidence and scope:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), §06 (persistence/migration). This self-contained story incorporates the preference requirements identified during backlog review and the user's request to remove reliance on the archived project. Detailed behavior below is a proposed implementation contract; verify the current code before estimating.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed):** Invalid fields fall back independently without deleting the source payload. Parsing a browser record never establishes its account ownership or triggers an upload.

## Acceptance criteria
