issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_DATES
**Specification status:** Proposed production-readiness contract; implementation and tests remain to be completed.

## Outcome

As a user, I want calendars to follow my selected first day of the week, so that dates match my planning habits.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Feed Sunday/Monday/Saturday from the shared preference selector into the common calendar abstraction. Inventory date pickers, cycle/scheduling calendars and keyboard week navigation. Keep date values, timezone and locale formatting separate from week presentation. Specify week-number conventions explicitly rather than silently changing ISO semantics.

**Evidence and scope:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), §06 (persistence/migration). This self-contained story incorporates the preference requirements identified during backlog review and the user's request to remove reliance on the archived project. Detailed behavior below is a proposed implementation contract; verify the current code before estimating.

## Business rule

**BR-01:** Changing week start changes presentation and navigation, never stored due dates or schedule execution times.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given each supported week-start value and a month/year boundary, when a calendar renders and the user navigates by week, then the first column and navigation match the selection under the documented week-number convention.
* **AC-02** — Given a mounted date picker has a selected date and locale, when the preference changes in another view, then the calendar updates without reload while preserving its selection, timezone and locale formatting.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given each supported week-start value and a month/year boundary.
* When a calendar renders and the user navigates by week.
* Then the first column and navigation match the selection under the documented week-number convention.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a mounted date picker has a selected date and locale.
* When the preference changes in another view.
* Then the calendar updates without reload while preserving its selection, timezone and locale formatting.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_NAMES
**Specification status:** Proposed production-readiness contract; implementation and tests remain to be completed.

## Outcome

As a user, I want my selected name format applied consistently, so that I can recognize people throughout Forge.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Use a shared person formatter in assignees, activity, comments, mentions, member lists and search results. Keep immutable user IDs for mention identity and command payloads; presentation is viewer-specific. Define a deterministic safe fallback for missing username/full name and disambiguation for collisions. Subscribe mounted consumers to preference updates.

**Evidence and scope:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), §06 (persistence/migration). This self-contained story incorporates the preference requirements identified during backlog review and the user's request to remove reliance on the archived project. Detailed behavior below is a proposed implementation contract; verify the current code before estimating.

## Business rule

**BR-01:** Name presentation must not change stored identity, mention targeting or permissions.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given people with complete, missing and duplicate names, when the viewer toggles Username and Full name, then every inventoried consumer updates immediately with deterministic fallback and unambiguous accessible labels.
* **AC-02** — Given two users share a displayed name, when a mention or assignee is selected, then the chosen immutable account remains the target after changing the name-format preference.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given people with complete, missing and duplicate names.
* When the viewer toggles Username and Full name.
* Then every inventoried consumer updates immediately with deterministic fallback and unambiguous accessible labels.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given two users share a displayed name.
* When a mention or assignee is selected.
* Then the chosen immutable account remains the target after changing the name-format preference.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_HOME
**Specification status:** Proposed production-readiness contract; implementation and tests remain to be completed.

## Outcome

As a user, I want new default views to open my chosen destination, so that I can start in the workspace I need.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Centralize default-route resolution for startup, an empty workspace window and new default tabs. Resolve Forge Agent, Inbox and My issues against enabled features and current membership. Prefer Forge Agent as the historical fallback only when available; otherwise choose the first authorized enabled core route. Preserve explicit URLs, auth return paths and restored navigation. Test the resolver separately from packaged desktop integration.

**Evidence and scope:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), §06 (persistence/migration). This self-contained story incorporates the preference requirements identified during backlog review and the user's request to remove reliance on the archived project. Detailed behavior below is a proposed implementation contract; verify the current code before estimating.

## Business rule

**BR-01:** A saved home preference cannot bypass feature gates or access checks, and explicit navigation always takes precedence.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given each available home choice, when Forge opens without an explicit target or opens a default tab, then the selected authorized route opens.
* **AC-02** — Given a disabled/deleted destination or an invalid stored value, when default routing is required, then a safe authorized fallback opens without redirect loops.
* **AC-03** — Given an issue deep link or auth return URL is supplied, when startup completes, then the explicit destination is preserved subject to its normal authorization.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given each available home choice.
* When Forge opens without an explicit target or opens a default tab.
* Then the selected authorized route opens.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a disabled/deleted destination or an invalid stored value.
* When default routing is required.
* Then a safe authorized fallback opens without redirect loops.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given an issue deep link or auth return URL is supplied.
* When startup completes.
* Then the explicit destination is preserved subject to its normal authorization.

## Outcome

As a writer, I want optional emoticon conversion, so that my messages follow my chosen style.

**BR-01:** Conversion is opt-in according to the persisted setting and never changes structured or protected content.

* **AC-02** — Given code, a URL, pasted structured content or active IME composition, when input reaches the editor, then content and composition are preserved with no premature transformation.

**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_SUBMIT
**Specification status:** Proposed production-readiness contract; implementation and tests remain to be completed.

## Outcome

As a keyboard user, I want my preferred submit shortcut, so that I can compose and send comments predictably.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Centralize Enter versus Command/Ctrl+Enter semantics in the shared composer. Preserve Shift+Enter as newline, suppress submission during IME composition, respect disabled/pending submission and prevent double dispatch. Document platform modifier mapping in the control and accessible hint. Retain draft content on request failure and route submission through the canonical comment command.

**Evidence and scope:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), §06 (persistence/migration). This self-contained story incorporates the preference requirements identified during backlog review and the user's request to remove reliance on the archived project. Detailed behavior below is a proposed implementation contract; verify the current code before estimating.

## Business rule

**BR-01:** One intentional submit produces at most one comment; keyboard preferences never discard an unsent draft.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given each submission mode on supported platforms, when Enter, Command/Ctrl+Enter and Shift+Enter are used, then only the configured submit action sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline and the hint matches.
* **AC-02** — Given active IME composition, an in-flight submit or a failed save, when submit keys are pressed, then composition is not submitted, pending requests do not duplicate, and failed content remains retryable.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given each submission mode on supported platforms.
* When Enter, Command/Ctrl+Enter and Shift+Enter are used.
* Then only the configured submit action sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline and the hint matches.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given active IME composition, an in-flight submit or a failed save.
* When submit keys are pressed.
* Then composition is not submitted, pending requests do not duplicate, and failed content remains retryable.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_SIDEBAR
**Specification status:** Proposed production-readiness contract; implementation and tests remain to be completed.

## Outcome

As a user, I want a configurable sidebar, so that frequently used destinations are easy to find.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Replace the Customize placeholder with a working editor for allowed visibility, ordering and badge-style settings. Persist stable destination IDs, reconcile removed/new destinations and feature gates, and keep required navigation reachable. Support keyboard reordering and announce changes. Apply immediately, include reset-to-defaults, and distinguish sidebar badge style from native dock badge mode.

**Evidence and scope:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), §06 (persistence/migration). This self-contained story incorporates the preference requirements identified during backlog review and the user's request to remove reliance on the archived project. Detailed behavior below is a proposed implementation contract; verify the current code before estimating.

## Business rule

**BR-01:** Customization affects navigation presentation only; it cannot expose unauthorized destinations or make settings inaccessible.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given a user edits supported visibility, order and badge style, when changes save and another session opens, then the same valid layout appears and mounted navigation updates immediately.
* **AC-02** — Given keyboard-only interaction at the minimum supported width, when items are reordered and defaults restored, then focus stays usable, ordering is announced and reset restores the defined default layout.
* **AC-03** — Given a saved item loses access or is feature-disabled, when the sidebar reconciles, then the destination is removed safely without exposing content or stranding navigation.

* When items are reordered and defaults restored.
* Then focus stays usable, ordering is announced and reset restores the defined default layout.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given a saved item loses access or is feature-disabled.
* When the sidebar reconciles.
* Then the destination is removed safely without exposing content or stranding navigation.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_LINKS
**Specification status:** Proposed production-readiness contract; implementation and tests remain to be completed.

## Outcome

As a desktop user, I want Forge links to respect my opening preference and Manage on Web to work, so that I can move between supported clients safely.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Replace Manage on Web with the canonical HTTPS settings destination for the active environment. Honor Open in desktop app only for allowlisted Forge URLs through the existing safe protocol/IPC boundary. Preserve workspace/resource paths and return through normal authentication when needed; never put bearer tokens in URLs. If the app is absent or browser launch is declined, keep a usable web fallback and avoid redirect loops. Capability state is device-local.

**Evidence and scope:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), §06 (persistence/migration), area 31 and §13 (desktop/quality). This self-contained story incorporates the preference requirements identified during backlog review and the user's request to remove reliance on the archived project. Detailed behavior below is a proposed implementation contract; verify the current code before estimating.

## Business rule

**BR-01:** Link routing never bypasses authentication or opens arbitrary origins/protocols through the desktop bridge.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given desktop opening enabled or disabled and an allowed Forge resource link, when the link is opened, then the chosen supported client receives the same target with normal authentication and authorization.
* **AC-02** — Given an absent desktop app, browser-only session or rejected protocol launch, when the user opens a link or Manage on Web, then the real web destination remains usable without looping or pretending success.
* **AC-03** — Given a foreign origin, unsafe protocol or token-bearing target, when link routing validates the request, then unsafe routing is rejected and no credentials are forwarded.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given desktop opening enabled or disabled and an allowed Forge resource link.
* When the link is opened.
* Then the chosen supported client receives the same target with normal authentication and authorization.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an absent desktop app, browser-only session or rejected protocol launch.
* When the user opens a link or Manage on Web.
* Then the real web destination remains usable without looping or pretending success.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given a foreign origin, unsafe protocol or token-bearing target.
* When link routing validates the request.
* Then unsafe routing is rejected and no credentials are forwarded.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_BADGES
**Specification status:** Proposed production-readiness contract; implementation and tests remain to be completed.

## Outcome

As a desktop user, I want reliable unread badges, so that I can notice activity without an unwanted count.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Map Off, Unread indicator and Unread count through the narrow native host bridge. Derive state from canonical unread notifications for the active authenticated scope; specify count cap and overflow display before coding. Reconcile live updates and reconnects, and clear on sign-out/account changes. Unsupported host capabilities use an explicit no-op fallback. Avoid notification content in IPC payloads.

**Evidence and scope:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), §06 (persistence/migration), area 31 and §13 (desktop/quality). This self-contained story incorporates the preference requirements identified during backlog review and the user's request to remove reliance on the archived project. Detailed behavior below is a proposed implementation contract; verify the current code before estimating.

## Business rule

**BR-01:** Off always clears native badges; an account switch must never briefly show another account's unread state.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given unread notifications and each badge mode, when the preference changes or a notification is read, then Off clears, indicator displays where supported and count matches the bounded authorized unread total.
* **AC-02** — Given a disconnected session then a different account signs in, when badge state reconciles, then stale counts clear before the new account's state appears.
* **AC-03** — Given a host without native badge support, when an unread update arrives, then the application remains usable with a safe no-op and no bridge error.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given unread notifications and each badge mode.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* When badge state reconciles.
* Then stale counts clear before the new account's state appears.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_SPELLING
**Specification status:** Proposed implementation contract; no passing result or delivery commitment is implied.

## Outcome

As a writer, I want supported web spellchecking to follow my preference, so that corrections behave predictably while I write.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Map the preference to supported editable web surfaces. Update mounted editors and initialize new editors with the latest value without reloading the page. Document browser capability differences and avoid promising control over browser-level behavior the app cannot govern. Preserve content, selection and the browser's available context-menu suggestions. Native Electron lifecycle and packaged-app verification are separate desktop work.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), area 31 and §13 (desktop). Requirements refined after removal of the archived preference project; verify current code before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01:** Changing spelling behavior never resets editor content; browser limitations are explicit. Web completion does not require a native application build.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given mounted and newly opened supported web editors, when spellchecking is toggled without reloading, then the toggle is reflected where supported and content/selection remain intact.
* **AC-02** — Given a browser with spelling suggestions and a misspelled word, when the browser context menu is opened while spelling is enabled, then available browser suggestions remain usable without application interception.
* **AC-03** — Given a browser cannot honor the setting, when the control is rendered or changed, then the limitation is explicit and no misleading success action is presented.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given mounted and newly opened supported web editors.
* When spellchecking is toggled without reloading.
* Then the toggle is reflected where supported and content/selection remain intact.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a browser with spelling suggestions and a misspelled word.
* When the browser context menu is opened while spelling is enabled.
* Then available browser suggestions remain usable without application interception.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given a browser cannot honor the setting.
* When the control is rendered or changed.
* Then the limitation is explicit and no misleading success action is presented.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_AUTO_CREATE
**Specification status:** Proposed production-readiness contract; implementation and tests remain to be completed.

## Outcome

As a contributor, I want new issues assigned to me when I opt in, so that work I create is immediately owned.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Resolve the human actor's server-side preference inside the canonical create command used by all composers and enabled API/tool adapters. Distinguish omitted assignee from an explicit null/unassigned choice; validate membership and assignment permission. Determine behavior for service credentials or delegated actors without a human preference as an explicit scope rule; default to no personal automation. Store resulting assignment and attributable activity atomically with the issue, not as a second client patch.

**Evidence and scope:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), §06 (persistence/migration). This self-contained story incorporates the preference requirements identified during backlog review and the user's request to remove reliance on the archived project. Detailed behavior below is a proposed implementation contract; verify the current code before estimating.

## Business rule

**BR-01:** Automation applies only when enabled and assignment was omitted. An explicit assignee or explicit unassigned choice always wins.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given an eligible human actor with auto-assignment enabled and omitted assignment, when any enabled creation entry point executes, then exactly one issue is created assigned to that actor with attributable history.
* **AC-02** — Given the preference is disabled, assignment is explicit, or the caller lacks an eligible human actor, when creation executes, then the explicit value is preserved and no unauthorized personal assignment is inferred.
* **AC-03** — Given a creation request is retried or actor membership changes, when the command is evaluated, then retries return the same committed outcome and current assignment authorization is enforced.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an eligible human actor with auto-assignment enabled and omitted assignment.
* When any enabled creation entry point executes.
* Then exactly one issue is created assigned to that actor with attributable history.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given the preference is disabled, assignment is explicit, or the caller lacks an eligible human actor.
* When creation executes.
* Then the explicit value is preserved and no unauthorized personal assignment is inferred.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given a creation request is retried or actor membership changes.
* When the command is evaluated.
* Then retries return the same committed outcome and current assignment authorization is enforced.

## Dependencies and completion

**Type:** Release gate · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_DESKTOP_GATE
**Specification status:** Proposed production-readiness contract; implementation and tests remain to be completed.

## Outcome

As a macOS release owner, I want preference behavior verified in packaged Forge, so that desktop users receive working native integrations.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Run the accepted web preference matrix in production-configured signed candidate artifacts for each supported architecture. For selected native controls require [FOR-135](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-135/respect-desktop-link-choices-and-open-real-web-settings>), [FOR-136](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-136/drive-desktop-badges-from-authorized-unread-notification-state>), [FOR-143](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-143/apply-native-spellchecking-preferences-in-packaged-electron>) and [FOR-146](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-146/deliver-authorized-native-notifications-with-safe-deep-links>) evidence as applicable. Test startup/new tabs, safe handoff, account switching/restart/update and capability fallbacks. Unselected controls must be explicitly unavailable under [FOR-20](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates>); native stories remain planned, not silently dropped. Security evidence in [FOR-119](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-119/verify-desktop-login-navigation-and-ipc-trust-boundaries>) is mandatory. **Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_NATIVE_SPELLING
**Specification status:** Proposed implementation contract; no passing result or delivery commitment is implied.

## Outcome

As a desktop writer, I want the native spellchecker to follow my preference, so that spelling corrections work without restarting Forge.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Connect the validated preference to the Electron spellchecker lifecycle through the trusted host bridge. Update supported existing editors/sessions and initialize new ones without restarting the app. Keep context-menu suggestions available when enabled, preserve editor content/selection and expose any OS limitation clearly. Limit IPC payloads to validated preference values and authorized sender contexts. The shared web editor setting is implemented separately; this story covers native integration only.

**Evidence:** [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>), area 30 (preferences), area 31 and §13 (desktop). Requirements refined after removal of the archived preference project; verify current code before implementation.

## Business rule

**BR-01:** A renderer cannot use the spelling preference bridge to access arbitrary native capabilities; toggling spelling never discards drafts.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given a packaged candidate with mounted and newly created editors, when native spellchecking is toggled, then supported native spelling behavior updates without app restart and draft content/selection remain unchanged.
* **AC-02** — Given native spellchecking enabled and a misspelled word, when the desktop context menu opens, then native suggestions remain available and applying one preserves the expected editor history.
* **AC-03** — Given an untrusted sender, invalid value or unsupported OS capability, when the bridge receives a spelling update, then invalid privileged requests are rejected and documented capability fallbacks preserve a usable editor.

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a packaged candidate with mounted and newly created editors.
* When native spellchecking is toggled.
* Then supported native spelling behavior updates without app restart and draft content/selection remain unchanged.

* When the desktop context menu opens.
* Then native suggestions remain available and applying one preserves the expected editor history.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given an untrusted sender, invalid value or unsupported OS capability.
* When the bridge receives a spelling update.
* Then invalid privileged requests are rejected and documented capability fallbacks preserve a usable editor.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-PREF_IMPORT
**Specification status:** Proposed during the 28 October 2026 whole-backlog audit. Implementation and acceptance results remain unverified.

## Outcome

As an existing user, I want to review and recover my old preferences during account migration, so that shared-browser data cannot overwrite my choices.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Extract account import from the runtime-schema story. Preserve a recoverable source payload and fingerprint; show destination account, supported fields, conflicts and excluded future-version data. Require explicit ownership/conflict choices before upload. Apply version-checked field patches with checkpointed idempotency; a failed or canceled import must leave the source intact. New accounts and valid runtime preference consumers do not wait for this migration flow.

**Evidence:** Scope split from <issue id="5478636d-5625-426b-9466-3e9d16dca57b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-128/validate-and-safely-migrate-personal-preference-schemas">FOR-128</issue>; source review §06 and its ownership-aware browser migration contract. [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>). Baseline repository revision remains `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Review current code before implementation; reuse working behavior.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation contract):** Possession of a browser payload does not prove account ownership. Import never silently replaces a newer server value.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given a shared browser has local settings conflicting with account values, when the signed-in user previews import, then destination, conflicts and exclusions are shown before any upload and cancel changes neither source.
* **AC-02** — Given a confirmed import stops after some fields commit, when the same manifest resumes, then confirmed fields are not duplicated, concurrent server edits receive a conflict, and remaining fields can resume.
* **AC-03** — Given a corrupt/future schema or changed source fingerprint is encountered, when migration loads or retries, then original bytes remain recoverable and the application still starts with validated defaults.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a shared browser has local settings conflicting with account values.
* When the signed-in user previews import.
* Then destination, conflicts and exclusions are shown before any upload and cancel changes neither source.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a confirmed import stops after some fields commit.
* When the same manifest resumes.
* Then confirmed fields are not duplicated, concurrent server edits receive a conflict, and remaining fields can resume.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given a corrupt/future schema or changed source fingerprint is encountered.
* When migration loads or retries.
* Then original bytes remain recoverable and the application still starts with validated defaults.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-127](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-127/keep-personal-preferences-consistent-across-authenticated-sessions>), [FOR-22](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-22/decide-ownership-and-conflict-rules-for-legacy-browser-data>).

Required before enabling this slice. An explicit release-scope exclusion must be enforced in UI, direct routes and background execution; it does not mark unfinished implementation complete.

Attach evidence for the named commit/environment and each AC/AT pair; desktop checks also identify the packaged artifact. Resolve named policy choices before implementing them. No deadline, estimate, assignee or passing test result is implied.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-NOTIFICATION_POLICY
**Specification status:** Proposed during the 28 October 2026 whole-backlog audit. Implementation and acceptance results remain unverified.

## Outcome

As a user, I want notification choices to control actual delivery across sessions, so that Forge respects which updates I want.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Use the existing notification-preferences schema as an inventory, not proof of delivery. Persist validated per-user channel/type choices and priority-inbox classification through authenticated commands. Distinguish issue subscription (owned by the subscription story), channel consent and mandatory service/security messages; define their precedence explicitly before enabling channels. Recheck current preferences and access when a queued optional delivery executes. Reuse account storage conventions without requiring cosmetic preference synchronization. Do not implement mobile or Slack delivery merely because controls exist: make unsupported channels unavailable under the release manifest.

**Evidence:** Source review §10; checked apps/forge/src/lib/notification-preferences.ts persists localStorage only and exposes desktop/mobile/email/slack controls. No delivery defect is assumed beyond this observed boundary. [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>). Baseline repository revision remains `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Review current code before implementation; reuse working behavior.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation contract):** Channel settings do not grant resource access. Turning off optional email/native delivery must not suppress essential account-recovery mail or delete the underlying inbox item.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given one account opens two sessions, when it disables comment email and changes priority-inbox types in one session, then both sessions read the same persisted choices and the inbox classification follows the selected types.
* **AC-02** — Given an optional email/native notification is queued and its preference is disabled or access is revoked, when the worker evaluates delivery, then delivery is withheld according to the recorded precedence while authorized inbox history remains.
* **AC-03** — Given mobile or Slack has no configured production adapter, when the settings screen and direct preference endpoint are used, then the channel cannot be represented as working and no successful-delivery state is fabricated.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given one account opens two sessions.
* When it disables comment email and changes priority-inbox types in one session.
* Then both sessions read the same persisted choices and the inbox classification follows the selected types.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given an optional email/native notification is queued and its preference is disabled or access is revoked.
* When the worker evaluates delivery.
* Then delivery is withheld according to the recorded precedence while authorized inbox history remains.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given mobile or Slack has no configured production adapter.
* When the settings screen and direct preference endpoint are used.
* Then the channel cannot be represented as working and no successful-delivery state is fabricated.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-65](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-65/deliver-authorized-issue-events-into-a-shared-inbox>).

Required before enabling this slice. An explicit release-scope exclusion must be enforced in UI, direct routes and background execution; it does not mark unfinished implementation complete.

issues.outcome: As a desktop user, I want permitted updates to appear as native notifications, so that I can return to the right work when Forge is not focused.
issues.guide: Implement the native notification adapter separately from dock badges. Consume authorized canonical inbox events with stable delivery IDs, current channel/type settings and OS permission/capability checks. Define foreground behavior and lock-screen preview policy in the release manifest; default to minimized content until explicitly configured. Notification clicks route through the existing validated deep-link resolver and reauthorize current account/workspace. Deduplicate replay, clear pending native deliveries on logout and provide a truthful permission-denied state. The packaged security/release gates remain mandatory before distribution but do not block implementation of the adapter.

**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_RETENTION
**Specification status:** Proposed during the 28 October 2026 whole-backlog audit. Implementation and acceptance results remain unverified.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want agent conversation data to expire according to the recorded policy, so that prompts, results and files do not remain indefinitely.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Inventory runs, messages/events, summaries, artifacts, attachments and approval/receipt references. Implement bounded scheduled cleanup for applicable records, preserving active runs and durable deduplication/audit guarantees for the accepted retry window. Reuse shared file tombstones/deletion workers for bytes; this story owns agent-specific eligibility and scheduler wiring, not a second blob sweeper. Checkpoint/retry failed batches, prevent archived or replayed data from resurrecting expired content, expose a safe expired-history state and alert on missed successful sweeps. Prove the actual scheduler invokes the job with test fixtures.

**Evidence:** Source review §10/§12; checked sweep-agent-retention.ts invokes artifact/attachment sweeps only and the review identifies missing agent retention scheduling. FILE_RETENTION owns shared object deletion; this story owns agent lifecycle orchestration. [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>). Baseline repository revision remains `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Review current code before implementation; reuse working behavior.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation contract):** Conversation expiry cannot invalidate an active run or erase evidence still required to reconcile an ambiguous command. Each class follows its accepted retention policy.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given expired conversation fixtures, an active run and unexpired receipts, when the scheduled cleanup runs twice, then only policy-eligible records disappear once, active work and required receipts survive and history shows a safe expiry state.
* **AC-02** — Given a worker stops after database cleanup while a file delete fails, when the next scheduled attempt resumes, then durable checkpoints/tombstones complete remaining cleanup without losing progress or reviving data.
* **AC-03** — Given no successful sweep occurs within the accepted freshness window, when monitoring evaluates the job, then an actionable alert identifies the affected scheduler and last successful checkpoint.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given expired conversation fixtures, an active run and unexpired receipts.
* When the scheduled cleanup runs twice.
* Then only policy-eligible records disappear once, active work and required receipts survive and history shows a safe expiry state.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a worker stops after database cleanup while a file delete fails.
* When the next scheduled attempt resumes.
* Then durable checkpoints/tombstones complete remaining cleanup without losing progress or reviving data.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given no successful sweep occurs within the accepted freshness window.
* When monitoring evaluates the job.
* Then an actionable alert identifies the affected scheduler and last successful checkpoint.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-77](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-77/keep-one-run-execution-alive-across-stream-reconnects-and-redeploys>), [FOR-37](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-37/reconcile-orphaned-files-and-retry-durable-deletion>).

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-MODEL_LIFECYCLE
**Specification status:** Proposed during the 28 October 2026 whole-backlog audit. Implementation and acceptance results remain unverified.

## Outcome

As an authorized user, I want model connections to expose truthful availability and credential ownership, so that I can select a usable provider without leaking credentials.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Verify and complete the existing ModelConnectionService and client flow rather than rebuilding them. Test personal versus workspace ownership, create/discovery, health refresh, stale model catalogs, credential replacement where offered, delete/revoke and workspace provider policy. Keep raw secrets server-side and clarify any broker-owned desktop credentials. Validate custom endpoints again on actual discovery/invocation, including DNS/redirect changes and bounded responses; creation-time checks alone are not release evidence. Define in-flight run behavior on disconnect under the accepted agent policy. Disabled providers and unsupported execution modes must remain unavailable.

**Evidence:** Source review area 20, §08/§12; checked model-connection-service.server.ts already implements create/list/refresh/delete and endpoint validation. This is verification and gap closure, not a claim those features are absent. [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>). Baseline repository revision remains `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Review current code before implementation; reuse working behavior.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation contract):** Keyring rotation changes encryption keys; this story governs user-visible provider credential/connection lifecycle. Neither test credentials nor another user's personal connection may leak through catalogs or errors.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given owner Alice, member Bob and a personal plus a workspace connection, when both users list, refresh and attempt updates, then only authorized connections/actions succeed, model status reflects real test-provider results and summaries contain no raw credentials.
* **AC-02** — Given a provider credential is revoked or a connection deleted, when catalog refresh and a new run admission occur, then a clear reconnect/unavailable state appears and no new invocation uses the revoked connection; in-flight work follows the recorded policy.
* **AC-03** — Given a custom endpoint resolves or redirects to a forbidden address after initial validation, when discovery or invocation is attempted, then the request is blocked before private-network access and diagnostics reveal no credential.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given owner Alice, member Bob and a personal plus a workspace connection.
* When both users list, refresh and attempt updates.
* Then only authorized connections/actions succeed, model status reflects real test-provider results and summaries contain no raw credentials.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a provider credential is revoked or a connection deleted.
* When catalog refresh and a new run admission occur.
* Then a clear reconnect/unavailable state appears and no new invocation uses the revoked connection; in-flight work follows the recorded policy.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given a custom endpoint resolves or redirects to a forbidden address after initial validation.
* When discovery or invocation is attempted.
* Then the request is blocked before private-network access and diagnostics reveal no credential.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>), [FOR-70](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-70/rotate-encrypted-provider-credentials-without-losing-access>), [FOR-75](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-75/define-provider-spending-and-execution-admission-policy>).

issues.title: Enforce browser request origins and session trust boundaries
issues.outcome: As an account holder, I want browser session writes restricted to trusted request contexts, so that another website cannot act through my signed-in session.
issues.guide: Inventory cookie-authenticated writes, auth callbacks and browser/API transports. Verify the installed auth framework's CSRF/origin safeguards, trusted-origin configuration and session-cookie behavior; fix uncovered routes without replacing working controls. Use explicit per-environment origin/redirect policy and credentialed CORS where intentionally supported. Test the actual candidate with two origins, direct server mutations and auth-return paths. Keep CSRF/session-origin checks distinct from Actor/resource authorization and include logout invalidation. Do not mark controls insecure solely because configuration was not previously audited.
issues.rule: Authenticated cookies do not authorize cross-origin mutation. Allowed transport origins do not replace resource permission checks.

issues.description:
**Type:** Technical enabler · **Release scope:** Core production · **Backlog key:** FPR-BROWSER_SECURITY
**Specification status:** Proposed during the 28 October 2026 whole-backlog audit. Implementation and acceptance results remain unverified.

## Outcome

As an account holder, I want browser session writes restricted to trusted request contexts, so that another website cannot act through my signed-in session.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Inventory cookie-authenticated writes, auth callbacks and browser/API transports. Verify the installed auth framework's CSRF/origin safeguards, trusted-origin configuration and session-cookie behavior; fix uncovered routes without replacing working controls. Use explicit per-environment origin/redirect policy and credentialed CORS where intentionally supported. Test the actual candidate with two origins, direct server mutations and auth-return paths. Keep CSRF/session-origin checks distinct from Actor/resource authorization and include logout invalidation. Do not mark controls insecure solely because configuration was not previously audited.

**Evidence:** Source review §12 explicitly requires CSRF/origin and CORS tests; current auth.ts has trustedOrigins, but no existing backlog item owned the complete browser request-boundary acceptance matrix. [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>). Baseline repository revision remains `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Review current code before implementation; reuse working behavior.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation contract):** Authenticated cookies do not authorize cross-origin mutation. Allowed transport origins do not replace resource permission checks.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given a signed-in browser and an untrusted origin, when that origin submits a state-changing request using the victim's session context, then the mutation is rejected with no data change; the same authorized action from the trusted application succeeds.
* **AC-02** — Given production and staging have different configured origins, when credentialed cross-origin requests, preflights and auth-return redirects are tested, then only explicitly supported origins/targets are accepted and no arbitrary redirect or credential exposure occurs.
* **AC-03** — Given the user signs out and a prior session cookie is replayed, when a protected browser request is made, then access is denied and the deployed cookie/session settings match the documented transport contract.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a signed-in browser and an untrusted origin.
* When that origin submits a state-changing request using the victim's session context.
* Then the mutation is rejected with no data change; the same authorized action from the trusted application succeeds.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given production and staging have different configured origins.
* When credentialed cross-origin requests, preflights and auth-return redirects are tested.
* Then only explicitly supported origins/targets are accepted and no arbitrary redirect or credential exposure occurs.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given the user signs out and a prior session cookie is replayed.
* When a protected browser request is made.
* Then access is denied and the deployed cookie/session settings match the documented transport contract.

## Dependencies and completion

Baseline repository revision remains `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Review current code before implementation; reuse working behavior.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation contract):** Authenticated cookies do not authorize cross-origin mutation. Allowed transport origins do not replace resource permission checks.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given a signed-in browser and an untrusted origin, when that origin submits a state-changing request using the victim's session context, then the mutation is rejected with no data change; the same authorized action from the trusted application succeeds.
* **AC-02** — Given production and staging have different configured origins, when credentialed cross-origin requests, preflights and auth-return redirects are tested, then only explicitly supported origins/targets are accepted and no arbitrary redirect or credential exposure occurs.
* **AC-03** — Given the user signs out and a prior session cookie is replayed, when a protected browser request is made, then access is denied and the deployed cookie/session settings match the documented transport contract.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given a signed-in browser and an untrusted origin.
* When that origin submits a state-changing request using the victim's session context.
* Then the mutation is rejected with no data change; the same authorized action from the trusted application succeeds.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given production and staging have different configured origins.
* When credentialed cross-origin requests, preflights and auth-return redirects are tested.
* Then only explicitly supported origins/targets are accepted and no arbitrary redirect or credential exposure occurs.

**AT-03 → AC-03**

* Given the user signs out and a prior session cookie is replayed.
* When a protected browser request is made.
* Then access is denied and the deployed cookie/session settings match the documented transport contract.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-26](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-26/validate-service-specific-production-configuration-at-startup>), [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>).

## Outcome

As an API client developer, I want access to enabled advanced planning records, so that my integration can work with initiatives and project milestones.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Extract initiatives, project milestones/updates and their authorized aggregates from the basic planning API contract. Reuse domain services and scope names, document schemas, version preconditions and bounded pagination. Each endpoint requires its product module to be enabled; denied/private aggregates must not expose hidden counts. Basic projects/cycles/labels can ship before this extension. Supply deployed contract examples to the API enablement matrix.

**Evidence:** Scope split from <issue id="2476ea46-b0d5-4240-bd49-e672604c1268" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-88/expose-authorized-projects-cycles-labels-and-initiatives">FOR-88</issue>; source review areas 8–10 and §11. ## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation contract):** Enabling the basic planning API does not implicitly expose initiatives or advanced project fields.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given advanced planning enabled for workspace A and a scoped client, when the client reads and updates an initiative or milestone, then canonical results and conflict rules match the UI with attributable changes.
* **AC-02** — Given a private linked project or disabled advanced module, when the client requests records or rollups, then private identifiers/counts do not leak and disabled endpoints return the documented unavailable response.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given advanced planning enabled for workspace A and a scoped client.
* When the client reads and updates an initiative or milestone.
* Then canonical results and conflict rules match the UI with attributable changes.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given a private linked project or disabled advanced module.
* When the client requests records or rollups.
* Then private identifiers/counts do not leak and disabled endpoints return the documented unavailable response.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-88](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-88/expose-authorized-projects-cycles-labels-and-initiatives>), [FOR-59](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-59/plan-initiatives-with-authorized-project-membership-and-rollups>).

**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated · **Backlog key:** FPR-AGENT_CONTENT_READS
**Specification status:** Proposed during the 28 October 2026 whole-backlog audit. Implementation and acceptance results remain unverified.

## Outcome

As a user, I want Forge to use documents I can access, so that its answers can cite my team's written context.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Extract document reading from the multi-domain agent story. Add bounded typed document retrieval/search through the canonical document service with revision/source references and current visibility checks. Treat rich text and embedded instructions as untrusted context, not tool authority. Gate this capability independently; planning/inbox and Calls tools need not wait for documents. Document writes remain outside this read-only slice.

**Evidence:** Scope split from <issue id="963d5369-aed0-436d-8ff6-4359f2ec3e78" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-82/let-forge-use-authorized-cycles-documents-inbox-and-call-recaps">FOR-82</issue>; source review areas 12/18 and §11. Document capability is independently gated. [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>). Baseline repository revision remains `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Review current code before implementation; reuse working behavior.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation contract):** Retrieval and citations cannot disclose a private document's title, excerpt or existence to an unauthorized caller.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given Alice can read document D at revision R, when Forge answers a question using D, then the answer uses a bounded authorized result and cites the canonical document and revision.
* **AC-02** — Given access is revoked, the document module is disabled or the document includes hostile instructions, when retrieval is attempted, then unavailable content is withheld and document text cannot expand tool permissions.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given Alice can read document D at revision R.
* When Forge answers a question using D.
* Then the answer uses a bounded authorized result and cites the canonical document and revision.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Given access is revoked, the document module is disabled or the document includes hostile instructions.
* When retrieval is attempted.
* Then unavailable content is withheld and document text cannot expand tool permissions.

## Dependencies and completion

Native **blocked by** prerequisites: [FOR-81](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-81/let-forge-search-create-and-update-shared-issues-and-projects>), [FOR-61](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-61/create-and-edit-shared-documents-with-revision-conflicts>).

**Specification status:** Proposed during the 28 October 2026 whole-backlog audit. Implementation and acceptance results remain unverified.

## Outcome

As a user, I want Forge to use call recaps I can access, so that decisions from meetings inform my work.

## Context and implementation guidelines

Extract Calls reading from the multi-domain agent story. Retrieve bounded recap/action context through the Calls service with provider/call identity, freshness and source links. Distinguish raw transcripts from retained derived data according to the retention policy, recheck current visibility, and treat transcript text as untrusted. Keep Calls disabled from tool discovery when its module is unavailable. No Call mutation or conversion-to-issue shortcut is introduced here.

**Evidence:** Scope split from <issue id="963d5369-aed0-436d-8ff6-4359f2ec3e78" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-82/let-forge-use-authorized-cycles-documents-inbox-and-call-recaps">FOR-82</issue>; source review areas 14/18 and §10/§11. Keeps provider OAuth and Calls sync off the planning/inbox tool path. [Production readiness review](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/production-readiness-review-28-october-2026-298d41b9c5e3>). Baseline repository revision remains `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`. Review current code before implementation; reuse working behavior.

## Business rule

**BR-01 (proposed implementation contract):** Having agent access does not grant meeting access, and stale or expired meeting context must never be presented as current.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-01** — Given an accessible call with a current recap, when Forge answers a meeting question, then only authorized bounded recap data is used with a canonical source and freshness information.
* **AC-02** — Given a private/expired call or disabled Calls module, when the same retrieval is requested, then protected metadata is withheld and unavailable or stale context is handled truthfully.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01**

* Given an accessible call with a current recap.
* When Forge answers a meeting question.
* Then only authorized bounded recap data is used with a canonical source and freshness information.

**AT-02 → AC-02**

* Then protected metadata is withheld and unavailable or stale context is handled truthfully.

## Dependencies and completion

issues.title: Enforce the Free workspace member limit across every join path
issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated; required for the selected public Free + paid launch.

**Source:** User decisions and supplied Linear Plans screenshots, 28 October 2026. [Forge launch plan matrix](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b>). This is an implementation specification; test examples below are not execution evidence.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want membership to respect my plan's member limit, so that inviting or joining a workspace cannot exceed its capacity.

## Business rules

**BR-01 — user-confirmed:** Free allows at most 5 active members, including owner/admin. Pending invitations do not count. Starter/Plus have no commercial member cap; independent abuse/operational controls still apply.
**BR-02 — implementation rule:** Recheck trusted plan and active count atomically with member insertion on invitation acceptance, domain join, invite link, direct admin addition and import. UI checks alone are insufficient. Do not accept client counts/plan names or unchecked legacy aliases.
**BR-03 — user-confirmed transition:** Returning to Free above five active members preserves existing member access and blocks new joins while the count is five or more. Below five, new membership may be admitted up to the cap. Do not evict members, force selection of five, erase consumption or treat an existing-member retry as a new join. Normal authorization and explicit removal still apply.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC-01 → BR-01:** Adding a fifth active Free member succeeds; adding a sixth is rejected without membership, entitlement or billed-seat changes. Pending invitations do not consume slots.
**AC-02 → BR-02:** All enabled membership creation paths apply the same capacity and authorization policy. Concurrent accepts cannot exceed five; retries do not double-count an existing member.
**AC-03 → BR-01/02:** A Starter/Plus workspace can add a sixth member with current server-confirmed access; a client plan override or cross-workspace attempt cannot bypass Free capacity.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01:** Given a Free workspace with owner + three accepted members and two pending invitations, when one invitation is accepted, then it has exactly five active members; accepting the other is refused without side effects.
**AT-02 → AC-02:** Given four active Free members, when two distinct accept/join requests run concurrently in real Postgres, then exactly one creates membership and the total is five. Replay the successful request and assert no extra member.
**AT-03 → AC-02/03:** Given fixtures for each enabled join/admin/import path and a forged paid plan in a request, when a sixth member is attempted on Free, then every path refuses; repeat on a genuinely paid workspace and assert success. Verify cross-workspace denial.

## Dependencies and completion

[FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>) coordinates broader resource authorization. It is related rather than a blanket completion blocker: all enabled membership entry points have their own verified current authorization checks; unrelated canonical issue/project enforcement can finish independently. Coordinate with [FOR-111](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-111/reconcile-payment-events-into-server-enforced-entitlements>)'s authoritative entitlement projection and [FOR-97](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-97/verify-signup-email-change-account-linking-and-workspace-invitations>)'s verified invitation lifecycle; those entire stories are not new blanket blockers for contract preparation. Use a transaction/lock or equivalent database invariant, not a Better Auth count check followed by an independent insert. Attach real database/concurrency and route evidence before Done.

## Current preparation

Atomic membership enforcement and enabled auth/join paths are implemented and verified on isolated PostgreSQL, including the freshly migrated persistent staging database. Production rollout remains separately release-gated; this issue's completion does not certify live paid entitlements or production deployment.

### Plan-aware allowance and admission preparation verified · 28 October 2026

Implemented locally (uncommitted/undeployed, base `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`): fixed Free US$5/workspace pool, paid per-member pool, explicit standard-plan validation, no usable Free overage even with stale paid opt-in/authorization, Free five-member capacity arithmetic with batch/overflow checks, and trusted plan/feature/payer usage classification. Paid Calls/Signals and BYOK bypass the allowance constraint and reserve **zero** customer allowance even when the agent pool is exhausted; independent operational admission still applies. Free Calls/Signals consume its fixed pool. Internal provider costs are not erased.

Verification: **9 billing test files / 155 tests passed**, app TypeScript, changed-file ESLint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Tests cover fixed Free pool through membership changes, stale paid overage refusal, fifth/sixth/batch membership boundaries, paid membership, unknown plan/feature/payer rejection, paid Calls/Signals after exhaustion and BYOK exclusion.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated; required for the selected public Free + paid launch.

**Source:** User decisions and supplied Linear Plans screenshots, 28 October 2026. [Forge launch plan matrix](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b>). This is an implementation specification; test examples below are not execution evidence.

## Outcome

As a workspace owner, I want team creation to respect my plan, so that I can see when an upgrade is needed without losing existing teams.

## Business rules

**BR-01 — screenshot allocation:** Free permits 2 teams; Starter permits 5; Plus/Enterprise have no commercial team cap. Screenshot Basic maps to Starter and Business to Plus; user Free overrides remain authoritative.
**BR-02 — implementation rule:** Authorize and check trusted plan/current team count in the same transaction as creation or bulk import. Server state, not a browser plan/count, determines access.
**BR-03 — confirmed downgrade behavior, 29 October 2026:** Keep existing teams accessible when a downgrade exceeds its new team cap. Block new creation/import and restoring archived teams while the resulting active-team count would exceed the cap; existing editing, reading and archiving remain available subject to normal permissions. Count active teams across the entire workspace, including private teams, without exposing hidden team details/counts in capacity errors. Archived teams do not consume active capacity; restoring one is an admission. Do not delete or conceal existing teams on downgrade. Sub-team depth follows the plan matrix separately.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC-01 → BR-01:** Free can create its second team and cannot create a third; Starter can create its fifth and cannot create a sixth, with an actionable capacity response and no partial team/member/label records.
**AC-02 → BR-02:** Concurrent creation/import through every enabled transport cannot exceed the relevant cap, and retries do not create duplicates.
**AC-03 → BR-01/02:** Plus can create a sixth team subject to authorization/operational policy; a forged Plus plan or cross-workspace request does not bypass another workspace's cap.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01:** Given Free with one team and Starter with four teams, when a team is created twice, then the first succeeds and the next is refused with unchanged persisted state.
**AT-02 → AC-02:** Given Free with one team, when two distinct team creations execute concurrently against real Postgres, then one succeeds and the total is two; replay the successful command and assert no extra team.

issues.description:
**Type:** User story · **Release scope:** Feature gated; required for the selected public Free + paid launch.

## Outcome

As a verified workspace owner, I want to try Starter or Plus for 14 days without entering payment details, so that I can evaluate the plan and decide whether to upgrade manually.

## Sources and business rules

Source: user decisions on 28 October 2026 and [Forge launch plans](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/forge-launch-plans-entitlements-and-usage-policy-026e65a8947b>).
**BR-01 — user-confirmed:** Starter and Plus trials last 14 days. Trial start collects no payment details, creates no provider subscription/checkout and creates no authority to charge.
**BR-02 — user-confirmed:** Expiry cannot automatically charge; paid access requires a manual owner/admin upgrade through hosted checkout followed by reconciled provider confirmation. Returning to Free preserves existing member access and blocks new joins at five or more.
**BR-03 — user-confirmed usage:** The 14-day trial has one fixed US$5 workspace pool, independent of membership. Agent, Calls and Signals consume it; BYOK remains excluded. No paid overage or automatic replenishment is authorized during the trial. Eligibility/redemption, cross-workspace anti-abuse and plan-switch/carryover behavior remain open; do not infer repeat eligibility or extensions.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC-01 → BR-01:** Eligible trial start records trusted workspace/plan and immutable server timestamps for 14 days without a Polar checkout/subscription or payment details. Retries cannot restart the window.
**AC-02 → BR-01/02:** At the exact expiry boundary trial-only entitlements cease on server reads/commands without waiting for a browser timer or a successful job; existing data and authorized membership remain. No charge or provider checkout is initiated by expiry.
**AC-03 → BR-02:** Only an explicit authorized manual upgrade opens paid checkout with hosted trials disabled. A redirect alone cannot grant paid access.
**AC-04 → BR-01/03:** Client timestamps/plan flags, cross-workspace requests and concurrent/replayed start commands cannot mint another trial or usage credit outside the approved eligibility policy.

## Acceptance tests

**AT-01 → AC-01:** Given an eligible verified owner and fixed server clock, when Starter or Plus trial starts twice concurrently, then one immutable trial window exists, ends 14 days after its trusted start, and no provider/payment method call occurs.
**AT-02 → AC-02:** Given a trial ending at an explicit UTC instant with six members and nonzero consumed usage, when requests run just before, at and after expiry (including a stopped expiry worker), then server policy applies the correct boundary; members/data remain, consumption does not reset and no automatic charge is made.
**AT-03 → AC-03:** Given an expired trial, when an owner explicitly upgrades, then checkout requests the server price/seats/currency with allow_trial=false; only reconciled success grants paid entitlements. A member, forged redirect or background expiry cannot trigger upgrade.
**AT-04 → AC-04:** Given used eligibility, another workspace ID, future client start date or repeated command ID, when trial start is attempted, then the approved server rule refuses or idempotently returns the original result, with no duplicate window/credits. Complete fixtures after BR-03 decisions.

## Dependencies and completion

<issue id="55e64c7b-7034-4ced-bf17-6c30cd33e38b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs">FOR-39</issue> supplies shared authorization. Coordinate with <issue id="0de68eed-860c-4aec-8c56-e69b7ba70627" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-97/verify-signup-email-change-account-linking-and-workspace-invitations">FOR-97</issue> for verified identity and <issue id="125b71bf-f1b7-46d5-b456-b81d02b0c0d0" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-111/reconcile-payment-events-into-server-enforced-entitlements">FOR-111</issue> for the single entitlement projection; full payment processing is not a blocker to implementing card-free trial persistence. Completion requires real database concurrent/replay tests, expiry read/command enforcement, UI verification and proof of no payment calls. The current provider adapter's hosted-trial suppression is preparation only. Status is Backlog; no app-managed trial has shipped.

**AC-05 → BR-03:** A trial never multiplies allowance by active members, opens a monthly refill inside its 14-day window, uses paid Calls/Signals exclusions, or permits paid overage. Exact expiry closes the original window.
**AT-05 → AC-05:** Given Starter/Plus trials with 1, 5 and 20 active members and exhausted US$5 pools, when agent/Calls/Signals operations are attempted with stale paid-overage authorization, then all metered work is refused. Repeat across a calendar-month boundary and at the exact 14-day expiry; no extra pool appears. Directly provider-paid BYOK work remains excluded from customer allowance subject to independent operational limits.

Local preparation: explicit standard/trial phase in allowance and charge policy, fixed US$5 trial pool, trial Calls/Signals metering, no trial overage, immutable 14-day period helper and hosted-trial suppression. Billing suite: 9 files / 164 tests passed. Actual persistence/redemption, server feature expiry, join transaction behavior and UI are still unimplemented; this story remains Backlog.

### Final trial usage policy and local contract verification

User confirmed one fixed **US$5 workspace pool for the 14-day trial**, with **Calls and Signals metered against it**. Trial allowance does not scale with members, refill at a calendar-month boundary or permit overage. BYOK remains excluded. Budget/charge policy now requires a trusted `standard`/`trial` access phase and rejects missing/unknown classifications. A workspace-scoped trial-period helper preserves the original 14-day half-open window and refuses usage exactly at expiry; it does not start a new pool. Paid Calls/Signals exemptions apply only outside trial. Card-free trial start/expiry persistence and UI are not implemented by these helpers.

Focused billing verification: **9 files / 164 tests passed**; app TypeScript, billing ESLint, formatting and diff checks passed. Broader app run: 210 files / 1,241 tests passed, with one review-screen emoji-picker test failure currently being rechecked. No live billing/membership changes; uncommitted and undeployed.
