auditDocument.title: Pre-implementation backlog audit · 28 October 2026
auditDocument.content:
# Pre-implementation backlog review — 28 October 2026

## Review result

The original **124-issue** backlog covered all 31 report headings, but feature-heading coverage concealed missing delivery behavior and over-coupled work. This review read every live issue's full specification and native relationships, compared them with the readiness review, and inspected the owning source for notification preferences, model connections, agent retention and onboarding. The repository remains at `ededa613588aaf885732ec05f6ecbf9cb17f43a4`.

The revised backlog contains **133 issues and 251 native prerequisite links**, down from 296 links despite adding nine issues. **73 existing issues were refined.** Five new items close missing coverage; four preserve existing scope in independently deliverable slices. No issue was deleted, marked Done, assigned an invented owner or given an invented estimate/date.

This is a backlog and specification audit, not a fresh production-readiness certification. No application implementation, deployment, load test or end-to-end test suite was run.

## Missing work now owned by stories

| New work | Why the previous coverage was insufficient | Scope |
| -- | -- | -- |
| [FOR-145](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-145/persist-notification-channel-choices-and-enforce-delivery-preferences>) — channel/type preferences | The checked notification-preferences module stores choices in localStorage and exposes desktop/mobile/email/Slack controls. Inbox state and email transport tickets did not own persisted choices, priority-inbox behavior and send-time preference precedence. Unsupported channels must be unavailable. | Feature gated |
| [FOR-146](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-146/deliver-authorized-native-notifications-with-safe-deep-links>) — native delivery | Dock badges were covered, but OS notification delivery, permission denial, replay deduplication, privacy and click reauthorization were not. | Feature gated |
| [FOR-147](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-147/expire-agent-conversation-data-through-scheduled-recoverable-retention>) — agent data lifecycle | Shared file cleanup and account deletion do not schedule policy-driven expiry of retained runs/messages/events or prove scheduler health. The checked script sweeps artifacts/attachments only. | Feature gated |
| [FOR-148](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-148/verify-model-connection-setup-refresh-revocation-and-endpoint>) — model connection lifecycle | Keyring rotation and live-provider evals do not fully own personal/workspace connection setup, refresh, revocation and changed endpoint routing. Existing services are reused and verified. | Feature gated |
| [FOR-149](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-149/enforce-browser-request-origins-and-session-trust-boundaries>) — browser session/origin boundary | The source report explicitly required CSRF/origin/CORS acceptance, but no issue owned that complete matrix. Existing auth controls must be verified, not presumed absent. | Core production |

Additional gaps were resolved inside their existing owners: fresh-account workspace/team bootstrap and email ownership proofs in [FOR-97](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-97/verify-signup-email-change-account-linking-and-workspace-invitations>); failed recovery mail in [FOR-96](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-96/recover-password-access-with-single-use-verified-reset-flows>); token refresh/disconnect races in [FOR-71](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-71/connect-reconnect-and-disconnect-meeting-providers-in-production>); unsafe rich text in [FOR-46](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-46/discuss-issues-with-durable-comments-and-mentions>) / [FOR-61](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-61/create-and-edit-shared-documents-with-revision-conflicts>); command/approval crash points and revoked-result replay in [FOR-32](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-32/commit-commands-receipts-audit-and-outbox-events-atomically>) / [FOR-80](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-80/execute-approved-agent-writes-with-crash-safe-command-receipts>); late upload authorization in [FOR-35](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-35/upload-files-directly-with-validated-upload-intents-and-finalize>); and bounded operating limits in [FOR-24](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-24/agree-capacity-service-and-recovery-objectives>).

## Bundled scope split without dropping functionality

| Prior coupling | Revised ownership |
| -- | -- |
| Runtime preference schema/defaults depended on account import and ownership policy. | [FOR-128](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-128/validate-and-safely-migrate-personal-preference-schemas>) is a pure schema/scope/default contract; [FOR-127](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-127/keep-personal-preferences-consistent-across-authenticated-sessions>) consumes it; [FOR-144](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-144/import-legacy-personal-preferences-without-overwriting-account-choices>) separately owns legacy import consent, conflicts and resumption. |
| Basic planning API waited for initiative/project-progress implementation. | [FOR-88](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-88/expose-authorized-projects-cycles-labels-and-initiatives>) owns basic projects/cycles/labels; [FOR-150](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-150/expose-enabled-initiative-and-advanced-project-metadata-through-the>) owns initiatives and advanced milestones/updates. |
| Planning/inbox agent context waited for both documents and meeting-provider sync. | [FOR-82](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-82/let-forge-use-authorized-cycles-documents-inbox-and-call-recaps>) owns cycles/inbox; [FOR-151](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-151/let-forge-read-authorized-documents-with-source-references>) owns document reads; [FOR-152](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-152/let-forge-read-authorized-call-recaps-with-provenance>) owns call recap reads. |

The four split-out items are [FOR-144](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-144/import-legacy-personal-preferences-without-overwriting-account-choices>), [FOR-150](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-150/expose-enabled-initiative-and-advanced-project-metadata-through-the>), [FOR-151](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-151/let-forge-read-authorized-documents-with-source-references>), [FOR-152](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-152/let-forge-read-authorized-call-recaps-with-provenance>). Existing parent stories were narrowed accordingly; the split does not duplicate their acceptance obligations.

## Duplicates and overlap

No exact duplicate titles or fully redundant user outcomes were found. Similar infrastructure and acceptance gates are retained when they own distinct deliverables.

| Overlap reviewed | Resolution |
| -- | -- |
| [FOR-33](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-33/deliver-external-effects-with-recoverable-outbox-processing>) and [FOR-64](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-64/run-leased-resumable-background-jobs-with-operator-recovery>) both described leases/retries/dead letters. | The job runner owns generic execution/recovery. Outbox owns event/provider semantics and consumes that runner. There is one lease/retry substrate, with separate acceptance for ambiguous external effects. |
| [FOR-47](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-47/react-to-comments-and-subscribe-to-issue-activity>), [FOR-66](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-66/sync-read-snooze-delete-and-subscription-state-across-devices>) and notification preferences mixed subscription/state concepts. | Issue subscription belongs to the first; read/snooze/hide/replay belongs to inbox state; channel/type delivery policy belongs to [FOR-145](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-145/persist-notification-channel-choices-and-enforce-delivery-preferences>). Inbox-item deletion never unsubscribes or deletes an issue. |
| [FOR-102](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-102/sync-editable-profile-extras-across-authorized-sessions>) and [FOR-127](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-127/keep-personal-preferences-consistent-across-authenticated-sessions>) share account persistence patterns. | They keep separate records and ownership contracts. Profile no longer waits for cosmetic preference implementation. |
| [FOR-34](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-34/store-all-agent-and-issue-files-durably-in-private-object-storage>), [FOR-48](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-48/attach-durable-files-to-issues-and-comments>) and [FOR-83](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-83/use-durable-attachments-and-artifacts-throughout-an-agent-run>) all mention files. | Retain adapter durability, issue/comment binding and agent-runtime transfer as distinct outcomes. [FOR-37](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-37/reconcile-orphaned-files-and-retry-durable-deletion>) owns shared byte deletion; [FOR-147](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-147/expire-agent-conversation-data-through-scheduled-recoverable-retention>) owns agent-specific eligibility/scheduling. |
| Implementation tests and release gates overlap scenarios. | Implementation issues prove their slice; release gates prove the selected candidate, deployment and enabled surface. A gate must not become a second implementation project. |

## Unnecessary blockers corrected

| Before | Now and rationale |
| -- | -- |
| [FOR-64](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-64/run-leased-resumable-background-jobs-with-operator-recovery>) waited on outbox and final operational alerts. | Runner depends on transactional identities and telemetry hooks; outbox consumes it. Final alert evidence stays a core release requirement. |
| Comments waited on an asynchronous delivery worker. | Comment writes emit atomic outbox rows through the command foundation; actual fan-out has its own owner. |
| Cycles waited on projects; recurrence always waited on cycles. | Team issue/cycle membership can be built independently of projects. Recurrence validates a cycle only when that option is selected. |
| Profile waited on preferences; external import waited on Forge export. | Both use shared foundations without forcing the neighboring product feature to ship first. |
| Basic API release waited on webhooks. | Webhooks have conditional enablement evidence; basic API may ship with registration/dispatch disabled. |
| Read-only MCP waited on issue mutation endpoints. | It uses the canonical read service and credential scopes directly. |
| MCP writes and user-approved PR feedback waited on internal agent approvals/runs. | They use shared command identities and explicit transport-specific authority. They never fabricate an internal run or require model execution for a human-approved operation. Autonomous agent posting remains outside the review story. |
| Skills waited on the full issue/project tool catalog; outbound connector reads waited on skill authoring. | Run-context and authorization contracts are the relevant prerequisites. Enabled material writes still require their approval evidence. |
| Every preference consumer waited on legacy import policy. | Consumers depend on the schema/account contract; import is separate. |
| Native adapters waited on the completed packaged-security gate. | Adapter implementation uses the existing trusted bridge and its own negative tests. The full packaged security gate remains mandatory before desktop distribution. |
| Preference gates required every optional control even when explicitly excluded. | Gates require shared safety/release foundations plus a **selected-surface evidence matrix**. Related links identify conditional implementations. Missing evidence for any enabled control still blocks release. |
| Password recovery and invitation verification waited on the collaborative domain schema/job runner. | Existing account-auth/mail flows can be implemented and verified independently. Current authorization, cookie/origin and delivery-failure requirements remain intact. |

Transitive links were also removed where another retained prerequisite already enforces the same ordering. The audit changed 95 existing blocking links by removal and added 32 replacement/required links; the nine new issues contribute 18 links. Arithmetic: **296 − 95 + 32 + 18 = 251**. This count includes structural cleanup and scope changes; it does not claim 95 distinct product defects.

One genuine missing implementation prerequisite was added: [FOR-35](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-35/upload-files-directly-with-validated-upload-intents-and-finalize>) requires shared [FOR-39](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs>) for upload intent/finalize permission checks. The core candidate gate now requires [FOR-149](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-149/enforce-browser-request-origins-and-session-trust-boundaries>). Agent release evidence now includes connection lifecycle and agent retention.

## Dependency and release rules

Native blocking links identify prerequisites for completing the acceptance contract. Preparation and fixture-based implementation can proceed concurrently once interfaces are agreed; a blocked issue does not forbid design work.

A related link is not an automatic prerequisite. **Conditional evidence is mandatory when its feature is selected**: webhooks, advanced API endpoints, skills/domain tools and optional preference/native controls must either pass their stated checks or be explicitly excluded by [FOR-20](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates>) and enforced by [FOR-103](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-103/disable-unfinished-features-consistently-across-ui-and-server-routes>). A release gate cannot close just because its unconditional blockers are Done.

The accepted release manifest must list each enabled capability, its implementation/gate issue, candidate evidence and owner. Exclusion never closes an unfinished implementation issue. No features were silently removed in this audit.

## Verification of the saved backlog

* Read back **all 133 issues**, including native relationships.
* Titles, priorities, labels, milestones, Backlog status and intended prerequisites match the revised plan.
* **251 prerequisites**, all inside this project; **no dependency cycles**.
* **All 57 core-production items** are connected to core launch, except the launch issue itself and the explicitly subsequent post-launch check.
* **No feature-gated or later-expansion item is an unconditional ancestor of core launch.**
* No archived preference issue references or unresolved authoring placeholders remain in issue descriptions.
* Every stable AC ID has a corresponding AT specification. This is a structural check; it does not imply that tests have passed or that every policy has been approved.
* Semantic duplicate review found the ownership overlaps above, not tickets that should be deleted.

## What can start and what still needs refinement

Three work items have no native prerequisites: [FOR-25](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-25/identify-the-serving-production-services-and-database>) (serving-environment identity), [FOR-20](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates>) (release contract), and [FOR-128](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-128/validate-and-safely-migrate-personal-preference-schemas>) (pure preference schemas/defaults). Foundation work can start while product decisions are resolved; policy-dependent acceptance cannot be signed off in advance.

| Decision still needed | Owning issue |
| -- | -- |
| Pilot audience, enabled providers/clients/channels/modules, individual release owners, and unavailable/preview behavior | [FOR-20](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-20/agree-the-production-release-scope-and-feature-gates>) |
| Cross-team projects, private-team aggregates and sharing rules | [FOR-21](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-21/decide-project-team-and-shared-resource-visibility-rules>) |
| Browser-data ownership, destination choices, duplicate/conflict handling and cleanup | [FOR-22](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-22/decide-ownership-and-conflict-rules-for-legacy-browser-data>) |
| Raw/derived/agent data lifetimes, account deletion and backup/restore exceptions | [FOR-23](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-23/define-retention-and-accountworkspace-deletion-behavior>) |
| Workload, measurable service/recovery objectives, storage/processing limits and retry windows | [FOR-24](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-24/agree-capacity-service-and-recovery-objectives>) |
| Provider modes, spend/concurrency/deadline policy and disconnect behavior | [FOR-75](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-75/define-provider-spending-and-execution-admission-policy>) |
| MCP transport/client compatibility and delegated versus pending-approval writes | [FOR-91](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-91/choose-external-mcp-transport-client-support-and-write-authority>) |
| Paid-plan provider, entitlements and commercial lifecycle, if charging | [FOR-109](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-109/agree-plans-entitlements-and-subscription-lifecycle-rules>) |
| Channel precedence and mandatory versus optional messages; OS permission/preview behavior | [FOR-145](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-145/persist-notification-channel-choices-and-enforce-delivery-preferences>), [FOR-146](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-146/deliver-authorized-native-notifications-with-safe-deep-links>) |
| SLA business hours, DST/catch-up behavior, selected integration providers and import formats | Refine [FOR-125](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-125/enforce-shared-sla-schedules-and-escalation-policy>), [FOR-68](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-68/generate-one-canonical-issue-for-each-recurring-occurrence>), [FOR-71](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-71/connect-reconnect-and-disconnect-meeting-providers-in-production>), [FOR-104](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-104/manage-authorized-external-connections-and-applications>), [FOR-114](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-114/import-supported-external-datasets-with-preview-and-reconciliation>) before implementing their selected modes. |

[FOR-126](<https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-126/migrate-legacy-planning-content-and-shared-views-when-enabled>) remains the planned advanced-content migration batch. If documents, views and initiatives are launched on different dates, split its adapters by the accepted module rollout before scheduling that batch; preserved local records must remain recoverable meanwhile. Provider-specific OAuth and external-format imports similarly need provider/format-sized execution tasks once their supported set is chosen. No estimates or rollout dates were invented to hide those choices.

**INVEST assessment:** value and testable outcomes are explicit; dependency cleanup improves independent delivery; unresolved policy keeps stories negotiable. Estimated size and sprint fit still require product/development/test refinement, especially provider integrations, deletion/export data classes and advanced-content migration. No workshop or stakeholder approval is claimed.

planMatrixDocument.title: Forge launch plans — entitlements and usage policy
planMatrixDocument.content:
# Forge launch plans: entitlements and usage

Source: the user's three Linear Plans screenshots and explicit decisions in this
conversation, 28 October 2026. Screenshot Basic maps to Forge Starter; Business
maps to Forge Plus. The user's overrides below take precedence over screenshot
values. The screenshots' annual billing is not adopted: the approved prices are
monthly. The user separately confirmed a 14-day Starter/Plus free trial with no
payment details and manual upgrade: Forge manages the trial, and no automatic
charge occurs at expiry. A trial receives one fixed US$5 workspace pool across its
14-day window, including Calls/Signals usage. Eligibility is once per workspace,
shared across Starter/Plus and all admins. Durable redemption and anti-abuse
enforcement still require implementation before launch.

This is the commercial feature allocation to implement. A checkmark does not
establish that Forge has shipped or verified that capability. Existing release
gates, authorization and operational limits still apply. Enterprise contractual,
support and compliance items require separate implementation, review and agreement;
they must not be advertised as achieved based on this table.

## Prices, limits and charging

| Item | Free | Starter | Plus | Enterprise |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly price per active member, before tax | 0 | EUR 10 / USD 10 | EUR 16 / USD 16 | Custom |
| Free trial | Not applicable | 14 days, subject to eligibility | 14 days, subject to eligibility | Agreement required |
| Trial payment/conversion | Not applicable | No payment details; manual upgrade | No payment details; manual upgrade | Agreement required |
| Trial AI pool | Not applicable | US$5 total/workspace for 14 days | US$5 total/workspace for 14 days | Agreement required |
| Trial Calls/Signals | Not applicable | Consume trial pool | Consume trial pool | Agreement required |
| Active workspace members | 5 | No plan cap | No plan cap | No plan cap |
| File upload size | 10 MB | No plan cap | No plan cap | No plan cap |
| Non-archived issues | 250 | No plan cap | No plan cap | No plan cap |
| Teams | 2 | 5 | No plan cap | No plan cap |
| Monthly included AI allowance | US$5 per workspace | US$5 per active member | US$5 per active member | Agreement required |
| Forge agent allowance consumption | At provider cost | At provider cost | At provider cost | Agreement required |
| Calls and Signals allowance consumption | At provider cost | No allowance debit or allowance-based overage | No allowance debit or allowance-based overage | Paid exclusion; custom operating terms |
| Capped paid AI overage | Unavailable | Explicit opt-in + payment authority + cap | Explicit opt-in + payment authority + cap | Agreement required |

Members include owners/admins and exclude pending invitations. The Free cap applies
when membership is actually created, including accepted invitations, domain joins,
invite links, direct administrative additions and imports. Pending invitations
do not contribute allowance or become billable seats. Every admission path must
serialize capacity checks with insertion; counting members before an independent
write is insufficient. On a paid-to-Free downgrade, existing members keep access;
block new joins while the active count is five or more. Do not evict existing
members, force an owner to select five, or delete data. Normal authorization and
member removal still apply. Existing-member retries must not be treated as new joins.

Free's fixed US$5 pool supersedes the earlier US$5-per-member Free proposal. Adding
or removing Free members never resets consumption or grants extra credits. Paid
allowance follows current active membership; billed subscription seat changes take
effect at next renewal with no mid-cycle proration. Those are separate quantities.
Free never receives usable overage, even if a stale paid opt-in survives downgrade.

EUR applies to EU27 + Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, UK and Switzerland, determined
by the workspace billing address country. Other accepted countries use USD. AI
allowance is denominated in USD independently of invoice currency. Paid allowance
resets use trusted workspace billing periods; Free uses workspace signup anniversary.
Paid agent overage is at provider cost, with no markup. BYOK/directly provider-paid
runs never debit Forge allowance or generate Forge overage on any plan.

Calls/Signals exclusions must use a trusted server feature classification and the
applicable plan snapshot. Preserve their provider-cost telemetry and operational
capacity controls. Exclusion from the customer AI pool does not mean zero internal
cost, unlimited concurrency or a second paid overage charge. Metering/reservation
integration must evaluate an exempt operation independently of an exhausted agent
allowance; do not reserve paid Calls/Signals against that pool.

"No plan cap" transcribes the screenshots' "Unlimited" commercial allocation.
It does not remove safe upload/request-size, storage, rate, abuse or execution limits.

## Feature allocation transcribed from the screenshots

| Feature | Free | Starter | Plus | Enterprise |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Customer requests | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

| Sub-initiatives | — | — | — | Yes |

| Agent platform | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Forge agent (reference: Linear Agent) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Coding sessions | Yes, consumes allowance | Yes, consumes allowance | Yes, consumes allowance | Custom usage agreement |
| Loops | — | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Agent for Slack | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

| MCP access | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

| Standard integrations | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Support integrations | — | — | Yes | Yes |
| Microsoft Teams integration | Yes | Yes | Yes | Multiple tenants |
| Salesforce integration | — | — | — | Paid add-on |
| Sub-teams | — | — | 1 level | 5 levels |
| Private teams | — | — | Yes | Yes |
| Guest accounts | — | — | Yes | Yes |
| Progress reports | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Insights | — | — | Yes | Yes |
| Dashboards | — | — | — | Yes |

| Asks: web forms | — | — | — | Yes |
| Asks: multiple Slack workspaces | — | — | — | Yes |
| Asks: private Slack channels | — | — | — | Yes |
| Asks: per-channel configurations | — | — | — | Yes |
| SSO | Google | Google | Google | Google + SAML |
| Admin roles | — | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Third-party app management | — | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Advanced authentication | — | — | Yes | Yes |
| IP restrictions | — | — | — | Yes |
| SCIM provisioning | — | — | — | Yes |
| Domain claiming | — | — | — | Yes |
| Audit-log access | — | — | — | Yes |
| HIPAA offering | — | — | — | Separate compliance review/agreement |

The screenshot's premium "Admin roles" row does not remove workspace ownership or
baseline access checks from Free. Audit-log availability to customers is distinct
from mandatory internal security/audit event collection on every plan. Screenshot
Insights is not silently equated with Forge Signals; Signals metering follows the
user's explicit rule above. The screenshots do not specify Forge-only Calls/Signals
feature limits beyond that rule.

## Implementation and verification requirements

The user confirmed **no Forge concurrency caps** per user, workspace or provider,
for every plan and trial. The earlier 3/20/10 choice is superseded. Active-run
telemetry and atomic spending reservations remain necessary, but run count alone
must never reject admission. Retired `FORGE_AGENT_*_CONCURRENT_RUNS` settings are
ignored. Monthly allowance, explicitly capped paid overage, per-run execution and
token bounds remain distinct controls.

Forge-funded usage is in scope for every built-in supported provider: OpenAI,
Anthropic, Google, MiniMax, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek and Kimi. Each still needs its
own credential, cost reconciliation and release verification. BYOK/provider-paid
subscriptions retain their separate payer classification.

The first paid billing period after Free or trial starts with a **fresh US$5 per
active member pool**. Earlier Free/trial consumption is not deducted. Keep old
ledger rows and outstanding reservations attached to their original period;
key the new grant to the authoritative paid period so replay cannot grant twice.
Switching an existing paid tier does not create another first-purchase grant.

Use one server entitlement projection, extending the existing
`workspace_entitlements` source rather than introducing another authority. Migrate
legacy `basic`/`business` values to Starter/Plus through an explicit data migration;
do not accept an unchecked cast or infer paid access from a browser plan name.
Enterprise's custom terms require explicit quota configuration; never default it
to a standard plan allowance.

Enforce numeric limits and feature gates in commands, APIs, agents, workers and
imports as well as UI. Member, team, active-issue and upload limits need their own
atomic enforcement and boundary/concurrency tests. Keep unavailable feature flags
off even if a plan is entitled. Plan changes must not bypass privacy/role checks.

Usage reservations/settlement must bind workspace, period, trusted plan, feature
and payer snapshots. Free exhaustion blocks additional metered agent/Calls/Signals
work; paid Calls/Signals must still pass independent safety/admission controls.
Existing consumption must survive membership changes, retries and plan transitions.
Starter→Plus upgrades now take effect after successful immediate prorated payment; Plus→Starter downgrades take effect at renewal. Failed upgrade payment retains the original Starter contract. A full refund of only that upgrade charge restores verified, already-paid Starter access through its original boundary. The fully refunded upgrade also renews on Starter; verified provider scheduling preserves existing renewal seats and retries safely. Other plan-change carryover decisions remain open. Cancellation and full/partial current-period refund timing are confirmed below. Member grandfathering on downgrade is confirmed above. Team and active-issue downgrades retain existing access and block creation/import or unarchiving above the new cap; existing content is not deleted or concealed. Upload over-capacity transitions still need rules. Currency changes are confirmed for next renewal, with a seven-day replacement-checkout grace deadline. Late checkout keeps the original monthly anniversary. The actual provider replacement/grace executor and durable short-month renewal correction remain gated. See `docs/renewal-currency-change.md`. EUR overage/caps and usage-time ECB
reference conversion are confirmed; durable ledger/invoice integration remains
required before live billing. See `docs/overage-currency.md`.

Failed-renewal access is confirmed: **7 days (168 hours) of paid access**, including
the included pool and paid overage under the existing opt-in/cap. Retries cannot
restart grace; an unpaid first subscription gets none. At expiry, resolve access
as Free while preserving existing members. Backend projection, time-aware
security/member checks and the signed webhook boundary are implemented and
verified on isolated staging. Webhooks remain disabled until remaining lifecycle
handlers, periodic reconciliation and the billing release gate pass. See
`docs/subscription-payment-grace.md`.

The local helpers implement fixed Free/trial allowance, paid per-member allowance,
overage rules and plan/phase/feature/payer usage classification. They are not yet
connected to the commercial reservation ledger. FOR-153 now has an atomic member
counter migration and auth/join integration verified against real PostgreSQL;
production migration/application rollout remains pending. See
[the member-capacity implementation guide](https://linear.app/atriumcrm/document/atomic-workspace-member-capacity-implementation-and-rollout-a8b750fd4060),
`docs/polar-billing.md` and FOR-76/FOR-111 for remaining integration work.


Owner cancellation timing is confirmed: retain paid access until the current billing period ends, then apply Free limits while preserving existing members. The server command, durable cutoff and reconciliation are implemented on isolated staging; see `docs/subscription-cancellation.md`. Cancellation cannot extend payment grace or issue another AI pool. Full current-period refunds end paid access immediately while preserving existing members. The signed order handler, durable period denial and shared feature/auth/SQL enforcement are implemented on isolated staging; see `docs/subscription-refunds.md`. Partial refunds keep paid access unchanged; positive partial totals are audited/receipted without updating entitlement state, and cumulative full refunds revoke access even on replay of an earlier event. Immediate provider termination now overrides paid-through access and grace; a durable terminal marker prevents ordinary active updates from reopening the subscription. See `docs/subscription-termination.md`. Tier-change timing, failed-upgrade payment and upgrade-only refund access are implemented in `docs/subscription-plan-changes.md`. A full upgrade-only refund renews on Starter. Subscription pause/resume is excluded at launch; use period-end cancellation. Unexpected provider pauses have a durable access cutoff (see `docs/subscription-pause-policy.md`). Controlled repeat-upgrade adjustment remains gated; billing remains gated.


Subscription pausing policy confirmed 29 October 2026: no pause/resume at launch; period-end cancellation is the supported exit path. The prepared server boundary refuses unexpected pause states and records a cutoff shared by feature/auth/SQL admission. Provider portal configuration and actual candidate flows still require release verification.


Overage currency confirmed 29 October 2026: EUR-billed workspaces use EUR for paid overage and its separate cap; USD-billed workspaces use USD. The included pool remains US$5 under the existing plan rules. Conversion is fixed when usage is incurred using the latest published ECB daily reference rate, with no added spread; invoice generation must reuse the recorded rate. Prepared currency-aware cap/conversion helpers are verified, with atomic ledger/quote retention and real provider billing still gated. See `docs/overage-currency.md`.


Billing-country currency changes confirmed 29 October 2026: switch EUR/USD at the next renewal; permit a seven-day replacement-checkout grace period if payment is incomplete. A durable owner/admin request now records the frozen boundary, deadline, provider-confirmed country and informational renewal tier/quantity with atomic audit/receipt. Polar cannot update currency in place through the pinned API; a replacement checkout/executor remains required. The request does not claim a scheduled provider change or activate grace. See `docs/renewal-currency-change.md`.


Original-anniversary confirmation · 29 October 2026: checkout paid within the fixed seven-day grace window keeps the old monthly anniversary and commercial usage period. Durable original-day capture and a read-only paid-replacement verifier/calendar plan are implemented, including February clamping and the required following-month correction. They do not execute the provider change, rebind paid access or mint a new pool. Existing opted-in caps automatically convert at the latest published ECB rate, frozen at verified cutover; consumed/reserved capacity carries over in the same period and historical charges remain unchanged. See `docs/renewal-currency-change.md`.


Tax confirmation · 29 October 2026: listed Starter/Plus prices exclude tax; add applicable tax at checkout. The prepared adapter now verifies the approved monthly seat catalog uses explicit exclusive tax behavior before creating checkout, and rechecks live context after catalog reads. No actual provider catalog or tax settings were changed.

memberCapacityDocument.title: Atomic workspace member capacity — implementation and rollout
memberCapacityDocument.content:
# Atomic workspace member capacity

FOR-153 implements the five-active-member Free limit. All accepted member rows
count, including owner/admin; pending invitation rows do not count. Existing
members keep access when a paid workspace becomes Free above capacity. New joins
are blocked at five or more, and become possible below five. Roles and existing
member retries do not consume new capacity.

## Database invariant

Drizzle migration `apps/forge/drizzle/0026_workspace_member_capacity.sql` creates
`workspace_member_capacity`, backfills counts without removing members, and installs
organization/member triggers. Migration backfill and installation hold write locks
in the same transaction. Run this through **Drizzle migrations**, not `db:push`:
the generated schema alone does not install the custom triggers/functions.

Every successful member insertion atomically increments one workspace counter only
when its current server entitlement allows another member. The conditional UPDATE
serializes concurrent admissions. Rejected inserts and multirow imports roll back
their records and counter changes together. Deletions release capacity; workspace
moves lock counters in a deterministic order and roll back if the destination is
full. Organization deletion safely cascades. The counter's nonnegative constraint
and missing-state failures prevent silent drift. `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` retries
do not fire AFTER INSERT and therefore do not consume another slot.

The same invariant covers Better Auth, invite links, approved-domain joins, trusted
admin additions and database-backed imports. It does not depend on a browser plan,
count or transport-specific precheck. Direct database credentials and migrations
are trusted infrastructure: do not expose counter writes or raw SQL to end users.
The internal adjustment function revokes PUBLIC execution. A future restricted
runtime database role will need explicitly reviewed permissions for these trigger
functions and their tables; the current application uses the established database
owner connection.

Active/trialing server entitlements recognize the existing `basic`/`business`
values and the explicit `starter`/`plus` names, plus Enterprise. These names do not
grant any other feature, bypass email verification or replace the planned canonical
plan migration. Missing/unknown/nonactive entitlement state uses Free capacity,
matching the current security entitlement resolver. Dunning/grace changes belong
in the authoritative entitlement projection before billing is enabled.

## Auth and join paths

Better Auth receives the server-resolved plan limit for a friendly preflight.
Its database adapter converts the named database violation into a public
`WORKSPACE_MEMBER_LIMIT` conflict while leaving unrelated failures unchanged.
Invite-link/domain commands expose the same actionable message.

The installed Better Auth version updates an invitation before its inner member
transaction. `handleAuthRequest` wraps the entire acceptance endpoint in a database
transaction and retains the SDK's inner transaction as a savepoint. This permits
its failure handler to restore a refused invitation without querying an aborted
transaction. Unsuccessful responses roll back the outer transaction. The API route
uses this handler. New programmatic invitation-acceptance adapters must preserve
the same complete transaction boundary rather than bypass it with an isolated
SDK call. Existing auth providers and desktop/API-key integrations remain in place.

## Verification

Run `bun run test`, `bun run typecheck` and the changed-file lint checks from
`apps/forge`. The default Vitest suite deliberately skips the live database file
unless explicit test credentials are provided. It never falls back to DATABASE_URL.

`bun run test:member-capacity:postgres` requires:

- `FORGE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`: direct connection to an isolated test branch.
- `FORGE_TEST_DATABASE_HOST`: the exact expected host.
- `FORGE_TEST_NEON_BRANCH_ID`: its exact `br-...` ID, verified inside Postgres.

Use a schema-only branch so the test begins with empty user/organization tables.
The harness rejects the configured application database host, including its direct
and pooled variants, even if that database is empty.
Fixtures include legacy Free and paid workspaces with six members before applying
the migration. Tests exercise actual PostgreSQL concurrency, batch rollback,
cross-workspace moves, role changes, existing-member retries, downgrade boundaries,
trusted admin additions, tampered invitations, real invitation acceptance, invite
links and approved-domain joins. Only UUID-prefixed test fixtures are cleaned up.

For repeated API checks on an already migrated, empty test branch,
`FORGE_TEST_REUSE_MEMBER_CAPACITY=1` is an explicit opt-in: installed trigger bodies
must exactly match the checked-in SQL, counters must be empty and PUBLIC helper
execution must be revoked. This mode does not rerun migration backfill; keep a
fresh-branch migration run as separate evidence. No database objects are dropped
or reset by the test.

Validated on Forge project `raspy-union-96305162`, schema-only branch
`br-square-sky-za2iavfk`, PostgreSQL 18.6. The fresh migration and initial ten
integration cases passed. The final eleven-case suite also covers verified-owner
workspace creation and authorized access after downgrade, using the empty verified
branch with matching trigger bodies. PUBLIC
helper execution was separately revoked/checked there after the initial migration
run. The initial attempt exposed the missing savepoint and an incomplete domain
fixture; both were corrected before the successful runs.

The temporary test branches were created with expiration. The empty first branch
`br-autumn-union-za0opf1e` has since been renamed `staging`, its expiration removed,
and a separate fresh `forge_staging` database created there. All 27 versioned
migrations, including 0026, were applied through the guarded serialized runner.
The second test branch keeps its expiration. Neither the default branch nor local
`.env`/`.neon` connection selection was changed. Credentials are
kept outside the repository and must not be included in evidence artifacts.

## Rollout

Apply migration 0026 to each intended deployment database before releasing the new
auth/join handlers there. Review lock timing for large workspaces and retain the
usual database rollback/restore plan. Do not remove the invariant while relying
on the friendly preflight; it cannot stop concurrent admissions on its own.

The production/default database has **not** received this migration during local
implementation. FOR-112 remains the billing release gate; production readiness
also requires the separate authorization, trial, entitlement and deployment work.
The full eleven-case real-auth/PostgreSQL suite also passed against the fresh
`forge_staging` database after its complete 27-migration history was applied.
This closes the membership implementation contract on isolated staging. The
separate production migration/application rollout remains a release-gate task.


## Payment-grace compatibility · 28 October 2026

The shared access reader and member-capacity invariant honor the confirmed 168-hour renewal grace. Migration 0027 replaces only the counter helper to evaluate paid period/grace timestamps; migration 0028 binds a provider subscription to one workspace. The complete history now has 29 migrations on isolated staging. The twelve-case member/auth suite passes, including a sixth-member acceptance during grace, refusal after expiry with the invitation still pending, and continued authorized access for existing members. Membership and security reads tolerate the previous entitlement schema. FOR-153 remains Done; production rollout and full billing reconciliation remain separately gated.

Scheduled cancellation now uses the same stored cutoff in feature reads, auth preflight and the SQL counter. The thirteen-case real-auth suite additionally proves that an existing sixth member keeps access after term end while a seventh invitation is refused and remains pending. Migration 0029 is applied only to staging/rehearsal; production rollout remains gated.


## Full-refund migration follow-up · 28 October 2026

Versioned migration 0030 adds the retained refunded-period history and updates member admission to deny refunded paid capacity. All 31 migrations are applied on the exact isolated staging and rehearsal targets. Three serialized migration ownership/fault cases pass against the complete history. The serving/default database is unchanged and still lacks the new production-readiness expansions; production rollout remains separately gated. See `docs/subscription-refunds.md`.


## Immediate termination migration follow-up · 28 October 2026

Migration 0031 adds finite provider-backed terminal state and makes SQL member admission deny paid capacity immediately on final revocation. All 32 migrations are applied only to isolated staging and rehearsal; three serialized ownership/fault cases pass against the complete history. Thirty-one billing-state and fifteen real-auth member cases pass on staging. Existing members stay authorized. No serving/default database or connection configuration changed. See `docs/subscription-termination.md`; production rollout remains separately gated.


## Upgrade-refund access migration follow-up · 28 October 2026

Migration 0032 records paid Plus grant identity and aligns refund-aware Starter fallback with SQL admission. All 33 migrations are applied only to isolated staging/rehearsal; three full-history migration ownership/fault cases pass. Staging: 43 billing and 16 real-auth membership cases pass, including temporary admission refusal without base proof and resumed paid Starter admission after verification. Existing member sessions are preserved. The serving/default database and local connection files are unchanged. See `docs/subscription-plan-changes.md`.


## Unsupported provider pause · 29 October 2026

Pause/resume is excluded at launch. Migration 0033 makes SQL admission honor the same durable pause cutoff as feature/auth access. At cutoff, new joins follow Free capacity while existing member sessions remain valid. The 17-case real-auth suite verifies a retained sixth-member session, blocked invitation acceptance and unchanged pending invitation after an ordinary resumed/active update. Current evidence: `docs/subscription-pause-policy.md`.

visibilityDocument.title: Forge resource visibility policy and implementation fixtures
visibilityDocument.content:
# Forge resource visibility policy

<issue id="6b5d1b04-fb02-43c8-a2ce-badcac2a8a29" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-21/decide-project-team-and-shared-resource-visibility-rules">FOR-21</issue> decision record, 28 October 2026. The user confirmed the project, initiative, administrator and document-sharing rules below. <issue id="dca691b0-e932-4812-87d9-34b4ede21c89" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-31/enforce-tenant-safe-identifiers-and-relationships-in-the-database">FOR-31</issue> owns database relationship integrity; <issue id="55e64c7b-7034-4ced-bf17-6c30cd33e38b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs">FOR-39</issue> owns enforcement across enabled adapters. This document is not certification that browser-local planning content is already server-backed.

## Read matrix

Every row requires current workspace membership and the credential scope for that operation. Workspace roles never cross workspace boundaries. An owner/admin role grants private-team read access independently of team write permission; a read-only `teams:read` key still has that role's read visibility.

| Resource | Regular member outside private team B | Member of B | Workspace owner/admin |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Workspace-visible team A and its issues | Visible | Visible | Visible |
| Private team B and its issues | Hidden | Visible | Visible |
| Project spanning A and B | Project details visible; B issues and derived counts hidden | Project details and authorized issues visible | Visible |
| Project belonging only to private teams | Hidden unless a participating team is readable | Visible when at least one participating team is readable | Visible |
| Project with no team restriction | Workspace-visible | Workspace-visible | Workspace-visible |
| Initiative metadata | Workspace-visible even when all child projects are private | Workspace-visible | Workspace-visible |
| Initiative child projects/issues and rollups | Only readable children contribute | Only readable children contribute | All same-workspace children contribute |
| Document originating from a private issue/team | Hidden by default; visible after an explicit workspace sharing grant | Visible | Visible; may explicitly share workspace-wide |
| Document originating from a project | Inherits project visibility unless explicitly shared workspace-wide | Same rule | Visible; may share |
| Workspace document or workspace label metadata | Workspace-visible | Workspace-visible | Workspace-visible |
| Any resource from another workspace | Hidden | Hidden | Hidden |

A shared project or initiative does not grant access to its teams' private issues. A workspace-shared document does not grant access to its source issue or project. Linking a private document from a shared project is not a sharing action. Only owners/admins may create or remove an explicit workspace sharing grant. Other document edit permissions remain unchanged.

## Relationship and response rules

Canonical relationships stay in one workspace. Creating a relation requires the actor to read both ends and have the relevant write authority. Cross-team issue parent links do not inherit permissions in either direction; parent cycles are rejected atomically. Existing unreadable parents, related issues, backlinks and source references are omitted from responses, including identifying titles, identifiers, team names and hidden relation totals. A visible child does not reveal an unreadable parent.

Labels defined at workspace scope have workspace-visible names and colors; their issue references and usage counts are filtered by issue visibility. Team-local labels follow their team. Creating a workspace label is an explicit publication at workspace scope; linking it to a private issue never publishes the issue.

Filter before search ranking/snippets, pagination, exports, counts, charts and progress calculations. Do not return a global total or hidden-count hint alongside a filtered result. Do not subtract hidden totals client-side. Shared initiative text and shared document bodies are deliberately shared content; operators should not automatically copy private issue titles or generated summaries into them. Generated summaries must read only the requesting actor's authorized inputs.

Files inherit their owning resource's current access. A document's explicit sharing grant covers that document's own embedded files, not other private issue attachments. Revoke access using current membership/grants at execution and download time; cached metadata, durable jobs, agent tools and idempotent receipts cannot authorize from a stale snapshot.

## Fixtures and adapter contract

Use workspace W1 with public team A, private team B (Bob), private team C (Cara), regular member Alice, owner Olivia and admin Amir. W2 is foreign even when a user is an admin in W1.

* Alice sees the A+B project, A issues and A-only progress. She cannot detect the number or titles of B issues.
* Bob sees the B+C project and B issues. C-only details and counts remain hidden.
* Alice cannot see the B+C project. She can see its initiative's shared metadata, with no B+C child reference or hidden-child total.
* Olivia and Amir see B without joining it. Their `teams:read` API keys may read B but cannot change membership without `teams:write`.
* A B-issue document linked to A+B remains hidden from Alice until Olivia/Amir explicitly share the document. After sharing, Alice reads the document and its own files, with no source-issue backlink metadata.
* Bob cannot share that document workspace-wide. An admin in W2 cannot share or read it.
* A hidden team sorting before visible teams never occupies a page slot or changes the visible next cursor. Foreign IDs and inaccessible team IDs both produce an absent resource response.

The pure resource rules are executable in `resource-visibility.test.ts`. Current persisted team enforcement uses a SQL predicate before LIMIT, shared by team list, direct lookup and web directory. `team-visibility.postgres.test.ts` verifies the actual queries on an isolated branch. Canonical project, issue, initiative and document adapters must use the resource policy and scoped SQL before they can pass <issue id="55e64c7b-7034-4ced-bf17-6c30cd33e38b" href="https://linear.app/atriumcrm/issue/FOR-39/enforce-one-authorization-policy-across-ui-api-tools-and-jobs">FOR-39</issue>; pure policy tests alone do not prove those adapters.

Session, API and agent adapters must resolve a current trusted Actor before applying resource visibility. Sessions require live workspace membership; external credentials require scopes as well. Document/initiative transports without a declared scope contract stay disabled until their enablement work supplies one. Jobs and replay paths reauthorize before effects and before returning stored private data.

environmentDocument.content:
# Serving-environment identity investigation

FOR-25 read-only evidence, 28 October 2026. The complete serving database chain is
**not yet verified**, so production migrations are blocked.

| Surface | Verified deployment | Alias | Region | Source commit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Web, project `prj_S0XLtdngbexhl2ao7WviBrlMScar` | `dpl_DHbhSDCAubnVvndVKDUgvCCzH5Bu` | `forge-app-mauve.vercel.app` | `iad1` | Missing in deployment metadata |
| Agent runtime, project `prj_NtW13t9fbFligQ3pWV4DdUxW5Mub` | `dpl_12bYPfjiXsMhFB7U2DkjZ4LuDn5r` | `forge-agent-runtime.vercel.app` | `iad1` | Missing in deployment metadata |

Vercel's deployment-alias API confirms these mappings. Both deployments report
READY / production / Node 24. The web and runtime roots return HTTP 200 and the
anonymous web `/api/auth/get-session` endpoint returns 200. Runtime `/health`
returns 404. These requests do not prove authenticated DB queries or an agent
execution.

Current project configuration has readable `BETTER_AUTH_URL` pointing to the web
alias and `EVE_AGENT_RUNTIME_URL` pointing to the runtime alias. Project config is
not proof of the immutable deployment's captured environment. Vercel lists web
`DATABASE_URL` and runtime `FORGE_APP_ORIGIN` as sensitive and withholds their
values. The connector's decrypt request and CLI environment execution did not
reveal them. No production object-storage environment references appear in the
listed variables. Web references include Better Auth, Resend and agent-signing
secrets; runtime references include the agent-channel secret. Secret values are
not included here.

Separately, read-only SQL confirms the **local application's configured** Neon
connection: project `raspy-union-96305162`, branch `br-muddy-queen-zaeeysjt`, database
`neondb`, PostgreSQL 18.6, pooled host
`ep-lingering-bread-zazpwrxp-pooler.c-2.eu-west-2.aws.neon.tech`. Latest journal row:
id 26, timestamp `1792843627355`, hash
`f75aa12984dcf6bc851fb30dd4faf4d314302b9c529a075e0f1ae1594a8a81f1`.
This is **not evidence** that Vercel serves that same branch. Local migration 0026
was applied only to isolated test/staging databases in this implementation.

Before production changes, an operator must verify the deployed connection's
hostname/project/branch/database and migration journal through a trusted runtime
diagnostic or deployment-secret reference, record the actual source revision, and
confirm runtime callback origin plus durable storage configuration. Do not infer a
commit from current Git HEAD or switch production to the local DB merely because
that connection is available. FOR-25 stays In Progress while these gaps remain.

migrationDocument.title: Forge isolated staging and serialized migration rehearsal
migrationDocument.content:
# Database migration ownership and rehearsal

FOR-27/FOR-28 implementation evidence, updated 29 October 2026. Production execution stays
disabled until FOR-25 verifies the actual serving database and source revision.

## Provisioned targets

| Use | Neon branch | Direct host | Database | Lifecycle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Persistent staging | `br-autumn-union-za0opf1e`, renamed `staging` | `ep-blue-shadow-zauhwkjz.c-2.eu-west-2.aws.neon.tech` | `forge_staging` | No expiry |
| Disposable rehearsal | `br-little-pond-zabdmew3` | `ep-fancy-firefly-zacgehbx.c-2.eu-west-2.aws.neon.tech` | `forge_migration_rehearsal` | Expires 2026-10-29 15:30:00 UTC |

The persistent staging branch was originally a schema-only root. The current
rehearsal replaces an expired disposable branch and is an expiring child of
isolated staging; its distinct rehearsal database started empty. Earlier
checkpoint references below describe the retired rehearsal. Before reuse, read-only SQL
confirmed the isolated branch/database identities and empty application data. New empty
databases avoid adopting the rowless schema-only copy's empty migration journal.
At the original checkpoint, staging and rehearsal applied all 29 then-checked-in
migrations. The latest checkpoint below advances both current targets to 36. No production rows were copied, no branches were manually
deleted, and the default branch/application connection selection was unchanged.

Staging is a database foundation. Hosted web/runtime, isolated object storage,
OAuth clients, provider sandbox credentials, fixture lifecycle and deploy guards
remain FOR-27 work. Existing test-branch `neondb` databases are separate from the
two named databases above.

## Operator entry point

Run `bun run db:migrate` from `apps/forge` with an explicitly selected direct
`DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED` and all four identity fields:

* `FORGE_MIGRATION_ENVIRONMENT`: `staging` or `rehearsal`.
* `FORGE_MIGRATION_BRANCH_ID`: the exact checked-in branch ID.
* `FORGE_MIGRATION_HOST`: the exact direct hostname.
* `FORGE_MIGRATION_DATABASE`: the exact database name.

Supply the credential privately from the Neon connection manager or deployment
secret store. Do not paste a connection string into tickets, documentation or
logs. Explicit process values take precedence over local environment files. The
runner does not modify local connection files. Application traffic continues to
use pooled URLs; migrations use a dedicated direct connection.

`scripts/lib/database-targets.ts` allows only the verified isolated targets.
Changing an environment name cannot turn a production connection into an allowed
target. The runner compares actual SQL branch/database identity before any DDL.
`db:push` now exits with instructions to generate a versioned migration. Direct
invocation of external tools remains an operator privilege outside this script;
production deployment credentials must not be available to untrusted build jobs.

## Serialization and failure behavior

One connected PostgreSQL session acquires advisory lock `646735021` **before**
reading the journal. A competing runner fails with `MIGRATION_BUSY`. The owner
validates that every applied hash/timestamp is an exact prefix of the release
files; missing, edited, extra or out-of-order history fails closed. The runner
wraps pending statements and journal writes in one transaction, with a five-second
lock timeout and five-minute statement timeout. Closing the session releases the
lock after a crash. No model, mail or payment calls run inside this transaction.

A failed migration rolls back its schema/data and receipt. A lost connection at
commit has an unknown outcome until the journal is re-read; retrying identical
files either applies the absent transaction or reports zero pending migrations.
Do not edit an applied migration. Add an expansion migration, deploy code that
supports both schemas, run resumable keyed backfills separately, verify counts,
then contract only after old app versions and durable jobs drain. This runner
does not make arbitrary destructive SQL or a long backfill safe.

The CLI redacts driver error details, which can contain private SQL values.
Inspect the migration journal on the explicitly verified target after any failed
or interrupted run; never interpret a timeout as proof of rollback.

## Verified evidence and remaining release checks

`serialized-migrations.postgres.test.ts` applied the real migration history to the
dedicated database. Three PostgreSQL cases passed:

1. Two independent connections competing for an appended migration yielded one
   owner, one busy rejection and one journal receipt; replay applied zero changes.
2. An injected SQL failure rolled back the fixture mutation and its journal row.
   Correcting the unapplied migration applied exactly once; retry was a no-op.
3. Edited applied history was refused before new migration work.

Three safety unit cases cover exact target matching, pooled/wrong hosts/databases,
an attempted production branch under a rehearsal name, and actual branch mismatch
before locking or DDL. Fixture cleanup removes only the invocation's random table
and exact hashes. No live database objects are reset by the tests.

FOR-28 remains In Progress: full old/new app rollback compatibility, resumable
backfill recovery and the hosted staging release rehearsal are still required.
FOR-27 remains In Progress until all staging resources and provider identities are
isolated. Neither passing helper tests nor the existence of a staging database
closes those release contracts.

Billing-grace expansion and provider-subscription binding (0027/0028) have since been applied to staging and rehearsal; both now contain the complete 29-migration history. The three migration fault/ownership cases passed again. The shared read path was also verified against the prior table schema without writes. Production execution remains disabled.

Migration 0029 adds the frozen scheduled-cancellation boundary and updates the counter helper. It was applied only to isolated staging/rehearsal, now 30 migrations. The complete-history migration ownership/failure cases passed again.


## Full-refund migration follow-up · 28 October 2026

Versioned migration 0030 adds the retained refunded-period history and updates member admission to deny refunded paid capacity. All 31 migrations are applied on the exact isolated staging and rehearsal targets. Three serialized migration ownership/fault cases pass against the complete history. The serving/default database is unchanged and still lacks the new production-readiness expansions; production rollout remains separately gated. See `docs/subscription-refunds.md`.


## Immediate termination migration follow-up · 28 October 2026

Migration 0031 adds finite provider-backed terminal state and makes SQL member admission deny paid capacity immediately on final revocation. All 32 migrations are applied only to isolated staging and rehearsal; three serialized ownership/fault cases pass against the complete history. Thirty-one billing-state and fifteen real-auth member cases pass on staging. Existing members stay authorized. No serving/default database or connection configuration changed. See `docs/subscription-termination.md`; production rollout remains separately gated.


## Upgrade-refund access migration follow-up · 28 October 2026

Migration 0032 records paid Plus grant identity and aligns refund-aware Starter fallback with SQL admission. All 33 migrations are applied only to isolated staging/rehearsal; three full-history migration ownership/fault cases pass. Staging: 43 billing and 16 real-auth membership cases pass, including temporary admission refusal without base proof and resumed paid Starter admission after verification. Existing member sessions are preserved. The serving/default database and local connection files are unchanged. See `docs/subscription-plan-changes.md`.


## No-pause migration follow-up · 29 October 2026

Migration 0033 adds a finite provider-backed unsupported-pause cutoff and aligns SQL admission with shared access policy. A fresh empty rehearsal database on the current expiring branch applied all 34 migrations; all 3 ownership/fault cases passed. Only then did the exact persistent staging target apply the one pending migration, now also 34. Current staging tests pass 52 billing and 17 real-auth membership cases. No serving/default database or local connection setting changed; no branches were manually deleted. See `docs/subscription-pause-policy.md`.


## Renewal-currency request migration · 29 October 2026

Migration 0034 adds the durable currency-request history, one-pending-intent index and finite-boundary/fixed-seven-day-deadline constraints. The isolated rehearsal database passed all 35 migrations and 3 full-history ownership/fault cases; exact persistent staging then applied the one pending expansion, now 35. Staging passes 58 billing and 17 real-auth member cases. This does not execute a currency migration or grant checkout grace; no serving/default database or local connection changed. See `docs/renewal-currency-change.md`.


## Original monthly anniversary expansion · 29 October 2026

Migration 0035 adds nullable original source period, anchor day and next boundary to durable currency intents, with all-null legacy or fully populated finite/range constraints. Original-day capture requires a matching verified source replay and atomic audit; no guessed data backfill is performed. A fresh empty database on br-little-pond-zabdmew3 passed all 36 migrations and all 3 ownership/fault cases. Exact persistent staging then applied one pending migration. Billing (62) and real-auth membership (17) cases pass.

An initial CLI database-create command used unsupported `--branch-id`; the CLI selected the default branch and created a new empty rehearsal database there. Verified SQL showed that exact new database contained zero user objects, then it was removed. No DDL migration, user data or existing serving database was changed. The correct command uses `--branch` and its returned identity must be verified before migration. The isolated allowlist and actual-SQL identity checks remained mandatory throughout.

graceDocument.title: Forge failed-renewal grace and subscription reconciliation
graceDocument.content:
# Failed-renewal access and reconciliation

FOR-109/FOR-111 implementation record, 28 October 2026.

## Confirmed policy

The user selected **7 days of paid access after a failed paid renewal**, including
the included AI allowance and paid overage under the workspace's **existing**
explicit opt-in and finite spending cap. Entering grace never creates consent or
raises that cap. A card-free trial still cannot incur overage. Grace lasts exactly
168 hours from the original failure, with a half-open interval: access is Free at
the expiry timestamp. Retries and unrelated subscription updates cannot restart
the episode. Payment recovery clears it. A later genuinely failed renewal can
start a new episode after recovery.

An unpaid first subscription cannot obtain grace: the stored subscription must
have a previous verified paid activation. Existing workspace members retain access
after grace expires; new joins follow the Free five-member rule. Do not evict
members, delete their data or reissue a trial. First Free/trial-to-paid purchase
still receives the separately confirmed fresh paid AI pool; ledger grants and
settlement remain FOR-76 work.

## Provider and trust boundaries

Polar distinguishes recoverable `past_due` from revocation, and emits an active
event when payment recovers. Its provider retry schedule is separate from Forge's
chosen access window. [Polar past-due events](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/webhooks/subscription.past_due),
[payment recovery and grace settings](https://polar.sh/features/subscriptions).

The pinned `@polar-sh/sdk@1.0.2` versioned `2026-10` client exposes `past_due_at`.
Forge requires that original provider failure timestamp; it does not anchor grace
to webhook delivery or an unrelated `modified_at` update. Missing required
timestamps fail reconciliation rather than minting a fresh window.

`POST /api/billing/polar/webhook` stays off unless both billing and
`FORGE_BILLING_WEBHOOKS_ENABLED=true` are explicitly configured. It bounds the body
at 1 MiB, verifies the exact bytes through the pinned SDK and validates the event's
identity shape. A signed event triggers a fresh subscription fetch. Its customer
external ID must match `forge:workspace:<workspaceId>`, with one approved
environment/product/currency mapping and monthly cadence. Webhook metadata,
success redirects, browser plan names and event payload status cannot grant access.

The implementation now also handles scheduled-canceled/uncanceled reconciliation.
Immediate revocation and standard full/partial subscription-period refunds are
implemented in the subsequent guides. Pause, unsupported invoice allocations and
other unimplemented event policies still return a retryable failure. Keep the route
disabled until the remaining lifecycle paths, periodic reconciliation and billing
release gate are complete. No live Polar credentials, webhook configuration or charges were
changed by this work.

## Persistence and ordering

Migration `0027_subscription_grace` expands the existing entitlement authority;
it does not introduce a second paid-plan source. It adds provider version/hash,
period, prior paid activation, original failure and grace expiry. Checks reject
malformed provider identity, invalid periods and grace beyond exactly 168 hours.
The member-counter helper uses the same time-aware policy for direct SQL imports
and auth writes. Migration `0028_subscription_binding` ensures a provider
subscription/environment can belong to only one workspace.

One transaction locks the workspace before its first entitlement row can exist,
then writes the projection, receipt and audit record atomically. Receipt keys are
unique by provider environment/event ID. Reusing an ID with different bytes or
workspace/subscription identity fails. Older snapshots are recorded as stale;
equal versions with conflicting contents are rejected for reconciliation. Duplicate
deliveries do not repeat projection or audit effects. During a failure episode,
the persisted timestamp can move earlier, never later. No raw payload or customer
PII is stored in the receipt; only digest, identity and outcome.

Read-time access checks enforce expiry without depending on a webhook or sweep.
Expired provider entitlements cannot retain paid features through stale feature
overrides. Existing opt-in/cap authorization must still be checked by the spending
ledger; `allowsExistingOverage` is permission to consider that existing authority,
not a new payment authorization.

## Deployment and compatibility

Both migrations were applied only to the verified isolated `forge_staging`
database, branch `br-autumn-union-za0opf1e`, through the serialized exact-target
runner. It now has all **29** checked-in migrations. The disposable rehearsal
database also passed the current migration history. Production/default databases
were not migrated and local connection files were not changed.

Security and member-limit readers select whole-row JSON and validate its fields,
so the pre-expansion table can still be read without selecting absent columns.
A read-only probe against the configured legacy database succeeded with zero
mutations. Projection/webhook writes require the expanded schema. Deploy the
migrations before enabling billing handlers; retain the gate until every serving
instance has the new expiry policy. Missing provider evidence fails closed.

## Verification and remaining acceptance

* Signed-boundary/provider unit tests cover exact-body signatures, altered bodies,
  missing/stale signatures, body limits, disabled routes, malformed identity,
  catalog/customer mismatches, unpaid states, missing failure evidence and safe
  error responses.
* Eight PostgreSQL cases cover concurrent signed duplicate delivery, one receipt and
  audit effect, no grace restart, payment recovery, stale events, initial unpaid
  checkout, expiry without a sweep, stale-feature-override denial, event/version
  conflicts, cross-workspace subscription binding, a daylight-saving boundary and atomic rollback when the audit insert fails.
* Twelve real PostgreSQL/Better Auth membership cases pass, including acceptance
  beyond five during valid grace, refusal after expiry, preservation of the refused
  invitation and authorized access for an existing sixth member.
* Three PostgreSQL migration-owner/fault cases pass against the complete current
  history. These are isolated fixture checks, with own records cleaned up.

FOR-111 remains In Progress. Remaining refund/immediate-revocation/pause policy, scheduled
provider reconciliation, entitlement-change communications, commercial usage
ledger integration and live Polar sandbox/candidate release checks are still
required. Passing these tests is not completion of the entire billing feature.


Period-end cancellation is now implemented as described in [the cancellation guide](subscription-cancellation.md). Staging/rehearsal contain 30 migrations; thirteen billing-state and thirteen real-auth member cases pass, including cancellation/grace interaction and term-end access. UI/public command wiring and the full billing release gate remain open.


## Immediate termination follow-up

The user confirmed that final provider termination overrides remaining payment grace. Current Polar `unpaid` after retry exhaustion is final revocation, even if retries end before the ordinary seven-day Forge grace boundary. A durable terminal marker now denies paid access while preserving the original failure/grace history and existing members. See `docs/subscription-termination.md` for current implementation and verification. Earlier checkpoint counts above are historical.

cancellationDocument.title: Forge period-end cancellation and retained access
cancellationDocument.content:
# Subscription cancellation at billing-period end

FOR-109/FOR-110/FOR-111 implementation record, 28 October 2026.

## Confirmed behavior

The user selected **keep paid access until the current billing period ends** when
an owner cancels. The provider command schedules cancellation; it does not revoke
immediately, issue refunds, prorate prices or change seats. Existing members keep
workspace access after paid access ends; new joins then follow Free capacity.
Cancellation does not create another trial or AI pool. During failed-payment
grace, access still ends at the earlier applicable grace/term boundary.

Polar exposes `cancel_at_period_end` separately from immediate revocation and
records the effective end of the subscription. Forge sets that flag only and
checks the returned/current state before reporting a confirmed schedule.
[Polar subscription update](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/subscriptions/update),
[subscription lifecycle](https://polar.sh/features/subscriptions).

## Server command and authority

The canonical `cancelWorkspaceSubscriptionAtPeriodEnd` entry point wires the live
context resolver into `PolarSubscriptionCancellation.schedule`, requiring a first-party owner/admin
Actor. `readCancellationContext` rechecks live workspace membership and derives
the environment-bound subscription ID from the server entitlement record. No
browser-supplied subscription/customer ID, price, seat quantity or effective date
is accepted. The command rechecks roles and binding after its first provider read,
immediately before the provider write. The atomic projection also reauthorizes
the Actor before returning a cached receipt.

Current provider customer identity, approved product/currency and cadence must
match. The only write body is `{cancel_at_period_end: true}`. If cancellation is
already scheduled, retries do not write again. After a lost response/timeout, a
new provider read can confirm the schedule without duplicating the write. A moved
period or unconfirmed schedule returns an error requiring reconciliation; no
guessed success date is returned. Confirmed termination is distinguished from a
pending schedule in the result.

The backend command and live-context resolver are prepared and tested. Wiring the
Forge billing UI/public action, durable external-effect processing and real Polar
sandbox verification remain FOR-110/FOR-33/FOR-112 work. This implementation did
not cancel any live subscription or enable billing.

## Durable cutoff and replay

Migration `0029_subscription_cancellation` adds `cancel_at_period_end` and
`cancellation_period_end` to the existing authority. Constraints require a finite
cutoff inside the associated period. The earliest scheduled cutoff remains frozen
across later updates or period shifts while cancellation stays scheduled. Only a
fresh, authoritative uncanceled state clears it; a stale webhook cannot restore
access. Equal-version changes cannot reactivate access.

The state fingerprint omits the new flag when false, preserving compatibility
with existing projection hashes. The only equal-version expansion permitted is
adding a restrictive cancellation boundary to an otherwise identical old snapshot;
it cannot change a plan, status or period or reenable access.

Signed canceled/uncanceled events use the same current-provider reconciliation as
active/past-due events. A completed scheduled cancellation retains the stored prior
paid proof and expires at its original boundary. An unpaid initial subscription
cannot receive paid time from a canceled event. A cancellation arriving during
grace preserves that original failure and expiry instead of converting it into a
full unpaid month. Immediate early revocations now use the confirmed terminal-access rule in
`docs/subscription-termination.md`; normal cancellation remains at period end.

Feature checks, Better Auth preflight and the SQL member-counter helper all apply
the cutoff at read/insertion time. Expiry does not depend on the final webhook or
a sweep. The old-schema JSON reader remains compatible before expansion. Roll out
the migration before any command/projection writes; do not enable customer billing
until all serving instances enforce the boundary.

## Verified scope

* Unit/provider checks verify the exact write body, session/role requirements,
  live reauthorization, already-scheduled retry, lost-response recovery, confirmed
  completion, identity mismatch and moved/unconfirmed boundaries.
* Thirteen PostgreSQL billing-state cases pass: the original eight grace/receipt
  cases plus owner scheduling and revoked receipt replay, role revocation during
  provider lookup, frozen cutoff and uncancellation, grace/cancellation interaction,
  and pre-expansion fingerprint compatibility with unpaid-initial refusal.
* Thirteen real Better Auth/PostgreSQL membership cases pass, including admission
  before term end, refusal after completion, preservation of the refused invitation
  and continued authorized access for an existing sixth member.
* Three migration-owner/fault cases pass against all **30** migrations on the
  dedicated rehearsal database. Migration 0029 was applied only to isolated staging
  and rehearsal; the serving/default database and local connection files are unchanged.

Billing remains disabled. Pause and plan-transition policy,
periodic reconciliation/outbox communication, commercial ledger integration,
customer-portal configuration and actual Polar sandbox/candidate tests remain.

Resubscribing after term end is a remaining release check: verify the old subscription is terminal before replacing its workspace binding with a newly paid subscription, retain old receipts/usage and refuse two active subscriptions. The current conflict guard stays strict until that path is implemented.


## Full-refund follow-up

A full refund of the current period now ends paid access immediately. The separate refund history overrides the cancellation schedule and cannot be cleared by later active subscription updates. See `docs/subscription-refunds.md` for implementation and current evidence; the earlier checkpoint counts above describe the cancellation commit.
