Partial refunds now keep paid access and its existing cancellation/grace boundary unchanged. Current order verification can promote an earlier partial event to full revocation when cumulative refunds reach the complete charged amount. See the refund guide for current verification evidence.

Immediate provider termination now overrides both the cancellation boundary and payment grace. The owner command reconciles a detected terminal subscription without another provider write, including termination during a moved-period scheduling race. See the termination guide for the new checkpoint.

refundDocument.title: Forge full-refund access revocation and durable reconciliation
refundDocument.content:
# Subscription-period refunds

FOR-109/FOR-111 implementation record, 28 October 2026.

## Confirmed policy

A full refund of the charge for the current subscription period ends paid access
immediately after verified reconciliation. Existing members keep workspace access;
new joins follow Free capacity, including grandfathering above five members.
Included paid AI and opted-in paid overage stop being authorized by that term.
A refund does not erase consumption, reservations, receipts or audit history and
does not mint a new Free/trial/paid pool. Commercial ledger settlement and in-flight
run handling remain FOR-76 integration work; this implementation enforces access.

A partial refund keeps paid access unchanged. It cannot restore ended access,
modify the paid-through or grace boundary, reset the included pool, or grant another
trial. Several partial refunds that cumulatively cover the full net charge and tax
follow the full-refund rule once the current provider order verifies that total.

A genuinely paid later period is separate. An old refund cannot revoke a
nonoverlapping later period or a different subscription/environment. A refunded
term cannot supply prior-paid proof for a subsequent failed renewal: reconciliation
clears that proof durably before considering grace, including on repeated retries.

## Provider verification

`order.refunded` means either a full or partial refund in Polar. Forge verifies the
exact signed bytes with the pinned SDK, validates the event identity, then fetches
the current order from the configured provider environment. It never trusts the
webhook's amount, plan, period or status fields.

The order must match the workspace customer, requested order ID, approved product
and currency, subscription ID and subscription-create/cycle billing reason. Require
a positive net charge, consistent total, zero applied balance and one nonprorated,
dated subscription line. Full refunds require refunded status and exactly full net
and tax refund amounts. Partial refunds require partially-refunded status, positive
cumulative refunds below the charge total, and neither net nor tax refunds above
their corresponding charged amounts. Contradictory statuses/totals are refused.
The billed period comes from that order line, never from a subscription whose period
may have advanced. Missing dates, unsupported mixed/balance-credit allocations, one-time
and overage charges return a reconciliation-required response with no access change
and no successful receipt. These require further allocation work before launch.

Sources: [Polar refund event](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/webhooks/order.refunded),
[order fields](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/orders/get), and the pinned
`@polar-sh/sdk@1.0.2` versioned 2026-10 `OrderItemSchema.start_timestamp/end_timestamp`.
Live API compatibility and actual sandbox refund fixtures remain a release gate.

## Durable reconciliation and enforcement

Migration 0030 expands the existing entitlement projection with `refunded_periods`,
an append-only application history containing environment, subscription/order IDs,
billed start/end and verified order modification time. It contains no raw payload,
email, address or credentials. Under the same workspace lock used by subscription
reconciliation, the refund sink appends an order once, writes an audit event and
persists the digest-only event receipt in one transaction. A failed audit/receipt
write rolls everything back. Conflicting event reuse or changed order-period
identity is rejected. Duplicate delivery is idempotent. Different orders cannot
race away each other's history.

A verified partial refund writes its own audit event and an unchanged-outcome
receipt in the same transaction. It does not insert or update entitlement state,
including when it arrives before activation. Duplicates do not duplicate audits.
On replay, fetching a now-fully-refunded order can atomically promote that same
receipt and append the full-period denial; a lost later event cannot strand access.
A late partial snapshot never removes a full-refund denial or reactivates a period.
The prior event digest/identity must still match exactly before promotion.

The history can be recorded before first activation. Ordinary subscription upserts
never overwrite it. Both the shared TypeScript access policy and SQL member-admission
function deny a provider period overlapping a recorded refund for that subscription
and environment. This includes active, canceled and grace states; moving a boundary
slightly cannot clear the denial. A later active update cannot regrant the term.

Workspace security, Better Auth admission and team thread-summary eligibility use
the shared access policy. Refunded/expired Polar state cannot retain paid feature
overrides. Existing sessions and members remain authorized for their workspace.
The whole-row JSON reader tolerates the old schema before expansion; migrate before
billing writes and deploy all enforcement consumers before enabling the webhook.

## Verification and rollout

Migration 0030 is applied only to `forge_staging` on `br-autumn-union-za0opf1e`
and `forge_migration_rehearsal` on `br-square-sky-za2iavfk`. Each has 31 migrations.
The serving/default database and local connection files are unchanged. No provider
refund, cancellation, charge or production deployment was performed.

Coverage includes signed dispatch and provider re-fetch; net/tax and allocation
refusal; duplicate/conflicting delivery; refund before activation; concurrent refunds
and activation; audit rollback; later active updates; overlapping boundaries;
refunded proof followed by failed renewal/retry and genuine payment recovery;
nonoverlapping later periods; feature-override denial; SQL admission; existing
member sessions and pending invitations. The verified checkpoint has **1,325 app tests, 4 workflow tests, 18 PostgreSQL billing
cases, 14 real-auth membership cases and 3 full-history migration fault cases** passing.
TypeScript, changed-file lint/format checks, diff checks and the production build
(including protected Workflow handlers) pass. The checkpoint JSON records source digests.

The full-refund checkpoint above describes commit `53d175f`. The partial-refund
follow-up verifies **1,331 app tests, 4 workflow tests, 24 PostgreSQL billing cases
and 14 real-auth membership cases**, including unchanged active/grace/canceled
state, duplicate delivery, partial-to-full receipt promotion, late partial snapshots,
preactivation ordering and partial audit/receipt rollback. TypeScript, changed-file
lint/format and production build pass. No new migration was required; migration
fault evidence remains the prior full-refund checkpoint's three cases.

Billing stays disabled. FOR-111 remains In Progress for pause/plan-transition
policy, verified old/new subscription replacement, periodic
reconciliation and durable effects/communications, commercial ledger integration,
provider configuration and actual Polar sandbox/candidate validation. This record
completes the confirmed full/partial-refund access slices, not the entire billing issue.

Immediate provider termination is now separately implemented and takes precedence over paid/grace access. Ordinary subscription or partial-refund updates cannot reopen it. See `docs/subscription-termination.md`; the refund checkpoint counts above describe the earlier commits.


## Upgrade-only refund follow-up

A full refund of only the prorated Plus-upgrade charge now restores the verified already-paid Starter period. This differs from refunding the full base subscription charge. Partial refunds still keep access unchanged. Migration 0032 and stored paid invoice references prevent stale payment proof from regranting refunded Plus. Missing base evidence removes unproven Plus and retries before restoring Starter; a new verified paid grant remains separate. See `docs/subscription-plan-changes.md` for current checks and limits. Earlier checkpoint counts above are historical.


## Upgrade-refund renewal follow-up · 29 October 2026

The user confirmed Starter at the next renewal after fully refunding only a Plus upgrade. The refund handler commits access restriction first, then verifies and schedules the approved same-currency Starter product with explicit next-period timing. Billed and scheduled seats, current charge and period are preserved. Existing refund intent redrives failed/lost responses and atomic confirmation; terminal/newer paid grants cannot be overwritten by old refund confirmation. No new migration or live billing change. See `docs/subscription-plan-changes.md` for current verification, retry boundaries and remaining release gates.

terminationDocument.title: Forge immediate subscription termination and access enforcement
terminationDocument.content:
# Immediate provider termination

FOR-109/FOR-111 implementation record, 28 October 2026.

## Confirmed behavior

The user confirmed that immediate termination by Polar ends paid access immediately,
even during the seven-day failed-renewal grace period. Normal owner cancellation
still runs until the current period ends. Existing members retain workspace access;
new admissions and paid-feature checks resolve to Free, preserving grandfathered
members above five. Termination does not erase consumption, outstanding reservations,
refund history or receipts and does not create another AI pool or trial.

Polar distinguishes recoverable `past_due` from final revocation, which can include
`unpaid` after retry exhaustion. Final revocation overrides remaining grace even if
the provider exhausts its retries before Forge's ordinary grace boundary. Forge
verifies signed bytes and identity, then fetches current provider state rather than
using the webhook's status as authority. The configured environment, workspace
customer, approved product/currency and monthly cadence must match.
[Polar revoked event](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/2026-10/subscription_revoked),
[subscription API](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/subscriptions/get).

## Verified terminal proof

The adapter recognizes current `unpaid`, an unscheduled `canceled` subscription, or
a canceled subscription with an actual `ended_at` timestamp. An actual end must be
no later than provider modification time; active/past-due state with an actual end
is contradictory and is refused. If a terminal state has no end timestamp, use
its authoritative modification time. Required period/identity fields must remain
valid; malformed provider state returns reconciliation-required rather than being
acknowledged. `unpaid` normalizes to the existing canceled storage contract.

Scheduled canceled state with no actual end remains nonterminal and retains only
its existing paid-through/grace access. A completed scheduled cancellation becomes
terminal at its actual end. A true termination is reconciled even if the provider
period moves while an owner cancellation command is running. The command performs
no additional provider write when it finds a terminated subscription.

## Durable access denial

Migration 0031 adds nullable `terminated_at`, constrained to finite provider-backed
state, and expands the atomic member-admission helper. One workspace lock serializes
termination with normal subscription and refund reconciliation. A first terminal
snapshot can bind the subscription before any activation, with no prior-paid proof.
For an already bound subscription, termination changes only its terminal marker
and update time; paid/failure/grace/cancellation clocks and the normal state
fingerprint remain available as history. Audit and receipt persistence are atomic.

Terminal proof is restrictive and can arrive with an older or equal provider
version without overwriting the newer normal projection. The earliest terminal
marker wins. A replayed event that previously fetched active state can now apply
verified terminal proof using the same identity/digest and receipt. Conflicting
identity or digest reuse is rejected, and a failed audit rolls the marker/receipt
change back for retry. Live owner/admin authorization is rechecked before a
command's cached receipt can be returned.

Once marked terminal, ordinary active, past-due, canceled or uncanceled snapshots
for that subscription cannot clear the marker or grant a later period. Shared
TypeScript access, workspace security/override checks, team thread-summary access,
Better Auth preflight and SQL member insertion enforce the marker independently
of the stored plan/status or any sweep. A separately verified paid replacement
subscription needs the existing explicit old-terminal/new-paid binding workflow;
that workflow remains a release gate. Do not relax the binding conflict guard or
infer reinstatement from an ordinary active snapshot.

## Verification and rollout

Migration 0031 is applied only to isolated `forge_staging` on
`br-autumn-union-za0opf1e` and `forge_migration_rehearsal` on
`br-square-sky-za2iavfk`. Both contain 32 migrations. The serving/default database
and local connection files are unchanged. The whole-row JSON access reader still
tolerates the schema before expansion; migrate before enabling writes and ensure
all serving access consumers enforce termination before enabling customer billing.

Verified: **1,343 app tests, 4 workflow tests, 31 PostgreSQL billing cases,
15 real-auth membership cases and 3 full-history migration fault cases**. Coverage
includes signed revoked/current-provider state; active/grace/canceled termination;
preactivation ordering; older/equal-version restrictive proof; later active/grace
snapshots; cached active-event promotion; audit rollback; frozen earliest marker;
paid feature overrides; SQL capacity; existing member sessions and pending invites;
and cancellation/termination races. TypeScript and changed-file lint/format checks
pass. The production build, including protected Workflow handlers, passes. The
checkpoint records source digests.

No provider termination, cancellation, refund or charge was performed. Nothing is
deployed; live billing stays disabled. FOR-111 remains In Progress for verified
subscription binding replacement, pause/plan-transition policy, periodic
reconciliation/outbox/communications, invoice allocation, commercial ledger
integration and actual Polar sandbox/candidate validation. This completes the
confirmed immediate-termination access slice.

planChangeDocument.title: Forge paid tier changes, payment proof and upgrade refunds
planChangeDocument.content:
# Paid tier changes and upgrade refunds

FOR-109/FOR-110/FOR-111 implementation record, updated 29 October 2026.

## Confirmed behavior

Starter→Plus upgrades take effect immediately after successful payment, with the
prorated difference invoiced now. Plus→Starter downgrades take effect at the next
renewal without a mid-period charge. Member quantity changes still apply only at
renewal. Tier changes preserve the current billing currency, billing anniversary,
current billed seats, original paid activation and accumulated usage. They do not
start another trial or first-purchase AI pool. Both paid tiers retain the already
confirmed US$5-per-active-member allowance policy.

If upgrade payment fails or is unverified, keep the existing Starter contract and
its paid-through/cancellation/grace boundaries. An unpaid upgrade cannot create or
restart payment grace or extend the old term. Grant Plus only after verifying a
paid, non-fully-refunded invoice for the current Plus period. A changed provider
product or an active status alone is insufficient evidence for this elevation.

A full refund of only the prorated Plus-upgrade charge returns the workspace to
Starter for its already-paid base period and schedules Starter at the next renewal.
The next-renewal rule was confirmed on 29 October 2026. Restoring current access requires a verified, still-paid
Starter base invoice. A full refund of that separate base charge still ends all
paid access. Partial refunds keep access unchanged. Existing members, usage,
reservations, refund records and receipts are preserved in every case.

## Owner/admin command

`changeWorkspacePlan` wires `readPlanChangeContext` into `PolarPlanChanger.change`.
It accepts a trusted Actor and a Starter/Plus target, with no browser-supplied
subscription ID, price, currency or seat count. The resolver rechecks current
owner/admin membership, environment-bound subscription identity, valid paid access
and the atomic active-member counter. API-key and ordinary-member actors cannot
manage billing. The command rechecks live authority/binding before each provider
write; a changed membership quantity requires a fresh seat reconciliation.

The upgrade body is exactly `{product_id: approvedPlusInExistingCurrency,
proration_behavior: "invoice"}`. Downgrade uses the approved Starter product with
`proration_behavior: "next_period"`. No price, trial, currency, period reset or
immediate seat quantity is sent. Current subscription ownership, approved monthly
catalog, period, seat count and pending changes must match. Canceled, terminal,
trial subscriptions require their own lifecycle path. Pause/resume is excluded at
launch; unexpected provider pauses are recorded and refused. An existing
failed upgrade can be inspected again without resubmitting its invoice.

After writes, fetch current provider state and verify the original period,
currency and billed seats. A downgrade must leave Plus and its current amount
unchanged with an explicit Starter change at the original period end. Retrying a
confirmed change does not send the product update again. A lost response is
reconciled from current provider state; an unconfirmed or conflicting result is
not reported as success. A detected termination is reconciled before refusing the
plan change.

Polar's immediate product update clears pending changes. The adapter therefore
restores the latest server-resolved member quantity using a separate renewal-only
seat update. The seat scheduler now preserves an approved pending Starter downgrade
when adding, replacing or withdrawing the quantity change. Withdrawing a pending
downgrade clears that pending row and restores the seat schedule. Product and seat
updates are never combined in an ambiguous union-shaped request.

Polar exposes immediate invoice and next-period modes; its current source also
shows pending quantity merging and clearing during immediate product changes.
These are tested through the pinned `@polar-sh/sdk@1.0.2` versioned 2026-10 client
boundary. Real sandbox confirmation remains required.
[Polar update API](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/2026-10/subscriptions/update-subscription),
[subscription behavior](https://polar.sh/features/subscriptions),
[pending-change implementation](https://github.com/polarsource/polar/blob/main/server/polar/subscription/repository.py).

## Payment proof and reconciliation

`findPaidUpgradeOrder` fetches current orders scoped to workspace customer,
subscription, approved Plus product and billing period. It verifies paid status,
zero amount due, net/tax totals, refund amounts, currency, identity and dated lines.
An upgrade invoice must contain consistent prorated lines within the current
period; a paid renewal must cover that exact full period. Zero-value paid invoices
are supported, but contradictory flags, fully refunded invoices and unrelated
charges cannot grant Plus. Three pages of at most 100 candidates bound each call;
missing proof leaves payment pending rather than inferring success.

The signed webhook also accepts `order.paid`, re-fetches that order's identity and
reconciles the current subscription and invoice evidence. A Starter→Plus snapshot
without evidence keeps the previous effective plan and all contract clocks. An
early provider downgrade likewise cannot remove already-purchased Plus before its
period ends. At the next authoritative period the Starter change can apply.

Payment proof is separate from the normal provider-state fingerprint. A matching
provider version or a replayed event that formerly lacked payment proof can now
promote Starter to Plus. Older provider state cannot. Terminal/full-refund denial
still takes precedence. Actor reauthorization, plan projection, confirmation audit
and digest-only receipt persistence are atomic. Command responses and confirmation
audits use the effective projection inside the workspace lock, so a refund racing
a paid-order fetch cannot produce a false Plus-success result. If a command audit
fails after Polar accepted payment, retrying observes the target and proof without
charging again. No raw invoice/customer payload is persisted in these receipts.

## Upgrade-only refund and Starter evidence

Migration 0032 adds the accepted paid Plus order ID and extends typed refund
history with an explicit upgrade marker and optional base Starter invoice/period.
The refund adapter recognizes consistent, fully refunded prorated Plus lines and
fetches a paid or partially refunded, nonprorated Starter create/cycle invoice for
the same subscription, currency and original period end. It does not infer a paid
Starter term merely because a Plus refund exists.

The refund, audit and receipt transaction records that marker and changes the
current effective tier to Starter when the refunded invoice supplied its Plus
grant. Shared access and SQL member admission validate the Starter base window.
This also works when the refund arrives before activation. If the base invoice
cannot be verified yet, remove unproven Plus access and return a retryable response;
replaying the same event can fill the verified base reference and restore Starter.
The original paid period is never extended. Existing member sessions remain valid,
and paid Starter admission resumes after base verification.

A delayed payment proof for the refunded upgrade is rejected by its recorded order
ID. An old upgrade refund cannot replace a separately verified newer paid Plus
grant. A full base-period refund or provider termination still denies paid access.
The SQL member-admission helper, whole-row JSON reader, workspace security and
thread-summary gates share these rules. Missing/expired base evidence cannot keep
paid capacity solely because the stored provider plan still says Plus.

## Starter renewal after an upgrade refund

`PolarUpgradeRefundRenewal` reads the durable verified upgrade-refund marker and
current environment-specific binding before any provider mutation. The signed
refund handler first commits the access restriction and original receipt, then
redrives this renewal step on every retry, including when base-invoice evidence
is temporarily unavailable. It acknowledges success only after scheduling and
confirmation; a network/provider/audit failure keeps the webhook retryable. No new
schema migration is needed: the existing full-upgrade-refund marker is the intent.

The only mutation is the approved Starter product in the subscription's existing
currency with `proration_behavior: "next_period"`. It sends no amount, seats,
refund, credit, cancellation, pause, trial or period reset. The adapter verifies
that current product, charge, billed seats, scheduled renewal seats and period
remain intact, and that the pending Starter product applies at the original end.
An already scheduled Starter change or an already-Starter subscription needs no
write. A lost response is recovered by fetching current provider state on retry.
It can schedule in past-due state without creating a payment or changing grace.

Live binding and refunded-grant identity are checked again before the write.
Atomic confirmation checks them under the workspace lock and writes an audit plus
digest-only receipt. If a separately paid newer Plus grant or replacement binding
has superseded the refunded grant, no old-refund confirmation is recorded.
Terminal provider proof is projected immediately; the adapter never uncancels or
unpauses a subscription. Scheduled cancellation/pause and unexpected periods or
pending changes remain retryable reconciliation exceptions, not silent success.
An old refund received after a genuine later term cannot downgrade that new term.

The owner/admin Plus command refuses to reuse an upgrade that has been fully
refunded or withdraw its Starter schedule. A new purchase requires a controlled
provider adjustment with fresh paid evidence; automatic repurchase remains gated.
Existing seat scheduling preserves the pending Starter product as member counts
change. Repeated signed deliveries cannot create duplicate confirmation effects.

## Verification and remaining release work

Verified: **1,412 app tests, 4 workflow tests, 46 PostgreSQL billing cases,
16 real-auth membership cases and 3 full-history migration fault cases**. Coverage
includes exact API bodies, retry/timeout recovery, pending seat/downgrade
composition, foreign and unpaid invoices, same-version payment promotion,
late-refund/payment ordering, base proof before activation, partial/full refund
separation, audit rollback, role revocation before charging, retained sessions and
restored Starter admission. TypeScript, changed-file lint/format and diff checks
pass. The production build, including protected Workflow handlers, passes; the
checkpoint records source digests. The initial broad run hit a timeout in the
unchanged review emoji picker; its isolated rerun and the final full run passed.

All 33 migrations were applied only to isolated staging and rehearsal. The renewal
follow-up uses the unchanged 33-migration staging database; migration fault results
are from the prior checkpoint. The
serving/default database and local connection files are unchanged. No live provider
invoice, refund, subscription or portal setting was changed, and nothing is
deployed. Live billing remains disabled.

These are prepared server commands and verified access/reconciliation behavior.
Public UI/actions, durable workspace serialization and effect/outbox processing,
ambiguous provider-outcome recovery, periodic reconciliation/communications,
commercial usage ledger integration, historical invoice allocations and actual
Polar sandbox/candidate flows remain required. Disable hosted portal plan/seat
changes that bypass Forge's asymmetric timing and membership rules before launch.

Starter renewal after a full upgrade-only refund is confirmed and implemented.
The controlled provider adjustment needed to buy Plus again while the refunded
provider product still says Plus remains gated; it cannot silently charge again
or restore Plus without new verified payment. Pause/resume is excluded at launch; `docs/subscription-pause-policy.md` records
its verified safeguards. Currency changes and team/issue/upload over-capacity
policies still need decisions. Keep FOR-110/FOR-111
In Progress until those policies and the remaining public/release gates are complete.
This is prepared backend behavior, not a live Polar sandbox/candidate result.
Durable workspace-wide external-effect serialization, periodic redrive and a
reactivation handler must enforce any pending refund intent before live billing.


The verification counts above describe the tier/refund-renewal checkpoint at `53f0226`. Current no-pause verification and the 34-migration staging/rehearsal follow-up are recorded in `docs/subscription-pause-policy.md`; the earlier checkpoint is historical.

pauseDocument.title: Forge launch cancellation policy and unsupported provider pauses
pauseDocument.content:
# Subscription pausing at launch

FOR-109/FOR-110/FOR-111 implementation record, 29 October 2026.

## Confirmed policy

Forge does not offer subscription pause or resume at launch. An owner/admin who
wants to stop future charges uses the already implemented period-end cancellation
path. Current paid access continues only through its valid original boundary;
refund, termination and grace restrictions still apply. No automatic cancellation,
unpause, credit, refund, new trial or usage pool is inferred from a pause event.

Before live billing, verify that customer-facing Polar portal settings and any
Forge billing UI do not expose a pause/resume path. This is a provider/candidate
release gate; no live organization or portal setting was changed here.

## Unexpected provider state

Polar represents pausing separately from its main subscription status. The pinned
2026-10 API returns `pause_at_period_end`, `paused_at` and `resumes_at`; checking
only `status: active` is insufficient. The adapter now requires and validates
those fields on every fetched subscription, including the actual `paused` status.
That status requires a verified pause timestamp and enters only the restrictive
projection path; it cannot create a paid activation or grace. Missing or contradictory dates fail
verification. Signed `subscription.paused` and `subscription.resumed` events are
accepted only as identities: the handler fetches current provider state rather
than trusting access or dates in the event body. A signed resume observed before
any pause delivery is also restrictive: its cutoff comes from the fetched provider
modification time, so it cannot become an unverified first paid activation.

An observed actual pause records its verified pause time as an access cutoff.
A scheduled pause records the current period end; it does not remove existing
paid access early. The shared policy denies paid features and existing paid
overage at or after that cutoff, including during failed-payment grace or a
verified Starter fallback. SQL member admission applies the same cutoff. Existing
members retain workspace/session access; additional joins follow Free capacity.

[Polar subscription API](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/2026-10/subscriptions/update-subscription).

## Durable reconciliation and commands

Migration 0033 adds finite provider-backed `unsupported_pause_at` and updates the
member-counter helper. Restriction, security audit and event receipt commit under
the existing workspace lock. Restrictive evidence can promote a previously
receipted active event and is independent of ordinary provider-version ordering.
Replays retain the earliest cutoff; a later scheduled date cannot extend it.
A new paused binding cannot mint a paid activation or payment grace.

Ordinary active/resumed events, later periods and paid-order evidence do not clear
the cutoff. Recovery needs separately verified and audited operational repair or
a legitimate replacement-subscription flow; neither is a public resume feature.
This deliberately leaves an unexpected provider pause as an operational exception
until reconciliation verifies the commercial contract. Paid replacement/repair and
communications remain release work rather than a claimed completed recovery path.

Plan changes persist newly observed pause restrictions before refusing provider
writes. The live plan context refuses a stored pause exception. Upgrade-refund
renewal likewise records newly observed restrictions and refuses to schedule an
unsupported paused binding. Period-end cancellation may still send only
`cancel_at_period_end: true`; it never writes a resume or clears pause state.
No raw customer/provider payload is stored in the restriction receipt.

## Verification

Verified: **1,428 app tests and 4 workflow tests**, TypeScript, changed-file
ESLint/Prettier, diff checks and production build including protected Workflow
handlers. Real isolated staging checks cover **52 PostgreSQL billing cases and
17 real-auth membership cases**. They include active/past-due/paused provider access,
signed paused/resumed delivery, cached-event promotion, non-extending scheduled
cutoffs, audit rollback/retry, pause before activation, whole-row JSON reader,
member-admission parity and retained sixth-member sessions/invitations.

A new empty rehearsal database applied the complete **34-migration** history;
all **3 migration ownership/fault cases** passed. Staging applied exactly migration
0033 after that rehearsal and now also has 34. The previous disposable rehearsal
expired; its replacement is an expiring child of isolated staging, with a distinct
empty rehearsal database. No serving/default database, local connection file or
live provider setting was changed. Nothing was pushed or deployed; billing stays
disabled. See `output/production-readiness/no-pause-2026-10-29.json` for source
hashes, exact targets and verification boundaries.

The no-pause policy and its backend/access safeguards are complete. Overall
FOR-109/FOR-110/FOR-111 stay In Progress for remaining commercial decisions,
public billing, durable provider effects/redrive/repair, ledger and actual Polar
sandbox/candidate release checks.

overageCurrencyDocument.title: Forge paid AI overage currency and usage-time ECB conversion
overageCurrencyDocument.content:
# Paid AI overage currency and usage-time conversion

FOR-109/FOR-76 implementation record, 29 October 2026.

## Confirmed commercial rules

EUR-billed workspaces use EUR for paid AI overage and its separate spending cap.
USD-billed workspaces use USD. Included AI allowance remains denominated in USD:
Free and trial receive their fixed US$5 workspace pools; paid plans receive US$5
per active member. A cap or invoice currency never changes that allowance.

The user selected fixing conversion when usage is incurred, using the latest
published ECB daily reference rate with no added spread. Preserve the source and
rate used for that usage; invoice creation must not reprice it. Capture the quote
before the provider usage starts and retain it with the authoritative server usage
identity and occurrence time. Replays use that original record, not today's feed.

ECB publishes informational reference rates and discourages transaction use. The
user explicitly selected this as Forge's agreed reference conversion, without
claiming it is an actual bank/payment-provider execution rate. Reference rates
are quoted as USD per EUR, so converting a USD provider cost into EUR divides by
that value. No FX spread or usage markup is added by these helpers.
[ECB rate guidance and source](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html).

## Implemented currency boundary

Enabled overage policies must carry an explicit currency. Budget admission takes
a trusted subscription currency and rejects a mismatched cap. Provider cost,
settled/reserved cost and included-pool arithmetic stay in USD millionths. Settled
and reserved overage are a separate ledger balance in billing-currency millionths.
`reserveWorkspaceOverage` converts only the incremental provider cost beyond the
included pool and compares it against that currency's cap and outstanding spend.
An EUR cap is never added to a USD allowance or compared directly with USD spend.

`evaluateWorkspaceBudgetAdmission` now composes those two balances. Legacy USD
summary fields (`usableOverageMicros`, `totalLimitMicros`, `remainingMicros`) are
null when an EUR overage cap is usable; they cannot pretend to describe a combined
USD limit. Callers use `costCurrency`, `overageCurrency`,
`overageRemainingMicros` and `billingOverageReservation` for explicit units.
Unlabeled enabled policies must be corrected explicitly, not silently assumed USD.

The included pool can still admit usage without an FX quote when no overage is
needed. Free/trial overage stays unavailable. BYOK/direct provider-paid usage and
paid Calls/Signals create no overage reservation and need no conversion quote.
The existing opt-in, payment-authority and cap requirements continue to apply.

## Rate source and precise arithmetic

`fetchEcbReferenceRate` reads only the fixed official daily XML URL. It sends no
customer data or credentials, disallows redirects, uses a ten-second timeout and
bounds the response to 64 KiB. A narrow parser requires exactly one dated daily
cube and one contained USD rate, rejects DTD/entities, incomplete/duplicate data,
future dates, nonpositive rates and malformed precision. It records source URL,
reference date, observation time, exact decimal USD-per-EUR value and SHA-256 ID.
A seven-day reference-age guard fails closed during an extended source outage;
provider/candidate monitoring must surface that condition.

The conversion uses bigint intermediates. Reservations round upward to a billing
currency millionth to protect the cap; settlement rounds half-up at that precision.
Both retain the exact rational numerator/denominator and original rate snapshot.
Invoice aggregation must preserve exact totals and handle final minor-unit
rounding once; these helpers do not implement the invoice writer. Integer overflow,
missing EUR rates, a quote observed after the usage, or stale/future reference data
are refused. There is no 1:1, current-invoice-rate or free-usage fallback.

## Verification and delivery boundary

**1,451 app tests and 4 workflow tests pass**, along with TypeScript, changed-file
ESLint/Prettier, diff checks and production build including protected Workflow
handlers. The new 23 cases cover inverse-rate conversion, USD identity, exact cap
boundaries, settled plus reserved EUR spend, included-pool crossing, zero-charge
exclusions, frozen replay, missing/future/stale/invalid quotes, bounded XML input,
reservation/settlement rounding and safe integer overflow.

A read-only live fetch through the actual adapter succeeded: reference date
2026-10-28, USD per EUR 1.1133, observed 2026-10-28T23:38:01.979Z. No model/payment
call, customer invoice, exchange transaction or provider setting was changed.
No migration was added. Existing isolated database evidence at commit `1ba1ff8`
remains 34 migrations, 52 billing cases, 17 real-auth membership cases and 3
migration-fault cases; those suites were not repeated for pure money helpers.

This completes the prepared currency/conversion/admission arithmetic slice, not
FOR-76's atomic ledger/run-reservation contract. Before enabling paid usage:

* Persist the selected quote, usage/payer/plan/period identity and both currency
  amounts atomically with quota reservation and run admission.
* Freeze the usage-time quote across retries/settlement/invoice generation; fetch
  before provider usage, and reconcile late or uncertain effects against retained
  evidence. Do not invent historical availability from a current daily feed.
* Reserve/adjust sufficient billing-currency funds before incurring provider cost;
  unknown cost/rate changes cannot authorize exceeding the cap. Reconcile actual
  cost, release unused reservations and retain immutable charge/credit history.
* Verify idempotent Polar reporting/invoice allocation, final minor-unit rounding,
  cancellation/refund/period/seat transitions, source freshness alarms and actual
  sandbox/candidate flows. Bank FX differences do not authorize an added spread.

Currency changes for existing subscriptions are confirmed for next renewal with
a seven-day replacement-checkout grace deadline; late payment preserves the
original monthly anniversary. The actual cutover/grace executor remains gated. See
`docs/renewal-currency-change.md`.
Public billing, ledger effects, rate retention and provider submission remain
gated. FOR-109 and FOR-76 stay In Progress. Nothing was pushed or deployed;
serving/default databases and local connection files were unchanged.


## Confirmed cap conversion on a billing-currency change · 29 October 2026

The user selected automatically converting the existing opted-in cap using the
latest published ECB reference rate. Freeze the quote when the verified currency
cutover is committed, retain it with the transition and reuse it for retries.
This conversion does not change the previously approved opt-in, grant payment
authority or switch on disabled overage.

`planOverageCurrencyCutover` prepares the new currency-tagged policy and carried
settled/reserved capacity for the same original commercial period. USD → EUR
divides by USD-per-EUR; EUR → USD multiplies. Use bigint rational intermediates,
round the cap down to a currency millionth and carried capacity up, and retain
exact fractions/rate snapshots. This avoids enlarging the approved spending
ceiling through rounding. Unchanged currencies and zero balances require no
unnecessary quote; positive cross-currency amounts fail without valid timely FX.

These carried balances are **capacity shadows**, not new charges. Keep old-currency
invoices, usage-time rates, reservations and settlement identities immutable. If
a workspace already spent/reserved half its cap during checkout grace, the
currency change preserves that consumed capacity; it does not grant another cap.
A disabled or exhausted policy stays unusable. Reconcile late old-currency
settlements against retained transition fractions under the same ledger lock,
without billing them again or resetting monthly consumption.

Tests cover both conversion directions, exhausted/disabled/zero policies,
committed capacity, conservative rounding, frozen repeatability, malformed/stale/
future/missing quotes, source-currency mismatch, period boundaries and overflow.
This is prepared arithmetic; atomic policy/quote/capacity persistence with paid
old/new binding replacement, concurrency/redrive and provider invoicing remain
FOR-76/FOR-111 release work. No live overage was enabled.

renewalCurrencyDocument.title: Forge renewal currency changes, replacement checkout and grace
renewalCurrencyDocument.content:
# Renewal-time billing currency changes

FOR-109/FOR-110/FOR-111 implementation record, 29 October 2026.

## Confirmed policy and provider capability

A paid workspace moving between EUR and USD billing-country regions should switch
currency at its next renewal. Current paid-through rights, charges, allowance
consumption, reservations, invoices and rate snapshots keep their original units.
If replacement checkout is not completed by renewal, the user approved a seven-day
checkout grace period. Its deadline is anchored to the original renewal boundary,
not the latest request, reminder or payment attempt. The user also confirmed that
payment during this grace period **keeps the original monthly anniversary**.
Late payment does not create a new monthly usage period or first-purchase pool.

The pinned Polar 2026-10 update API has no currency update field. Its product-change
implementation resolves prices in the existing subscription currency; changing a
product is not a currency migration. Programmatic subscription creation accepts
free products; paid creation uses checkout. The pinned checkout subscription_id
option upgrades free subscriptions rather than replacing an existing paid one.
An automatic currency PATCH or silent paid replacement is therefore not implemented.
[Update API](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/2026-10/subscriptions/update-subscription),
[paid creation requirement](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/subscriptions/create),
[provider product validation](https://github.com/polarsource/polar/blob/main/server/polar/subscription/service.py).

## Implemented first-party request

`requestWorkspaceRenewalCurrencyChange` → `PolarRenewalCurrencyPlanner.request`
resolves live owner/admin authority and the environment-specific subscription,
fetches current provider state, verifies workspace/customer/catalog/paid lifecycle
and reads the provider-confirmed billing-address country. No browser-supplied
country, subscription, currency, amount or seat quantity reaches this entry point.
Only the idempotent request UUID is supplied by the calling first-party action.

The source must be actively renewing, within its current paid period, with no
unreconciled paid-plan mismatch or conflicting pending change. An approved pending
Starter downgrade is carried into the intended renewal tier; pending seats do not
change current charges. A refunded-upgrade Starter fallback can compose only with
its verified pending Starter renewal. Newly observed pause/termination restrictions
are persisted before the planner refuses the request. Authority is rechecked after
the provider read and again transactionally before a cached or new result.

`recordVerifiedRenewalCurrencyRequest` locks the workspace and holds a shared lock
on the live membership row. It validates the current binding, effective paid tier,
period and provider version, reads the current atomic active-member counter and
records an informational renewal-tier/seat/price snapshot from approved prices.
That snapshot is not authorization for a later charge; checkout must re-resolve
members, price, country, lifecycle and current authority.

Migration 0034 adds `workspace_currency_change_requests`. The request row, audit
and digest-only event receipt commit together. A partial unique index permits one
requested transition per workspace. Replays reuse the request without another
row/audit; changed-body/cross-workspace/environment reuse is refused. Revoked actors
cannot retrieve a cached result. New country edits supersede prior intents while
retaining history; returning to the current currency withdraws the pending switch.
An unfinished request cannot silently move to another renewal boundary.

The stored checkout grace deadline is always exactly 168 hours after that original
boundary. SQL constraints enforce supported currencies, plan/state/country shape,
finite dates and safe positive informational seat/price values. Successful request
responses explicitly return `status: requires-checkout` and
`providerChangeScheduled: false`. Current entitlements, paid activation, refund
history and consumption are untouched by recording a request.

## Original anniversary and paid replacement verification

Migration 0035 adds the original provider period start, original UTC anchor day
and next renewal boundary to each request. Recover the day only from adjacent
verified monthly start/end boundaries. Preserve UTC time and clamp the day in
short months without losing the original day: January 31 → February 28 → March 31.
Reject nonmonthly or inconsistent windows instead of guessing.

Existing pre-expansion rows remain null; the migration does not invent an anchor.
A matching, freshly provider-verified replay can capture those fields under the
same workspace lock and live authority/binding checks, with one atomic audit.
Concurrent replays capture once; an audit failure rolls back all captured fields.
Requests whose original source period can no longer be verified require repair.
SQL rejects partial, out-of-range, infinite and reversed anchor fields.

`replacementAnniversarySchedule` accepts payment only in the original half-open
window [renewal, renewal + 168 hours). It retains the original commercial usage
period and returns the original next renewal, following renewal, stored day and
whether a later provider correction is required. It explicitly grants no fresh
paid pool. A replacement payment is a continuation of the workspace subscription.

`PolarReplacementAnniversaryVerifier.plan` is a **read-only internal verifier**.
The default live context reads the pending workspace/environment/source binding
and current owner/admin role. The verifier fetches the referenced order, its
checkout and replacement subscription through the pinned SDK. It checks:

* Exact order → checkout → new subscription/customer/catalog/currency identity,
  bound request/workspace/source metadata, original target region and tier.
* A succeeded checkout and paid initial invoice, positive approved price/quantity,
  matching taxes/totals/line sums, no outstanding balance/refund/discount/trial,
  full nonprorated original invoice window, and active unpaused/uncanceled state.
* Payment in the original grace window, valid observed timestamps and either the
  natural checkout period end or already aligned original renewal. Retain the
  original invoice window when verifying an already aligned provider response.
* A second live context/authority check after provider reads. Changed, superseded,
  revoked, cross-workspace/environment or missing legacy anchor context is refused.

The result reports payment proof and a calendar plan from those provider responses; it performs
no provider update, old-subscription cancellation, entitlement rebind or grace
activation. Its response explicitly requires verified source-stop proof and an
atomic cutover; an informational request price is not checkout/charge authority.
The verifier and its payment shapes still require actual Polar sandbox evidence.

Polar's billing-period update accepts a future end date and retains the current
period start. Provider implementation also sets its hidden anchor day to the day
of that supplied end date. Thus a single update to February 28 would drift from a
stored original 31st. The schedule retains the original day and identifies the
following March 31 correction; the eventual durable worker must apply/reconcile
that correction before renewal without resetting allowance or repricing invoices.
[Update API](https://polar.sh/docs/api-reference/2026-10/subscriptions/update-subscription),
[provider implementation](https://github.com/polarsource/polar/blob/main/server/polar/subscription/service.py).

## Confirmed before-tax price and catalog preflight

Starter's EUR/USD 10 and Plus's EUR/USD 16 per member are **before tax**;
applicable tax is added at checkout. `PolarBillingProvider` now fetches the
configured product before creating checkout. Require a live monthly recurring
product and exactly one active catalog seat-based price: correct currency,
explicit exclusive tax behavior, one flat tier at the approved per-seat price,
minimum one seat and no commercial maximum. Refuse inclusive/location-dependent
or inherited/null tax behavior, ambiguous active prices, archived/nonmonthly
products, wrong amount/currency or finite seat tiers. CheckoutCreate has no
explicit tax-behavior override in the pinned SDK, so enforce it on the catalog
rather than inventing an unsupported request parameter.

Re-resolve trusted country/member/workspace authority after catalog I/O and refuse
changes before creating checkout. Discount codes and provider trials are disabled;
checkout never submits an ad-hoc price override. The replacement verifier also
requires the completed checkout's resolved `tax_behavior=exclusive` and matching
net/tax/total invoice amounts. This validates the approved policy without claiming
that a real Polar catalog has already been configured or paid checkout tested.

## Execution remains gated

The verified request/calendar/payment-plan prerequisites are implemented. They do
**not** cancel the old subscription, create/charge a replacement checkout, change
the provider period, rebind entitlements or activate the seven-day grace
entitlement. A request or plan is never access proof. No public action is enabled.

Before executing cutover:

* Serialize durable effects for this workspace, re-fetch confirmed country and
  lifecycle, retain pending tier/seat changes, honor withdrawal/cancellation, and
  stop the old renewal only through a verified owned period-end cancellation.
  Do not create overlapping paid subscriptions or charge the target currency early.
* Implement explicit checkout-grace authority from verified transition evidence,
  bounded to the original deadline. Unexpected immediate termination/refunds and
  pause exceptions remain restrictive. A request alone cannot mint allowance or
  override the shared access policy.
* Re-resolve approved member/price/country context before creating checkout and
  prove the new paid invoice before executing/re-fetching the period adjustment.
  Persist original anchor, paid invoice window, expected provider state and a
  durable short-month follow-up. Retry lost responses safely and serialize with
  renewal/product/seat events; planning alone is not an executed provider change.
* Atomically replace the verified old/new binding, retain historical receipts,
  refunds, usage and original currency units, and map commercial usage to the old
  anniversary without granting a new trial or first-purchase pool. Redirects
  cannot grant access. Ensure retained old-binding events still restrict correctly.
* Convert an existing opted-in cap at the latest published ECB rate when the
  verified currency cutover commits. The user selected automatic ECB conversion.
  Freeze that quote with the transition; carry consumed/reserved capacity in the
  same commercial period and keep original charges/usage-time quotes unchanged.
  `planOverageCurrencyCutover` implements the arithmetic but not the atomic ledger
  writer or payment authority. Disabled overage stays disabled. See the overage
  guide for conservative rounding and retained capacity shadows.
* Complete communications, retries, duplicate/out-of-order payment events,
  expiry/recovery, idempotent settlement/invoices and actual Polar sandbox/candidate
  evidence, including the source stop and recurring anniversary repair.
